resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin bulk flag updates can wait indefinitely on database locks and exhaust the dashboard pool.

original_members.claim: Admin bulk flag updates can wait indefinitely on database locks and exhaust the dashboard pool.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, another transaction retains a row lock on an active partner. Authorized raid/chat configuration writes then wait indefinitely for that row. Once outstanding writes occupy pool_max connections, unrelated dashboard requests cannot acquire a connection and fail, although PostgreSQL remains reachable.
original_members.evidence: The raid handler awaits bulk_update_partner_flags at lines 154-163; the chat handler repeats this at lines 208-217. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/admin_config.rs:87-99 executes UPDATE twitch_partners without a deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 uses tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-57 bounds acquisition but sets statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, not this pool. The inspected router and serving layers add no request deadline.
original_members.expected_behavior: A blocked configuration operation should fail within an agreed deadline rather than indefinitely consume a shared connection. No explicit deadline contract was found, so selecting timeout and cancellation policy remains a C recommendation, not an automatic fix.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication and CSRF restrict access. The connection acquisition timeout bounds waiting callers, but not queries already holding connections. A PostgreSQL server/session timeout could prevent this scenario; live database settings were not inspected. The same bulk-update helper serves both raid and chat configuration, so these are one finding.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Signup-block creation trusts stale local login mappings without checking the current Twitch account.

original_members.claim: Signup-block creation trusts stale local login mappings without checking the current Twitch account.
original_members.failure_scenario: The local identity or partner table still maps oldname to account A after A renames. Twitch has reassigned oldname to account B, and the admin submits a block for the current oldname. Even with a working Helix client, the resolver immediately returns A's cached ID. The endpoint writes an A-anchored block and deletes A's OAuth credentials, although the requested current login belongs to B.
original_members.evidence: The assigned resolver at lines 171-173 returns any local match before Helix get_users at line 181. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:69-108 resolves solely through stored login comparisons without freshness verification; lines 249-251 delete credentials for the resolved ID. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/poller/engine.rs:322-335 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:787-790 reconcile mappings upon observed stream or EventSub identities, not synchronously before this admin request.
original_members.expected_behavior: An action targeting a current Twitch login should resolve the account currently owning it before applying ID-scoped destructive effects. The required freshness and offline-fallback policy is not established, so changing the explicitly documented local-first behavior remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: The existing rename reconciler repairs mappings after the relevant account is observed, but cannot guarantee fresh mappings for offline or unobserved accounts at request time. Stable-ID storage prevents later rename bypass only when the initial ID resolution is correct. Admin authentication, CSRF, and database uniqueness do not verify the current login-to-ID association.

findings.title_de: Parallele Raid-Sperre rollt gültige Anmeldesperre zurück
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Parallele Raid-Sperre rollt gültige Anmeldesperre zurück.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A concurrent raid-blacklist insert can roll back an otherwise valid signup-block request.

original_members.claim: A concurrent raid-blacklist insert can roll back an otherwise valid signup-block request.
original_members.failure_scenario: The target initially has no raid-blacklist row. During the signup-block transaction, its INSERT SELECT evaluates NOT EXISTS as true. A bot blacklist transaction concurrently inserts the same normalized target_login and commits before the signup transaction's uniqueness check. The signup INSERT then raises a duplicate-primary-key error. The entire signup transaction rolls back, leaving no denylist entry and leaving credentials and any active partner unmodified; the endpoint returns 500.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:223-236 uses INSERT SELECT WHERE NOT EXISTS without ON CONFLICT, and propagates its error before commit at line 289. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/raid_blacklist.rs:88-115 independently inserts the same key without the signup advisory lock. Its reachable bot callers include /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/raid_arrival_wiring.rs:293-348 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/auto_raid_pipeline.rs:1006-1035. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:2247-2248 defines the conflicting primary key.
original_members.expected_behavior: An existing independent raid-blacklist reason must be preserved while the signup block and its other effects succeed. This is explicit in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:194-204. Both serial orderings permit both operations, so mere concurrent insertion must not invalidate the signup operation.
original_members.countermeasures: The per-user partner_signup advisory lock serializes cooperating signup writers, but the independent raid-blacklist writer does not acquire it. NOT EXISTS does not lock an absent row; the unique constraint detects the race by aborting the transaction. The handler maps the error directly to 500 without retry. The same underlying add function is also reached through the assigned tag-block backfill handler, so that path shares this defect.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Laufender Tag-Nachtrag sperrt nach Regelentfernung.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: An in-flight tag backfill can create a permanent channel block after the tag rule has been removed.

original_members.claim: An in-flight tag backfill can create a permanent channel block after the tag rule has been removed.
original_members.failure_scenario: A tag-add request starts its backfill. For an inactive, unblocked historical channel, enforce reads the matching rule and is then paused before calling partner_signup_block::add. A second admin removes the rule and receives success. The first request resumes and creates a new persistent channel denylist entry and raid blacklist using the deleted rule. No later sweep removes that entry.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed SHA, the assigned handler calls db::backfill after separately committing db::add. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_tag_block.rs:267-307 retains the rule in memory across subsequent awaits and passes it to the write function. The transaction in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:124-158 rechecks active-partner and existing-denylist state, but never rule existence. Rule removal at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_tag_block.rs:230-252 uses no shared rule lock. Its test at lines 733-751 establishes that channel exclusions persist after rule removal.
original_members.expected_behavior: The removal UI at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/pages/community/PartnerSignupBlocks.tsx:167-175 says the tag will no longer be automatically excluded, and the no-rule backfill test at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_tag_block.rs:1027-1039 expects no channel writes. However, whether already-running enforcement must stop immediately is not explicitly contracted. This needs a cancellation/serialization decision and remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: Repeated active-partner and existing-denylist checks prevent overwriting those states, but do not validate the cached rule. User-level advisory locking does not serialize rule deletion. Keeping already-existing channel exclusions is intentional and is not the finding; the issue is newly created exclusions after removal. The same cached-rule pattern is shared by backfill and sweep through enforce.

original_members.claim: Adding a tag-block rule can exhaust dashboard memory by loading every matching historical session.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated administrator adds 'Deutsch' when matching historical session tag strings exceed available dashboard memory. For example, 3,000,000 matching sessions with 200-byte tag strings exceed 512 MiB of memory headroom before row and allocation overhead. The request commits the rule, then fetches the entire matching history into the dashboard process and can terminate it through allocation failure/OOM instead of returning its success response. Repeated sessions for the same channel remain separate input rows.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A partner-block write can hold a dashboard database connection indefinitely while waiting for an advisory lock.

original_members.claim: A partner-block write can hold a dashboard database connection indefinitely while waiting for an advisory lock.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout both zero, another database session holds the partner_signup advisory lock for a locally known Twitch user in an open idle transaction. An authorized add request for that user acquires a pool connection and waits indefinitely inside db::add while its HTTP client remains connected. Enough concurrently authorized requests can occupy the pool and cause unrelated dashboard database operations to fail their acquisition deadline.
original_members.evidence: The assigned handler awaits db::add at lines 254-263. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:122-127 begins a transaction and awaits pg_advisory_xact_lock without a local deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 uses tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:10-11,20-58 sets an acquisition/connection deadline, but sets statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, which this dashboard path does not use. The relevant admin router and global layers in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1287-1298,2204-2271 contain no request deadline.
original_members.expected_behavior: A persistently blocked database dependency should eventually produce a bounded failure and release the checked-out connection. The existing contract specifies acquisition/connection limits, not a query or administrative-request deadline. Choosing that policy therefore remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin and CSRF guards prevent anonymous triggering. The finite pool bounds connection count, but its acquire_timeout does not cover an already-acquired connection's SQL execution. Helix resolution has a 20-second per-request timeout and bounded retries, which do not cover this database wait. An externally configured PostgreSQL timeout or proxy cancellation may mitigate it; live role/proxy settings were not inspected. Targeted twin: the assigned tag-block handler's backfill reaches the same advisory-lock operation through enforce and partner_signup_block::add.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin research queries can indefinitely occupy shared database connections while waiting on a table lock.

original_members.claim: Admin research queries can indefinitely occupy shared database connections while waiting on a table lock.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout unset, a maintenance transaction holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_stats_category without completing. Valid admin research requests acquire connections and wait on their subject and baseline SELECTs. Repeated requests can occupy the entire shared pool; unrelated dashboard requests then fail acquisition while the original queries remain blocked.
original_members.evidence: Verified against 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The primary handler constructs unbounded query futures at lines 456-478 and awaits try_join! at 480-484. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 creates its pool with tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:10-11 selects read_only=false; its statement_timeout setup at 47-53 only applies to read_only=true. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2240-2271 and 2309-2314 add no execution deadline. The same wait pattern reaches suggestions_handler at primary lines 519-525 and the Scout scan at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/admin_scout.rs:146.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled database dependency should produce a bounded failure rather than permanently consuming shared dashboard capacity. No explicit deadline contract for these handlers was found, so choosing and introducing that deadline remains a class C policy decision.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin checks restrict reachability. Pool size and acquisition deadlines bound connection count and subsequent waiters, not already running SQL. The existing 20-second readonly-pool timeout is not enabled by production connect(). Scout detection caps results at 25, which bounds its loop but not SQL waits. Deployment role SQL resets role settings and does not install a statement timeout. An externally configured PostgreSQL timeout could mitigate this scenario; live database and proxy settings were not queried under the read-only assignment.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A nonexistent first master_dash_session cookie bypasses fingerprint validation of the authenticated admin session.

original_members.claim: A nonexistent first master_dash_session cookie bypasses fingerprint validation of the authenticated admin session.
original_members.failure_scenario: An attacker possessing a valid fingerprint-bound admin session S sends Cookie: master_dash_session=nonexistent; master_dash_session=S from a different IP or browser fingerprint. The authentication extractor skips the nonexistent cookie and authenticates S. The forward-auth handler instead loads the first cookie, receives Ok(None), and returns 200 without verifying S. This also bypasses fp_pending rejection. Caddy consequently admits a request that the session binding should reject.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review revision, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/level.rs:408-474 iterates all admin cookie values and records the selected AuthenticatedAdminSessionId. Its extract_cookie helper at lines 231-234 returns only the first value. The assigned handler uses that helper at line 65, accepts Ok(None) at line 81, and returns 200 at line 89. Fingerprint rejection is implemented in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:114-147. The reachable native login creates bound sessions in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/discord_admin_login.rs:578-590. Static evidence only; no tests or requests were executed.
original_members.expected_behavior: Verify the fingerprint of the exact admin session selected by authentication. Reject its IP mismatch, passive-fingerprint mismatch, or pending fingerprint step with 401. This is the explicit handler contract at lines 20-24 and 45-49. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/docs/HOST_ROUTING_CONTRACT.md:46-55 confirms Caddy relies on this check before admitting admin-panel requests.
original_members.countermeasures: A valid admin session is still required, so this is a session-binding bypass rather than anonymous access. Central session validation, encrypted session storage, expiry checks, and the initial privilege guard do not validate the selected session's fingerprint. Database errors fail closed, but a nonexistent first cookie returns Ok(None), not an error. The selected-session extension is already available and is respected by the CSRF middleware, but this handler ignores it. The other fingerprint-validation caller, the login handler, does not admit a request when its first cookie is nonexistent.

original_members.claim: Duplicate admin cookies bypass forward-auth fingerprint checks because the handler checks the first cookie rather than the authenticated session.
original_members.failure_scenario: Send Cookie: master_dash_session=nonexistent; master_dash_session=<valid-session> with a valid second session whose stored IP or passive fingerprint does not match the request, or whose fp_pending is true. DashboardAuthLevel skips the nonexistent cookie and authenticates the second session. The handler reloads only the first cookie, receives Ok(None), skips all fingerprint checks and returns 200. Possession of a valid session cookie therefore suffices to bypass its device binding.
original_members.evidence: Static path at review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af: auth/level.rs:408-473 iterates all admin-cookie candidates and records the selected AuthenticatedAdminSessionId. auth/level.rs:232-234 extract_cookie returns only the first candidate. forward_auth.rs:65-83 uses extract_cookie and treats a missing first session as permission to continue. auth/session.rs:114-147 rejects mismatched binding and incomplete fingerprints. Native pending sessions are created at auth/session.rs:881-903 and imported centrally by auth/discord_admin_login.rs:606-619.
original_members.expected_behavior: Verify the session that actually authenticated the request and return 401 when its device binding fails or its fingerprint step is incomplete. The contract is explicit in forward_auth.rs:20-24, auth/session.rs:853-858 and docs/HOST_ROUTING_CONTRACT.md:46-61.
original_members.countermeasures: Central validation and local session expiry checks establish that the second session exists, but do not verify the request fingerprint. build_entry_admin_router in src/lib.rs:1587-1614 adds no additional fingerprint guard. Caddy relies on this endpoint's 200/401 decision. The selected-session extension already exists and is honored by auth/csrf.rs, but this handler ignores it.

original_members.claim: A leading invalid admin cookie bypasses device-binding checks for a valid second admin cookie.
original_members.failure_scenario: Send Cookie: master_dash_session=missing; master_dash_session=valid, where valid is an unexpired native admin session belonging to another device or still marked fp_pending. Without an internal credential or Twitch session, the auth extractor accepts the second cookie. Its extract_cookie helper at lines 231-234 instead returns the first value. The assigned handler uses that helper at line 65 and permits a missing session at line 81. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:860-904 creates native device-bound sessions with fp_pending=true, while lines 114-147 reject mismatched bindings and pending fingerprints.
original_members.expected_behavior: Forward-auth must verify the admin session actually accepted by the auth cascade. The handler's documented device-binding contract and AdminSessionFingerprint::verify require 401 for mismatched bindings or an incomplete fingerprint step.
original_members.countermeasures: Session lifetime and optional central validation are checked by the extractor, but neither checks the current request's device binding. The extractor explicitly permits valid local sessions when central validation fails. The neighboring login fingerprint check does not grant access after a missing-cookie lookup, so it does not repair this path. No live requests were made.

findings.title_de: Unicode-Login trennt möglicherweise anderen ASCII-Kanal
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Unicode-Login trennt möglicherweise anderen ASCII-Kanal.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Unicode login encoding can make the admin disconnect endpoint disconnect a different ASCII channel.

original_members.claim: Unicode login encoding can make the admin disconnect endpoint disconnect a different ASCII channel.
original_members.failure_scenario: With the internal bot API configured and channel alpha present, an authenticated admin sends POST /twitch/api/admin/streamers/%C5%A1lpha/disconnect-bot with valid CSRF and {"confirm_login":"šlpha"}. The path extracts šlpha and the confirmation passes. The encoder truncates š (U+0161) to byte 0x61, producing %61lpha. The internal endpoint consequently receives alpha and disconnects that channel, although the confirmed input was not alpha.
original_members.evidence: Static path at review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af: admin_streamers.rs:670-677 confirms the original input; :702-706 forwards the encoded login; :762-770 encodes Unicode scalar values using other as u32 as u8 instead of their UTF-8 bytes. The internal handler at rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:1018-1056 validates the resulting alpha login, removes moderator privileges, departners it and sets its opt-out flag. Domain validation at rust/crates/tb-domain/src/login.rs:64-69 permits only ASCII Twitch logins.
original_members.expected_behavior: The disconnect operation must target the confirmed channel only. An invalid Unicode login must remain invalid or be rejected, not silently become another valid account. admin_streamers.rs:654-658 explicitly binds confirmation to the path login, and the internal domain validator rejects non-ASCII logins.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication and CSRF guard caller privileges, not path encoding. Confirmation checks the pre-encoding string. Internal normalization cannot reject this case because it sees an already corrupted, valid ASCII login. Existing encoder tests at admin_streamers.rs:1733-1736 cover only ASCII. Targeted searches found no matching scalar-to-byte encoder twin in the dashboard and internal API handler directories.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af bestätigt: Der Encoder kürzt Unicode-Codepoints mit `other as u32 as u8` auf das niederwertige Byte. Dadurch wird ein bestätigter ungültiger Unicode-Login vor der internen Validierung zu einem anderen gültigen ASCII-Login. Die vorhandenen Schutzschichten verhindern diese Identitätsänderung nicht. B statt A, weil ein berechtigter Admin-Kontext erforderlich ist und keine Rechteausweitung nachgewiesen wurde.
result.failure_scenario: Bei normal konfigurierter interner Bot-API und aktivem Partner `umiwaver` sendet ein berechtigter Admin POST /twitch/api/admin/streamers/%C5%B5miwaver/disconnect-bot mit {"confirm_login":"ŵmiwaver"}. Der decodierte Pfad und die Bestätigung stimmen überein. `ŵ` ist U+0175; der Encoder erzeugt daraus %75 und damit den internen Pfad /streamers/%75miwaver/disconnect-bot. Intern wird `umiwaver` validiert und dessen Partnerstatus auf `departnered` sowie manual_partner_opt_out auf 1 gesetzt. Bei verfügbarem Moderator-Port werden außerdem dessen Moderator-Rechte entfernt. Kein Unicode-Datensatz ist erforderlich.

Die Kodierung reduziert Unicode-Codepoints auf ihr niederwertiges Byte und verändert dadurch den bestätigten Zielkanal. Die Admin-Prüfung verhindert eine belegte Rechteausweitung, nicht diesen Zuordnungsfehler. Deshalb B, nicht A.
result.failure_scenario: Bei regulär konfigurierter interner Bot-API und einem aktiven ASCII-Partner umiwaver sendet ein gültig angemeldeter Admin einen zulässigen Same-Origin-POST an /twitch/api/admin/streamers/%C5%B5miwaver/disconnect-bot mit {"confirm_login":"ŵmiwaver"}. Pfad und Bestätigung stimmen überein. Doch ŵ ist U+0175; der Cast auf u8 ergibt 0x75. Der interne Aufruf verwendet deshalb /streamers/%75miwaver/disconnect-bot. Die interne API erhält umiwaver, akzeptiert diesen gültigen ASCII-Login und beendet dessen Partnerschaft samt Wiederaufnahme-Sperre. original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated, confirmed disconnect request reaches the bot. Twitch moderator removal succeeds, and partner departure can also persist, but the internal response headers are lost or delayed beyond the dashboard's 20-second timeout. reqwest send returns an error, and the dashboard responds 503 with a message asserting that disconnection was not executed, despite those completed changes.

claim.claim: Disconnect transport failures falsely report that no disconnection occurred after side effects may already have completed.

result.reason: Confirmed at SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The dashboard equates every POST send error with no disconnection. A reachable downstream retry takes up to 22 seconds after disconnection mutations have committed, exceeding the dashboard's 20-second timeout. This contradicts the explicit partial-outcome reporting contract. No security vulnerability is established.
result.failure_scenario: An authenticated admin submits a correctly confirmed disconnect for an active partner with a Discord link. Moderator removal succeeds quickly; the partner becomes departnered, manual_partner_opt_out becomes 1, and raid_enabled becomes false. The subsequent Discord-role request receives no response: its 10-second timeout, 2-second retry delay, and second 10-second attempt keep the internal handler awaiting completion. At 20 seconds, the dashboard POST times out and returns 503 with 'Trennung nicht ausgeführt, bitte erneut versuchen.' The admin UI displays that message although the earlier effects are already committed. Cancellation of the remaining handler cannot undo those effects.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/admin_streamers.rs:680-685 requires the internal partial-step report to be passed through unchanged for both disconnect callers.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:921-933 explicitly requires reporting each outcome, including failed steps; :1066-1074 and :1105-1117 implement truthful partial reporting.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:2885-2915 asserts persisted departure and opt-out; :2943-2973 requires acknowledging departure even when moderator removal fails. These are source assertions, not executed test results.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:1039-1083 performs departure and opt-out before awaiting Discord-role removal. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/streamer_lifecycle.rs:260-308 executes partner and raid-auth updates directly against PgPool, without a request-spanning transaction.

Guard sources: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/csrf.rs:125-164 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/security.rs:147-200.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af ist ein konkreter Timeoutpfad nach bereits gespeicherten Änderungen belegt. Der Proxy behandelt jeden send()-Fehler als Nichtausführung. Sein 20-Sekunden-Limit kann jedoch während des nachgelagerten Discord-Schritts ablaufen. Das ist eine falsche Ergebnismeldung, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.
result.failure_scenario: Ein angemeldeter Admin bestätigt einen aktiven Partner mit verknüpftem Discord-Konto. Moderator-Entzug und Datenbankänderungen sind innerhalb einer Sekunde erfolgreich: status='departnered', manual_partner_opt_out=1 und raid_enabled=false. Anschließend liefert der Discord-Broker bei beiden Rollenentzug-Versuchen keine Antwortheader. Dessen zwei 10-Sekunden-Fristen plus 2 Sekunden Wiederholungswartezeit überschreiten das 20-Sekunden-Limit des Dashboard-Proxys. Dieser liefert HTTP 503 mit „Trennung nicht ausgeführt, bitte erneut versuchen“, obwohl die Partnerschaft bereits beendet ist. Die Admin-Oberfläche zeigt diese Meldung unverändert.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/admin_streamers.rs:708-730 setzt 20 Sekunden Gesamtfrist und gibt bei jedem send()-Fehler die definitive Nichtausführungsmeldung zurück.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/lib.rs:371-374 registriert die interne Route. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2072-2078,2160-2170 verdrahtet den echten BrokerDiscordDirectory als Rollen-Port.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/oauth_followups.rs:81-84,194-196 delegiert den Rollenentzug an BrokerRelay. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:31-33,235-237,311-329,392-408 belegt zwei Versuche mit jeweils 10 Sekunden und 2 Sekunden Wartezeit.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/api/client.ts:170-191 übernimmt das message-Feld einer 503-Antwort. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/pages/streamers/StreamerDetail.tsx:871-890 zeigt es als Fehlermeldung an.

original_members.claim: Nach einem Raid-Auth-Fehler während der Departnerung überspringen Verify-Retries die ausstehende Bereinigung.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein aktiver Partner besitzt raid_enabled=TRUE und aktivierte Engagement-Settings. Ein Admin sendet verify mit mode=clear. Der Partner-UPDATE auf status=departnered wird erfolgreich committed. Vor dem anschließenden Raid-Auth-UPDATE fällt die DB-Verbindung aus oder dieses Statement scheitert. Der Handler meldet 500, während Raid-Auth und Engagement aktiviert bleiben. Nach Wiederherstellung liefert derselbe Verify-Aufruf 404, weil nur aktive Partner geladen werden; beide ausstehenden Abschaltungen werden nicht mehr erreicht.
original_members.evidence: admin_streamers.rs:525-539 ruft departner_streamer auf und behandelt None als 404. Der Helper lädt ausschließlich status=active (streamers_crud.rs:405-424), committed den Partner-UPDATE separat auf dem Pool (495-523) und führt erst danach Raid-Auth-UPDATE und Engagement-Abschaltung aus (525-547). Es existiert keine umschließende Transaktion. Die vorhandenen Tests verlangen beide Abschaltungen (1618-1691). Der gezielt geprüfte Zwilling tb-internal-api/src/streamer_lifecycle.rs:201-316 besitzt dieselbe Reihenfolge und denselben Active-only-Guard.
original_members.expected_behavior: Eine fehlgeschlagene Departnerung muss entweder den vorherigen Zustand erhalten oder bei Wiederholung ihre ausstehende Bereinigung durchführen können. Der festgelegte Ablauf in streamers_crud.rs:385-392 und die Tests verlangen status=departnered, raid_enabled=FALSE und deaktiviertes Engagement zusammen.
original_members.countermeasures: GREATEST schützt das bestehende Opt-out, nicht die Transaktionsgrenze. Die Schema-Trigger synchronisieren Identitätsdaten und deaktivieren weder Raid-Auth noch Engagement. Andere Partner-Gates können die tatsächliche Raid-Ausführung verhindern; deshalb wird keine unerlaubte Raid-Ausführung behauptet. Sie reparieren aber nicht den widersprüchlichen gespeicherten Zustand oder den Verify-Retry. Das interne Idempotenz-Wrapper wird vom direkten Dashboard-Verify-Pfad nicht verwendet.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Parallele Archive- und Block-Toggles verlieren jeweils einen Zustandswechsel.

original_members.claim: Parallele Archive- und Block-Toggles verlieren jeweils einen Zustandswechsel.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein Partner ist nicht archiviert. Zwei gültige Admin-Requests senden gleichzeitig archive mit mode=toggle oder leerem Body. Beide SELECTs lesen admin_archived_at=NULL; danach setzen beide UPDATEs einen Zeitstempel und beide Requests melden Erfolg. Zwei Toggles lassen den Partner fälschlich archiviert, statt den Ausgangszustand wiederherzustellen. Identisches Interleaving beim Block-Toggle: Beide lesen nicht blockiert und setzen blocked, sodass der zweite Zustandswechsel verloren geht.
original_members.evidence: admin_streamers.rs:592-595 und 612-618 reichen die Toggle-Modi direkt an run_archive und archive_streamer weiter. Archive-Toggle trennt SELECT und unbedingten UPDATE durch separate Pool-Aufrufe (streamers_crud.rs:747-778). ToggleBlock tut dasselbe (712-745). Der vorhandene Test archive_toggle_wechselt_archived_state fordert nach zwei Toggles den ursprünglichen Zustand (1825-1860). Der geprüfte Legacy-Form-Alias verwendet denselben Helper (handlers/admin_form_aliases.rs:107-112,138).
original_members.expected_behavior: Jeder erfolgreich ausgeführte Toggle muss den zum Änderungszeitpunkt aktuellen Zustand genau einmal umschalten. Zwei erfolgreiche Toggles derselben Eigenschaft müssen den Ausgangszustand wiederherstellen; dies ist für Archive ausdrücklich im bestehenden Test belegt.
original_members.countermeasures: Die Admin- und CSRF-Middleware prüfen Berechtigungen, serialisieren aber keine Mutationen. SQL-Zeilensperren greifen nur während der einzelnen UPDATEs; der vorausgehende SELECT und dessen Ergebnis sind nicht geschützt. Es gibt weder FOR UPDATE in einer gemeinsamen Transaktion noch einen Vergleich des gelesenen Zustands im UPDATE. Eindeutigkeitsindizes verhindern diesen Lost Update nicht.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin streamer queries can exhaust the shared dashboard database pool indefinitely while waiting for a table lock.

original_members.claim: Admin streamer queries can exhaust the shared dashboard database pool indefinitely while waiting for a table lock.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout both disabled, an uncommitted transaction holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_stream_sessions. N concurrent authorised streamer-list requests, where N equals pool_max, acquire all dashboard connections and wait indefinitely. Subsequent dashboard requests requiring the same pool fail their acquisition deadline, while the original requests remain blocked until the transaction releases its lock.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, list_handler directly awaits list_streamers at the reported location. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/admin_streamers.rs:443-446 reads twitch_stream_sessions, and lines 502-504 execute fetch_all(pool).await without an execution deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 and 476-477 create the ordinary shared pool and pass it into the router. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 bounds connection acquisition but sets statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, not the connect path used here. The detail handler at lines 328-334 has the same exposure through its session-statistics query.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled database operation should have a finite execution deadline so it cannot retain every shared connection indefinitely. The repository does not establish a required deadline for these ordinary dashboard queries, so this remains C rather than an automatic-fix candidate.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication limits who can trigger these queries. Pool size and acquire_timeout bound connections and later acquisition waits, but do not terminate already executing SQL. The checked router and server wiring contain no encompassing request timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/twitch-runtime-roles.sql:22-29 resets role settings without installing a query deadline. A database-wide or DSN-supplied statement_timeout would prevent this scenario; live database settings were not inspected. Separate protections were verified for the other external path: disconnect HTTP calls have a 20-second timeout, and Brain has bounded connections, statement deadlines, a 150-second build response deadline, and two fail-fast planning slots retained by blocking work.

original.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, list_handler directly awaits list_streamers at the reported location. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/admin_streamers.rs:443-446 reads twitch_stream_sessions, and lines 502-504 execute fetch_all(pool).await without an execution deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 and 476-477 create the ordinary shared pool and pass it into the router. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 bounds connection acquisition but sets statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, not the connect path used here. The detail handler at lines 328-334 has the same exposure through its session-statistics query.
original.expected_behavior: A stalled database operation should have a finite execution deadline so it cannot retain every shared connection indefinitely. The repository does not establish a required deadline for these ordinary dashboard queries, so this remains C rather than an automatic-fix candidate.
original.countermeasures: Admin authentication limits who can trigger these queries. Pool size and acquire_timeout bound connections and later acquisition waits, but do not terminate already executing SQL. The checked router and server wiring contain no encompassing request timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/twitch-runtime-roles.sql:22-29 resets role settings without installing a query deadline. A database-wide or DSN-supplied statement_timeout would prevent this scenario; live database settings were not inspected. Separate protections were verified for the other external path: disconnect HTTP calls have a 20-second timeout, and Brain has bounded connections, statement deadlines, a 150-second build response deadline, and two fail-fast planning slots retained by blocking work.

original_candidate_group.claim: Behind a loopback reverse proxy, one unauthenticated visitor can exhaust the Self-Explainer quota for every visitor.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Behind a loopback reverse proxy, one unauthenticated visitor can exhaust the Self-Explainer quota for every visitor.

failure_scenarios.value: With the public dashboard behind a local reverse proxy, visitors with different client IPs all arrive with the same socket peer, such as 127.0.0.1. An attacker sends ten POST requests with malformed JSON, for example the body '{', within 60 seconds. Each reserves a slot before returning 400. Every legitimate visitor routed through that proxy subsequently receives 429 until slots expire. Repeating the bursts denies service without authentication or model calls.

Two distinct visitors access the public endpoint through the same loopback reverse proxy. Visitor A sends ten requests within 60 seconds, even malformed JSON requests. Visitor B's first question then receives HTTP 429 because both visitors are recorded as 127.0.0.1, regardless of their distinct forwarded client addresses.

evidence.value: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, the finding file lines 816-820 uses only ConnectInfo.ip() as the limiter key; lines 50-51 set ten hits per 60 seconds; lines 585-600 reserve hits, and lines 828-836 parse JSON afterward. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:234-237 copies the original socket ConnectInfo unchanged. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:604-607 installs socket-derived ConnectInfo. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:124-128 registers the endpoint publicly. The tracked local-proxy topology is shown by /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/caddy/partner-profiles.caddy:8-10, which forwards to 127.0.0.1:8769 and carries client identity in X-Forwarded-For instead.

At the fixed review SHA, lines 816-820 derive the limiter key exclusively from ConnectInfo's socket IP. Lines 622-625 share one process-wide limiter with a ten-hit, 60-second window; lines 820-837 consume allowance before JSON validation. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:228-238 copies socket ConnectInfo without interpreting forwarded addresses. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:604-607 installs socket-based ConnectInfo. The public route is registered without authentication in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:124-127.

expected_behavior.value: A visitor's quota must not consume unrelated visitors' quotas. The finding file documents a per-peer public limiter at lines 13-15 and tests independent peer buckets at lines 1140-1149. The existing proxy-aware client-key implementation in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:309-338 explicitly handles loopback proxy peers using forwarded client identity. Such identity must be accepted only from a trusted proxy.

Distinct public clients should have independent allowances. The primary limiter test at lines 1140-1149 explicitly verifies peer independence. The existing client-key implementation in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:309-337 explicitly accounts for loopback reverse proxies by using the forwarded client address.

countermeasures.value: The public subrouter has no authentication or proxy-aware rate-limit layer; its CORS and extensions do not change ConnectInfo. The shared audit middleware passes this non-admin path through unchanged. Model deadlines, input truncation and knowledge scope guards occur after the exhausted quota and cannot prevent the denial. The authenticated sibling assistant uses server-derived Twitch user IDs instead, so that targeted twin does not share this defect. Full live Caddy site configuration was not inspected or probed; this finding applies to the documented loopback reverse-proxy deployment.

The mutex correctly serializes allowance updates, but cannot isolate clients mapped to the same key. OptionalConnectInfo does not replace the socket address, and the public handler does not call the existing proxy-aware client-key helper. Proxy-provided X-Forwarded-For therefore does not prevent bucket sharing. Targeted neighboring OptionalConnectInfo consumers use socket identity for internal loopback guards rather than this public limiter; no additional twin is claimed.

claim.claim: Behind a loopback reverse proxy, one unauthenticated visitor can exhaust the Self-Explainer quota for every visitor.

result.reason: Confirmed at SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af for the stated topology: visitors forwarded from the same loopback IP to one dashboard process share its ten-request Self-Explainer bucket. An unauthenticated visitor can therefore deny this endpoint to other visitors. This is an availability vulnerability, not permanent quota exhaustion.
result.failure_scenario: A loopback reverse proxy forwards requests to one dashboard instance with peer IP 127.0.0.1. One anonymous visitor sends ten POST requests to /twitch/api/v2/self-explainer/ask with body {} within 60 seconds. Each consumes a slot before returning 400 for the missing question, without invoking the model or database. Another visitor, even with a different X-Forwarded-For address and a valid question, receives 429 because the handler also keys that request as 127.0.0.1. This affects every visitor using that proxy IP and process until slots expire; repeating the batches can sustain the denial.
reachability_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:124-128,156-161 registers the public POST handler without authentication or the proxy-aware rate-limit middleware.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:476-483,598-606 builds the production router and supplies socket-address ConnectInfo through axum::serve.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:234-237 copies socket ConnectInfo unchanged. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/self_explainer.rs:816-825 uses only its IP and ignores forwarded client identity.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/self_explainer.rs:50-51,585-602,622-625 defines one process-wide limiter with ten accepted requests per key per 60 seconds; :828-850 validates JSON and the question only after consuming the slot.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/website/src/components/layout/SiteChatbot.tsx:89-102 calls this endpoint without an authentication requirement and displays failure on 429.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/self_explainer.rs:13-15 documents public, per-peer limiting; :1140-1149 explicitly tests that another peer has an independent quota.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:309-337 documents and implements client-IP recovery from X-Forwarded-For behind a loopback proxy; :563-572 tests that topology. This supports independent client buckets rather than an intentional proxy-wide quota.
countermeasures: The existing proxy-aware rate_limit_middleware derives a separate client key, but it neither rewrites ConnectInfo nor wraps the Self-Explainer route. It cannot protect this handler's separate limiter.
Quota locking and expiry work correctly. Denied requests do not extend the window, limiting each burst's impact to the remaining 60-second window, but not preventing repeated starvation.

Question validation, model timeouts, and database constraints cannot prevent this scenario: {} consumes the slot and returns before model execution or log insertion. The log table has no quota constraint (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260617040000_self_explainer_and_irc_read.sql:13-21).
gaps: No builds, tests, network requests, or live infrastructure inspection were performed, as required.

The complete deployed proxy configuration is not established by the pinned sources. Confirmation is conditional on the claim's specified single-loopback-peer topology, not a verified production incident. Multiple processes or distinct proxy source IPs have separate buckets.

result.reason: Unter der vorausgesetzten Loopback-Proxy-Topologie besteht eine unauthentisierte Verfügbarkeitslücke: Der Handler verwendet ausschließlich die TCP-Peer-IP. Alle Besucher desselben Proxy-Upstreams teilen dadurch einen einzigen 10-Anfragen-Bucket. Weitergereichte Besucheradressen ändern diesen Schlüssel nicht. Auch abgewiesene Eingaben verbrauchen das Kontingent.
result.failure_scenario: Ein Proxy verbindet alle Besucher mit derselben tb-dashboard-Instanz über 127.0.0.1. Ein Besucher sendet innerhalb weniger Sekunden zehn POST-Anfragen an /twitch/api/v2/self-explainer/ask mit dem Body {}. Jede reserviert einen Slot und erhält anschließend HTTP 400 wegen der fehlenden Frage. Eine unmittelbar folgende gültige Frage eines anderen Besuchers erhält HTTP 429. Der Angriff benötigt weder Anmeldung noch Modell- oder Datenbankzugriff. Betroffen sind alle Besucher über denselben Proxy-Peer, bis Slots nach 60 Sekunden ablaufen.
reachability_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/docs/HOST_ROUTING_CONTRACT.md:17-26 dokumentiert das Backend 127.0.0.1:8769 und öffentlich erlaubte generische /twitch/*-Pfade.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:124-161 registriert den POST-Handler im öffentlichen Router ohne Anmeldung oder CSRF-Gate.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:476-483,604-606 verwendet den Produktionsrouter und liefert TCP-ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:228-238 liest ConnectInfo unverändert aus den Request-Extensions.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/self_explainer.rs:50-51,585-602,622-625,816-849 belegt das prozessweite Sliding-Window, den IP-Schlüssel und die Reservierung vor Eingabevalidierung.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/self_explainer.rs:13-15,1140-1149 beschreibt eine peerweise Begrenzung und verlangt im bestehenden Test ausdrücklich unabhängige Kontingente für verschiedene Peers.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:309-337,563-572 dokumentiert und testet die Besucheradress-Ermittlung über X-Forwarded-For bei Loopback-Proxies. Dieser Vertrag wird im Self-Explainer-Pfad nicht angewendet.
countermeasures: Die vorhandene proxybewusste Rate-Limit-Middleware verändert ConnectInfo nicht und ist am öffentlichen Self-Explainer-Router nicht registriert: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/security.rs:342-353 und /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:112-161,2204-2271.
Das globale Admin-Audit lässt diesen Nicht-Admin-Pfad unmittelbar passieren: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/admin_audit.rs:16-24,100-102.
Das 60-Sekunden-Fenster begrenzt die Dauer einer einzelnen Sperre, verhindert aber keine erneute Kontingentbelegung.

Datenbank-Constraints schützen hier nicht: Die nachgelagerte Protokollierung wird bei den beschriebenen HTTP-400-Anfragen gar nicht erreicht. Beleg: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/self_explainer.rs:845-850,891-909.
gaps: Alle Quellbelege stammen aus 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. Keine Tests, Builds oder Laufzeitproben ausgeführt.

Die vollständige laufende Caddy-Konfiguration und zusätzliche externe Schutzschichten wurden nicht geprüft. Bestätigt ist der Quellpfad unter der ausdrücklich vorausgesetzten Loopback-Proxy-Topologie, nicht ein beobachteter Produktionsangriff.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af bestätigt. Der Dashboard-Start installiert die geprüfte Momentaufnahme, aber die Readiness ermittelt ihr internes API-Ziel ausschließlich aus alten Umgebungswerten. Dadurch kann sie eine gesunde, korrekt konfigurierte API als unerreichbar melden. Das ist ein belegter Konfigurationsfehler, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.
result.failure_scenario: Die aktive Momentaufnahme enthält internal_api.client_base_url='http://127.0.0.1:8776'; der gesunde Bot lauscht dort mit passendem internem Zugang. Datenbank und OAuth sind verfügbar. In der Dashboard-Prozessumgebung bleibt TWITCH_INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:18776' zurück, wo kein Dienst lauscht. GET /readyz prüft ausschließlich Port 18776 und liefert HTTP 503 mit upstream_connection_failed statt HTTP 200 für das konfigurierte gesunde Ziel. Beide URLs bestehen die Loopback- und Schema-Prüfung; die Bot-Port-Härtung erlaubt den tatsächlich verwendeten Standardport 8776.

original_candidate_group.claim: The self-explainer ignores the configured knowledge directory.

failure_scenarios.value: Start in Legacy mode with knowledge.directory pointing to a valid absolute documentation directory, no KNOWLEDGE_DIR environment variable, and a working directory without rust/knowledge. A documented Auto-Raid question receives the not-documented fallback because the self-explainer loads the nonexistent working-directory-relative path and permanently caches an empty knowledge base.

evidence.value: self_explainer.rs:354-375 ignores the active snapshot and selects KNOWLEDGE_DIR or rust/knowledge. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-knowledge/src/base.rs:42-73 explicitly skips missing namespace directories and returns an empty successful load. self_explainer.rs:453-461 then returns FALLBACK_NOT_DOCUMENTED without generation. failure_scenarios.value: Send question Auto-Raid with two user-history entries containing respectively 500 consecutive x characters and 500 consecutive y characters. Both entries are accepted unchanged. The 1000-character retrieval budget is exhausted by history, so Auto-Raid disappears completely. Lexical retrieval has no matching tokens and the Legacy or Shadow route returns the not-documented fallback even though public Auto-Raid documentation exists.

evidence.value: self_explainer.rs:181-204 permits these bounded user-history entries. At 409-419 the helper places two historical user messages before the current question and truncates the combined string from the front. The historical prefix alone is 1001 characters. At 453-461 empty retrieval results bypass generation. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-knowledge/src/base.rs:87-105,109-141 selects only documents with matching query tokens. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/knowledge/bot/auto-raid.md:1-19 is public documentation matching the omitted question.

expected_behavior.value: The current question must remain in the retrieval query; historical context may supplement it but must not consume its entire budget.

countermeasures.value: The eight-message and 500-character history limits do not prevent two messages from exhausting this separate 1000-character budget. Passing the question separately to the model cannot compensate because the empty-hit branch returns before invoking the model. Typed mode builds a different context and is not affected by this truncation. result.failure_scenario: Legacy- oder Shadow-Modus, öffentliche Wissensbasis geladen. H besteht aus 125 durch einzelne Leerzeichen getrennten Vorkommen von „der“, insgesamt 499 Zeichen. Im Website-Chat zweimal H fragen, dann „Wie funktioniert Auto-Raid?“. Die beiden vorherigen Nutzerbeiträge werden akzeptiert. retrieval_query verbindet H, H und die aktuelle Frage; diese beginnt erst bei Zeichenindex 1000. truncate behält höchstens die ersten 999 Zeichen plus Auslassungszeichen und entfernt deshalb die gesamte aktuelle Frage. Die verbleibenden „der“-Tokens sind ausschließlich Stoppwörter. KnowledgeBase::select liefert keine Dokumente, und answer_question gibt FALLBACK_NOT_DOCUMENTED mit grounded=false und leeren sources zurück, obwohl das öffentliche Auto-Raid-Dokument vorhanden ist. Kein Modellverhalten ist für diesen Fehlerfall erforderlich.

findings.title_de: Healthprobe weist IPv6-Loopback-HTTP zurück
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Healthprobe weist IPv6-Loopback-HTTP zurück.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: The health probe rejects valid IPv6 loopback HTTP URLs.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The health probe rejects valid IPv6 loopback HTTP URLs.

failure_scenarios.value: Provide a nonempty internal credential and TWITCH_INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL=http://[::1]:8776 for a worker bound to IPv6 loopback. URL parsing succeeds, but host_str returns [::1]. Parsing that bracketed string as IpAddr fails, so normalization treats it as non-loopback and rejects it. /readyz reports internal_api_not_configured instead of checking the valid loopback worker.

evidence.value: health_probe.rs:258-267 passes Url::host_str directly to is_loopback_host; 284-292 does not remove IPv6 brackets before IpAddr parsing. Rejection makes internal_api_config return None at 238, leading to the readiness reason at 172-174. The fixed dependency is url 2.5.8, whose /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/url-2.5.8/src/lib.rs:1130,1162-1167 documents and implements bracketed IPv6 host serialization.

expected_behavior.value: IPv6 loopback must qualify for the same HTTP loopback allowance as IPv4 loopback. The active configuration accepts loopback IpAddr values and its client URL builder correctly brackets IPv6 socket addresses.

countermeasures.value: Even enabling the non-loopback override does not allow this HTTP URL, because the incorrectly classified host subsequently requires HTTPS at 266-267. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-config/src/global.rs:305-307 accepts ::1, so configuration validation does not make the scenario unreachable. The neighboring Discord-login loopback helper receives separately normalized Host-header input and does not establish a guard for this probe.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af ist der Fehler statisch belegt. Url::host_str() liefert beim IPv6-Literal „[::1]“. Die Probe übergibt diesen geklammerten Wert unverändert an IpAddr::parse, das eine ungeklammerte Adresse erwartet. Dadurch wird echtes Loopback als extern eingestuft. Ein beabsichtigter IPv4-only-Vertrag ist nicht erkennbar; die vorhandenen Verträge unterstützen IPv6-Loopback ausdrücklich.
result.failure_scenario: TWITCH_INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL=http://[::1]:8776, ein vorhandener passender TWITCH_INTERNAL_API_TOKEN und eine gesunde interne API auf [::1]:8776. Datenbank und OAuth sind bereit, kein Fingerprint-Konflikt. normalize_internal_base_url verwirft die gültige HTTP-URL, internal_api_config liefert None und es erfolgt kein Upstream-Aufruf. GET /readyz beziehungsweise /health liefert fälschlich 503 mit internal_api_not_configured; /healthz meldet internalApiConfigured=false.
reachability_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:228-239,258-268,284-292: Der konfigurierte Basis-URL-Wert erreicht host_str und anschließend den fehlschlagenden IpAddr-Parse ohne Entfernung der IPv6-Klammern.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:113-129,172-188: Der öffentliche Readiness-Handler verwendet diese Konfiguration; None erzeugt internal_api_not_configured und HTTP 503.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:117-119,2204,2245-2248 und /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/admin_audit.rs:95-102: Die Probe-Routen sind im produktiven Router registriert; die globale Audit-Middleware lässt GET passieren.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:441,476-484,604-607: Produktiver Start ruft die Startup-Probe auf und stellt den Router bereit.
/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2053,2183-2195: Die interne API bindet die konfigurierte IpAddr als SocketAddr und kann auf ::1 lauschen.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:254-267,284-292: HTTP ist für Loopback vorgesehen; die Prüfung verwendet IpAddr::is_loopback und enthält keine Beschränkung auf IPv4.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-config/src/global.rs:99-125,302-307 und /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-config/src/dashboard_options.rs:319-337: Der interne API-Vertrag unterstützt Loopback-IpAddr und korrekt geklammerte IPv6-Clientziele. Die URL-Validierung entfernt ausdrücklich IPv6-Klammern und erlaubt HTTP auf Loopback.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/security.rs:137-159,416-421,440-444: Der Server akzeptiert IPv6-Loopback; bestehende Tests verlangen die Annahme von [::1] und http://[::1]:8080.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:555-579: Vorhandener Readiness-Test verlangt bei gesundem Upstream und eingerichtetem OAuth HTTP 200 ohne Fehlergründe.
countermeasures: TWITCH_INTERNAL_API_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=true behebt HTTP-IPv6 nicht: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:263-268 verlangt für den fälschlich extern eingestuften Host weiterhin HTTPS.
127.0.0.1 oder localhost vermeiden den Parsefehler, ersetzen aber kein ausschließlich auf ::1 erreichbares Ziel.
Serverseitige Loopback- und Zugangskontrollen greifen erst nach dem hier unterbundenen Request. Sie erklären die Ablehnung nicht.

Die Probe liest ihre URL direkt aus der Prozesskonfiguration, nicht aus einer Datenbanktabelle oder einem eingehenden Proxy-Header. Solche Constraints können die fehlende Klammernormalisierung nicht kompensieren.
gaps: Keine Builds, Tests oder Laufzeitprobes ausgeführt; Nachweis ausschließlich durch Quelllektüre am festen SHA. Die tatsächlich produktiv verwendete URL wurde nicht geprüft.

Die vier Tests in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:518-660 konstruieren InternalApiConfig direkt und umgehen die URL-Normalisierung. Sie enthalten keinen IPv6-Regressionsfall.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af bestätigt. Url::host_str() liefert für http://[::1]:8776 den geklammerten Host [::1]. Die Health-Probe übergibt ihn unverändert an IpAddr::parse, das keine URL-Klammern akzeptiert. Dadurch wird eine ausdrücklich unterstützte Loopback-Adresse fälschlich als entfernt behandelt und HTTP abgelehnt. Das ist ein Korrektheitsfehler, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.
result.failure_scenario: Der Bot lauscht mit internal_api.host='::1' auf Port 8776. Das Dashboard erhält TWITCH_INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL=http://[::1]:8776 und den passenden, nichtleeren internen Zugangsschlüssel. Datenbank, OAuth und Bot sind gesund. GET /readyz führt dennoch zu internal_api_config()=None und HTTP 503 mit internal_api_not_configured; die Anfrage an den Bot wird gar nicht gesendet. /healthz meldet gleichzeitig internalApiConfigured=false.

original_candidate_group.claim: Analytics database fingerprints ignore PostgreSQL DSN host overrides.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Analytics database fingerprints ignore PostgreSQL DSN host overrides.

failure_scenarios.value: Dashboard and worker use postgres:///analytics?host=/var/run/pg-a and postgres:///analytics?host=/var/run/pg-b, respectively, with those sockets serving distinct PostgreSQL instances. Actual connections use different servers, but both fingerprints hash the same ||analytics input. The startup check cannot detect the database mismatch and readiness remains successful when its other dependencies pass.

Actual pools connect using the full DSN at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:57. findings.title_de: Bereitschaftserfolg trotz unlesbarem HTTP-Antwortkörper
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Bereitschaftserfolg trotz unlesbarem HTTP-Antwortkörper.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: Readiness reports success when reading an HTTP 200 upstream health response body fails.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Readiness reports success when reading an HTTP 200 upstream health response body fails.

failure_scenarios.value: The internal API sends HTTP 200 headers, then its connection breaks or the response body times out. With a healthy dashboard database, configured OAuth and no cached fingerprint mismatch, /readyz returns HTTP 200 with ok=true and internalApiHealth={} despite the failed upstream health request.

The internal API sends HTTP 200 headers but leaves the response body unfinished until the ten-second request deadline expires. With a successful database check, configured OAuth and no cached fingerprint mismatch, GET /readyz or /health nevertheless returns HTTP 200 with status ready.

evidence.value: Sources checked against review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. Line 317 replaces response.text() errors with an empty string. Lines 354-358 convert that empty string into Some({}); lines 329-336 accept any JSON object. Lines 154-170 therefore take the success branch, and lines 184-200 emit ready/HTTP 200. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:117-119 registers /readyz and /health directly to this handler.

At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, response.text().await.unwrap_or_default() at line 317 turns a body-read timeout into an empty string. parse_json at lines 354-359 converts that string into an empty JSON object, which passes the object check at lines 329-336. readyz_response at lines 154-170 therefore records successful upstream health without adding an error reason; lines 184-189 select HTTP 200. The same helper also serves the startup fingerprint check at line 52.

expected_behavior.value: An upstream body transport failure must follow the existing upstream-error path and make readiness HTTP 503, just as connection failures do; an unreadable body is not a successful health payload.

A health request that exceeds INTERNAL_HEALTH_TIMEOUT must be treated as failed. map_reqwest_error at lines 339-345 already defines upstream_timeout, and readyz_response at lines 159-170 and 184-189 converts upstream failures into degraded HTTP 503 responses. Body-read timeouts should follow that failure path rather than become successful empty health payloads.

countermeasures.value: The ten-second request timeout and disabled redirects do not help because the body error is subsequently discarded. HTTP statuses >=400 and non-object JSON are rejected, but neither guard rejects the synthetic empty object. Other readiness checks can independently fail, so the false success requires them to pass.

The ten-second reqwest timeout and disabled redirects are present and bound the upstream wait, but the body-read error is discarded after the deadline fires. Other readiness failures can mask the false success, so the scenario explicitly requires those checks to pass. Within this slice, the Discord relay's similar body-error suppression only formats an already unsuccessful response for logging; it does not create another successful health verdict.

original_candidate_group.claim: Self-explainer database logging discards both SQL failures and logging timeouts without diagnostics.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Self-explainer database logging discards both SQL failures and logging timeouts without diagnostics.

failure_scenarios.value: The logging INSERT fails because its database role lacks INSERT permission, or database acquisition/execution exceeds three seconds. The visitor still receives an answer, but no question-and-answer row is stored and this handler emits no diagnostic identifying the lost database log.

evidence.value: Lines 897-909 discard the complete timeout result, including both Ok(Err(sqlx::Error)) and Err(Elapsed). /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/self_explainer_log.rs:41-63 returns SQL errors with await? and performs no internal error logging. expected_behavior.value: Keep answers independent of best-effort logging, but make a failed INSERT or elapsed logging deadline observable. A stronger durability or retry guarantee is not established, so this remains C.

countermeasures.value: The three-second timeout protects response latency, and the independent Discord relay may preserve a copy, but neither exposes the database logging failure. The focused twin /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/dashboard_assistent.rs:386-394 also discards its background logging result.

findings.title_de: Startup-Fingerprint wird nach Erholung nicht nachgeprüft
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Startup-Fingerprint wird nach Erholung nicht nachgeprüft.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: A failed startup fingerprint check is never completed after the internal API recovers.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A failed startup fingerprint check is never completed after the internal API recovers.

failure_scenarios.value: The internal API is unavailable during dashboard startup, leaving the cached upstream fingerprint absent and mismatch=false. It later becomes available with a fingerprint different from the dashboard's database. Subsequent readiness requests fetch that differing fingerprint but still return ready if the other checks pass; the initial failed comparison remains unperformed for the process lifetime.

evidence.value: Lines 43-48 initialize an absent upstream fingerprint and false mismatch; lines 75-81 only warn after a failed startup request. Lines 154-158 retain fresh health data without comparing fingerprints, and lines 180-181 consult only the startup mismatch flag. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:441,484 performs the check once and installs its result as an immutable extension. The test at health_probe.rs:626-658 explicitly confirms that a fresh mismatch does not change cached readiness.

expected_behavior.value: A recovery policy could complete an initially failed identity check once the upstream returns, preventing ready status with unverified database identity. Because the existing test deliberately preserves startup-only comparison semantics, changing this policy requires a C decision rather than an automatic fix.

countermeasures.value: Startup failures are warned, live upstream availability is checked on every readiness request, and a mismatch detected at startup does block readiness. None completes a comparison that failed initially. The explicit cached-only test is evidence against classifying this behavior as an obvious B bug.

findings.title_de: Bereitschaftsabfrage hält DB-Verbindung unbefristet
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Bereitschaftsabfrage hält DB-Verbindung unbefristet.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: The readiness database query can hold a pool connection indefinitely.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The readiness database query can hold a pool connection indefinitely.

failure_scenarios.value: A readiness request successfully acquires a database connection, then its PostgreSQL backend stops responding while the socket remains open. The SELECT 1 await has no execution deadline. The request does not reach the degraded response or the upstream check and retains its connection until cancellation or database recovery. Repeated probes can occupy the available pool connections.

evidence.value: At the fixed review SHA, health_probe.rs:117-123 awaits fetch_one without a timeout. Dashboard startup uses tb_db::connect at rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400. In rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:10-11 and 20-58, that selects read_only=false; acquire_timeout bounds acquisition, while the statement_timeout configuration at lines 47-53 applies only to the unused readonly mode. The public route registrations and serving wrappers inspected in tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs and tb-dashboard/src/main.rs contain no request timeout covering this query.

expected_behavior.value: A stalled database should eventually yield a degraded readiness result rather than indefinitely retain a probe and connection. health_probe.rs:149-151 and 184-189 already define database_unavailable and HTTP 503 for database failures, but no database execution budget is specified. Selecting that budget is therefore classified C, not an automatic fix recommendation.

countermeasures.value: The pool-size limit caps database connections, and acquisition/connect deadlines bound callers waiting for a connection; neither bounds a query after acquisition. The readonly pool's twenty-second statement timeout is not installed on the production dashboard pool. The internal API's ten-second timeout begins only after the database query finishes. Caller-side cancellation can end an individual probe, but the handler has no independent deadline.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Log-API schwärzt Zeit- und Level-Felder nicht.

original_candidate_group.claim: The error-log API returns secrets unredacted in its timestamp and level fields.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The error-log API returns secrets unredacted in its timestamp and level fields.

failure_scenarios.value: A scanned logs/*.log file contains the nonstandard error line `ERROR access_token=example123 - request failed`. The supported two-part fallback returns timestamp=`ERROR access_token=example123`, exposing the value in GET /twitch/api/admin/system/errors even though context is redacted. A four-part line with a secret in its third part similarly exposes it through level. These examples use synthetic values, not actual credentials.

evidence.value: In errors.rs, lines 139-168 collect and read log candidates; lines 183-185 accept the example because it contains ERROR. Lines 193-202 copy raw split fields into timestamp and level. Lines 205-206 sanitize only message and context, while lines 221-227 retain timestamp and level unchanged. Lines 88-100 serialize those entries in the API response.

expected_behavior.value: The explicit contract in errors.rs:11-12 says secrets in log lines are masked before output. Secret-bearing derived metadata must not retain the original value while message and context redact it.

countermeasures.value: require_admin at errors.rs:81-83 limits exposure to authenticated admins, so this is a redaction-contract bug rather than a demonstrated authentication bypass. Existing secret patterns cover access_token, but they are never applied to timestamp or level. Strict metadata validation or applying the existing redactor to those fields would close this specific bypass.

findings.title_de: SQL-Konsole ersetzt Standardwerte durch Typplatzhalter
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: SQL-Konsole ersetzt Standardwerte durch Typplatzhalter.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: SQL console replaces standard NUMERIC and naive timestamp values with type placeholders.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: SQL console replaces standard NUMERIC and naive timestamp values with type placeholders.

failure_scenarios.value: An authenticated administrator submits SELECT 12.34 AS amount. Validation accepts it and PostgreSQL returns a non-null NUMERIC value, but every attempted decoder is incompatible, so the successful API response contains rows=[["<NUMERIC>"]] instead of [["12.34"]]. SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-10-08 12:00:00' AS t similarly returns <TIMESTAMP> instead of the timestamp value.

evidence.value: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/system/query.rs:212-245 promises scalar stringification but handles neither NUMERIC nor NaiveDateTime. SQLx type checks reject incompatible decoders before decoding: /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-core-0.9.0/src/row.rs:112-133. Its String compatibility list excludes NUMERIC/TIMESTAMP, and DateTime uses TIMESTAMPTZ: /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-postgres-0.9.0/src/types/str.rs:11-36 and /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-postgres-0.9.0/src/types/chrono/datetime.rs:11-21.

expected_behavior.value: Successful SELECT results must retain standard scalar values as strings, preserving their value and precision, as specified by the scalar-stringification contract.

countermeasures.value: The placeholder prevents a panic but discards the actual result. READ ONLY, timeouts, and the 200-row limit do not affect decoding. SQL NULL is handled separately by SQLx's nullable extraction and is not the reported defect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/pages/monitoring/DatabaseQuery.tsx:62-69 displays the returned strings directly without recovering lost values.

result.reason: Am SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af fehlen Decoder für NUMERIC und TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE. SQLx konvertiert diese Typen bei try_get nicht automatisch in String oder Float; DateTime<Utc> entspricht TIMESTAMPTZ, nicht dem naiven TIMESTAMP. Nichtleere Zellen erreichen deshalb den Typplatzhalter. Das widerspricht dem ausdrücklich dokumentierten Vertrag für alle Skalartypen. Kein Sicherheitsbefund.
result.failure_scenario: Ein gültig angemeldeter Admin führt in der SQL-Konsole SELECT 1.25::numeric AS n, TIMESTAMP '2026-10-08 12:34:56' AS t aus. Die Abfrage besteht die SELECT-Prüfung und benötigt weder Tabellen noch bestehende Datensätze. Statt der Werte „1.25“ und „2026-10-08 12:34:56“ liefert der Handler HTTP 200 mit rows=[["<NUMERIC>","<TIMESTAMP>"]] und rowCount=1. Die Oberfläche zeigt diese Platzhalter unverändert.
