countermeasures: SELECT-Validierung, READ ONLY, Zeitlimits und Zeilenlimit schützen die Ausführung, wandeln aber keine Ergebnistypen um. Tabellen-Constraints und Schema-Migrationen können den tabellenlosen Fehlerfall nicht verhindern.

Der Platzhalter ist laut /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/system/query.rs:243 eine bewusste Panic-Abwehr für unbekannte Typen. Das belegt keine beabsichtigte Ausnahme vom Vertrag für standardmäßige Skalartypen.

Manuelle ::text-Casts umgehen den Fehler, werden aber weder vom Handler noch vom Client eingefügt. Der Legacy-Proxy ist nur ein Fallback für nicht registrierte Routen, siehe /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:501-503; er ersetzt diesen nativen Handler nicht.

Die gelesenen Handler-Tests decken NUMERIC und naive TIMESTAMP-Zellen nicht ab. Die Häufigkeit entsprechender produktiver Abfragen wurde nicht untersucht.

Nicht-NULL-Werte landen deshalb im Typplatzhalter, obwohl der Handler ausdrücklich alle Skalartypen als Stringwerte verspricht. Der absichtliche Fallback verhindert Panics, rechtfertigt aber nicht diesen Wertverlust. Korrektheitsbug, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke und keine notwendige Datenmigration.

findings.title_de: Leeres SQL-Ergebnis verliert Spalteninformationen
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Leeres SQL-Ergebnis verliert Spalteninformationen.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: SQL console loses result-column metadata when a SELECT returns no rows.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: SQL console loses result-column metadata when a SELECT returns no rows.

failure_scenarios.value: An authenticated administrator submits SELECT 1 AS n WHERE FALSE. findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Admin-Log sieht native systemd-Dienstfehler nicht.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: Admin error log endpoint cannot see native service errors in the shipped systemd deployment.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin error log endpoint cannot see native service errors in the shipped systemd deployment.

failure_scenarios.value: Using the shipped service units on a fresh deployment, a system-health database read fails and health_handler emits a tracing ERROR. Native tracing writes to the process output captured by systemd, not to the legacy files scanned by errors_handler. A subsequent authenticated request to /system/errors returns no entry for that error, potentially total=0 despite a real service failure.

Die ausgelieferte Dashboard-Unit läuft ohne alte Logdateien. Eine Datenbankabfrage scheitert beispielsweise wegen einer fehlenden Tabelle und der Handler schreibt tracing::error!. Ein anschließender berechtigter GET auf /twitch/api/admin/system/errors liefert trotzdem HTTP 200 mit entries=[] und total=0, weil diese Fehlerausgabe nicht in den gelesenen Dateien landet. Bot-Fehler sind aus demselben Grund ebenfalls unsichtbar.

evidence.value: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/system/errors.rs:34-39 and 139-169 scan only relative logs/*.log files and silently skip absent files. Native logging is initialized with the default formatter at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:373-375 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:482-484. The complete shipped units at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/deadlock-twitch-dashboard-rust.service:1-72 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/deadlock-twitch-bot-rust.service:1-74 do not redirect process output into these files. Their logs bind mounts also point to separate service-private directories.

Ein konkreter Fehlerproduzent ist /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/system/database.rs:48-51. Der Router registriert den Errors-Endpunkt in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1035-1038 und bindet den System-Router bei 2239 ein. Statischer Nachweis für den ausgelieferten Startvertrag, keine Aussage über außerhalb des Repos eingerichtete Logweiterleitungen.

expected_behavior.value: The admin error view should expose native service errors or clearly distinguish an unavailable log source from an error-free service. The exact supported logging source after the Rust cutover is not specified clearly enough for an automatic fix.

Die Fehleransicht soll Laufzeitfehler aus dem Monitoring-Endpoint anzeigen, wie /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/pages/monitoring/ErrorLogs.tsx:49-60 beschreibt. Fehlende Anbindung der tatsächlichen Fehlerquelle sollte nicht als fehlende Fehlereinträge erscheinen. C, weil der Handler ausdrücklich einen Legacy-Dateivertrag nachbildet und die Auswahl einer neuen Fehlerquelle samt dienstübergreifender Leserechte über einen eindeutigen lokalen Fehlerfix hinausgeht.

countermeasures.value: LogsDirectory and BindPaths create accessible directories but do not populate the scanned files or expose the bot's private log directory to the dashboard. The deployed wrappers have no output-to-file bridge. Classified C because choosing journal access, shared files, or a new native logging sink requires an operational logging-contract decision.

Admin-Prüfung, Maskierung und die Suche nach weiteren *.log-Dateien sind vorhanden, stellen jedoch keine Verbindung zur stdout-/Journal-Ausgabe her. Das tolerierte Fehlen alter Logdateien verhindert Panics, verdeckt aber die fehlende Quelle. Beide Rust-Logger und beide Startskripte wurden gezielt als Zwillinge geprüft. Empfehlung nur dokumentieren: tatsächliche Fehlerquelle und sichere Freigabe an das Dashboard festlegen; keine Änderung ausgeführt.

findings.title_de: SQL-Konsole behält Sitzungssperren nach Rollback
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: SQL-Konsole behält Sitzungssperren nach Rollback.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: Admin-console session advisory locks survive request rollback and can block the bot's monthly season closure.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin-console session advisory locks survive request rollback and can block the bot's monthly season closure.

failure_scenarios.value: An authenticated admin submits SELECT pg_advisory_lock(713219, 27) while that lock is free. Validation accepts it, FETCH evaluates it, and the request succeeds. PostgreSQL session advisory locks survive ROLLBACK, so the dashboard's pooled connection retains the lock. A subsequent due monthly season closure waits on the identical transaction advisory lock until the dashboard connection closes or the lock is explicitly released.

evidence.value: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, the assigned query.rs lines 55-86 accept this SELECT; lines 151-185 execute it on a pooled transaction; lines 187-209 only roll back before returning. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:41-58 configures reusable connections without a release/reset hook. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/monthly_raid_boost.rs:143-153 waits on pg_advisory_xact_lock(713219, 27). /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/monthly_raid_boost.rs:22-35,54-61 reaches that method from the periodic scheduler; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:546 starts it. Static review only, as required.

expected_behavior.value: Diagnostic SQL should not leave locks blocking unrelated bot operations after a request finishes. However, query.rs lines 10-11 explicitly permit arbitrary authenticated-admin SQL and disclaim a SQL sandbox. The policy for side-effecting SELECT functions is therefore unclear; this is C, not an automatically authorized behavior change.

countermeasures.value: require_admin restricts reachability to admins. SELECT validation, READ ONLY, statement_timeout and lock_timeout do not release successfully acquired session advisory locks. The inspected role configuration at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/twitch-runtime-roles.sql does not revoke these built-in functions. Connection retirement eventually releases the lock. No public privilege escalation is claimed; any restriction or disposable-connection isolation needs an explicit contract decision.

findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: Admin SQL results have no byte bound despite the 200-row limit.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin SQL results have no byte bound despite the 200-row limit.

failure_scenarios.value: On a dashboard with less than 1 GB of available memory, an authenticated admin submits SELECT repeat('x', 10000000) FROM generate_series(1, 200). This short, SELECT-only query passes validation and requests exactly 200 rows, but its text cells total 2 GB. If the local database supplies enough rows before the five-second statement deadline, fetch_all exhausts dashboard memory before result conversion or serialization completes.

evidence.value: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, query.rs:179-185 buffers complete PostgreSQL rows with fetch_all. Lines 201-217 create additional owned strings, and lines 128-138 serialize the entire result. Neither validation nor fetching limits cell size or cumulative result bytes.

expected_behavior.value: The documented resource hardening at query.rs:8-9 bounds row count, SQL input size and statement duration. A byte budget would also prevent a small valid query from exhausting service memory, but no existing maximum result-byte contract was found. Selecting that limit changes accepted query behavior, so this remains C.

countermeasures.value: Admin authentication, the 16 KiB input cap, READ ONLY, a non-held cursor, MAX_ROWS=200, statement_timeout=5s and lock_timeout=1s are present. None bounds bytes per fetched row. This is not an unauthenticated vulnerability; no probe or test was executed.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Logabfrage liest ganze Dateien auf Tokio-Workern.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: Error-log requests scan complete files synchronously on Tokio workers.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Error-log requests scan complete files synchronously on Tokio workers.

failure_scenarios.value: Persistent logs contain multi-gigabyte files on slow storage. Authorized error-log requests occupying all runtime workers each read those files from their beginning before returning even the first page. Unrelated dashboard requests and background tasks cannot progress on those workers during the synchronous scans. An exceptionally large unterminated log line additionally causes allocation proportional to that entire line, despite the later message-length caps.

evidence.value: errors.rs:88 calls load_error_log_entries directly from the async handler. Lines 155-169 synchronously iterate BufReader::lines until EOF; max_lines only controls deque eviction, not bytes read or line allocation. The 200-entry early return happens at lines 124-130 after a complete file has already been read. The deployed service binds persistent logs at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/deadlock-twitch-dashboard-rust.service:38-41.

expected_behavior.value: errors.rs:27-28 and 106-108 describe scanning the latest 4,000 lines. Log retrieval should not monopolize the shared async runtime or allocate unbounded input lines. A bounded reader must also preserve the existing entry-ID semantics; the byte budget and compatible reading strategy are not specified, so this remains C.

countermeasures.value: require_admin, the 4,000-line deque, the 200 returned-entry cap and the 1,200/2,000-character output caps were checked. These limit retained line count or final output, not full-file I/O or raw-line size. Router composition has no blocking-task offload for this handler. External log rotation could reduce exposure, but its live configuration was not inspected.

findings.title_de: DB-Statistik wartet unbefristet auf Tabellensperre
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: DB-Statistik wartet unbefristet auf Tabellensperre.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

original_candidate_group.claim: Database-stat requests can retain shared pool connections indefinitely behind a table lock.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Database-stat requests can retain shared pool connections indefinitely behind a table lock.

failure_scenarios.value: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout unset, a maintenance transaction holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on twitch_streamers. Concurrent authorized database-stat requests reach COUNT(*) and wait while retaining every connection in the shared dashboard pool. Other database-backed dashboard requests then fail pool acquisition, although PostgreSQL remains reachable.

evidence.value: database.rs:48 awaits database_stats without a deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/system_database.rs:55-65 performs COUNT(*) without a statement or lock timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 uses tb_db::connect; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-55 sets SQL statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, not this production path. System routes share this pool through /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2239.

expected_behavior.value: A blocked monitoring query should terminate and release its connection rather than disable unrelated dashboard operations. No explicit deadline contract for this endpoint was found, and live PostgreSQL defaults were not inspected. Choosing the timeout policy therefore remains C.

countermeasures.value: Admin authentication and bounded tracked-table count are present. acquire_timeout bounds obtaining a connection, not execution after acquisition. The SQL-console handler's separate 5s/1s transaction limits do not protect database_stats. Production router composition has no request timeout; externally configured PostgreSQL deadlines could prevent this scenario.

original_members.claim: Manual plan saves discard valid timezone-less expiry timestamps.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated admin submits login for an existing streamer, plan_id=plus and expires_at=2026-12-31T18:00:00 through POST /twitch/admin/manual-plan. The offset-free ISO timestamp fails parse_from_rfc3339, becomes None, and is stored as NULL. The request reports success, but the gifted Plus plan remains active after the specified expiration.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, primary lines 349-367 parse only RFC3339 after the date-only special case. Lines 161 and 184-199 persist the resulting Option without validation. The nullable text column is defined in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:373-374. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:451-457, absent expiry means not expired.
original_members.expected_behavior: The handler identifies its parser as a port of the entitlement repository parser at primary lines 344-348. The equivalent canonical parser explicitly accepts offset-free ISO timestamps as UTC in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:621-628,649-662. Its test at lines 956-961 confirms that 2026-06-30T12:00:00 must retain its timestamp and receive a UTC offset.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication and session CSRF protect who can submit, not expiry semantics. The save path neither rejects this nonempty value nor restores its expiry. The ordinary dashboard date picker emits date-only values, which are unaffected, but the registered form endpoint accepts this timestamp string directly. A targeted twin search found the canonical parser already handles naive timestamps; the defective duplicate is the manual-plan handler parser. No code changes or runtime probes performed.

original_members.claim: Manual-plan saves silently discard offset-free ISO expiry timestamps and create non-expiring overrides.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated admin with valid form CSRF submits login for an existing streamer, plan_id=plus and expires_at=2026-12-31T12:00:00. The save succeeds, but manual_plan_expires_at is stored as NULL. The override remains active after the requested expiration.
original_members.evidence: The assigned parser at lines 349-367 supports date-only values and RFC3339 timestamps but has no offset-free ISO branch. RFC3339 parsing rejects the given value, and .ok() converts the error to None. set_manual_plan at lines 161 and 184-206 binds that None directly into manual_plan_expires_at and returns success. The same domain's canonical parser in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:621-663 explicitly supports naive ISO timestamps as UTC, with the exact format asserted at lines 956-962. NULL expiry is treated as not expired at lines 451-457.
original_members.expected_behavior: Preserve the documented shared parse_datetime_value contract: an offset-free ISO timestamp represents UTC and must retain its expiration. The manual-plan parser identifies itself as a port of that same parser at lines 344-348. The existing canonical resolver test explicitly verifies this accepted input format.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin and session-bound CSRF checks run before saving but do not validate expiry semantics. The current date-picker UI ordinarily submits date-only values, which work, but the registered form endpoint accepts the stated timestamp without another format guard. Invalid and blank values intentionally map to None; this finding concerns a valid format supported by the shared contract. A targeted twin search found only the canonical resolver parser and this handler parser; the canonical implementation already contains the missing naive-UTC handling.

result.reason: The save handler silently converts a supported timezone-less timestamp into SQL NULL. Its explicit parser-parity contract and the canonical parser's UTC handling establish the expected behavior. The date-only UI limits exposure but does not prevent authenticated form requests.
result.failure_scenario: An authenticated admin with valid CSRF submits POST /twitch/admin/manual-plan for an existing streamer with a Twitch user ID, plan_id=plus and expires_at=2026-12-31T12:00:00. The RFC3339-only save parser returns None, the UPDATE writes manual_plan_expires_at=NULL, and the handler reports success. Instead of expiring at noon UTC, the plus override remains active without an expiry.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Saving a free manual override can immediately overwrite it with an analytics trial.

original_members.claim: Saving a free manual override can immediately overwrite it with an analytics trial.
original_members.failure_scenario: A streamer has first_login_at more than 24 hours ago, trial_ever_granted=0 and no paid billing subscription. An admin saves plan_id=free or raid_free with a note. After writing the requested override, the handler calls effective_plan_id, which auto-grants analytics_trial and replaces the freshly written plan, expiry and note before returning.
original_members.evidence: Primary lines 184-214 write the override and immediately call the effective-plan resolver through lines 316-317. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:384-389 runs trial eligibility before resolving the manual override. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/trial.rs:306-323 allows this state because free and raid_free are placeholders under lines 22-27; lines 325-339 overwrite the plan, expiry and notes.
original_members.expected_behavior: The manual-plan handler promises to set the requested override, and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:480-483 describes an explicit admin downgrade to raid_free as terminal. However, the trial policy explicitly treats free plans as eligible placeholders. Whether an explicit admin downgrade should suppress the automatic trial is therefore an unresolved policy conflict, not an authorized B fix.
original_members.countermeasures: The one-time flag, 24-hour grace period and paid-subscription guard prevent this in other states, but do not distinguish an explicit admin free override from a default free placeholder. Non-free manual rights block the grant. Resolving the conflict requires clarifying that distinction before changing behavior; no fix is proposed as automatic.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The trial-start endpoint grants trials after a failed paid-subscription lookup, overriding existing paid access.

original_members.claim: The trial-start endpoint grants trials after a failed paid-subscription lookup, overriding existing paid access.
original_members.failure_scenario: An active authenticated partner has an active paid Stripe subscription, no manual override and no previously granted trial. During POST /twitch/api/billing/trial/start, the subscription SELECT fails with a query cancellation or transient connection error. Subsequent queries succeed. The endpoint responds HTTP 200 with status granted and commits an analytics_trial manual override instead of rejecting the paid customer.
original_members.evidence: At the pinned review SHA, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/trial.rs:233-250 maps every subscription-query error to false. grant_trial_inner at lines 142-215 performs this check before starting its transaction, then inserts the trial and commits when the other guards are false. The assigned handler maps Granted to HTTP 200 at lines 38-44. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:480-491 makes the resulting active manual override terminal, preventing fallback to the paid subscription.
original_members.expected_behavior: An existing paid subscription must prevent a trial grant, as asserted by /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/trial.rs:435-457. A non-missing-table database failure must not establish that no subscription exists; the handler's documented DB-error outcome is HTTP 500 with status error.
original_members.countermeasures: Partner authentication, active-partner gating and CSRF protection restrict callers but do not validate subscription-check results. The transaction begins after the failed SELECT, so that failure does not abort the subsequent grant. The manual-plan and once-only guards do not help in the stated initial state. Missing billing tables have an explicitly documented compatibility fallback, but cancellation and connection failures are swallowed by the same wildcard. The same helper is used by the automatic trial grant at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/trial.rs:282-349; this is a verified shared twin, not a claim of coverage of other callers.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A stale score refresh within the same second can restore a manual raid boost after the override is cleared.

original_members.claim: A stale score refresh within the same second can restore a manual raid boost after the override is cleared.
original_members.failure_scenario: A partner has only a plus manual override, with no other boost source. A save-triggered refresh reads the active plus override and then pauses. Within the same UTC second, an admin clear request removes the override and completes its refresh, storing multiplier 1.0. The earlier refresh subsequently writes its cached boosted input. Both last_computed_at values are identical after second truncation, so the conflict guard accepts the stale write and leaves an inflated score after both requests complete.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Admin billing requests have no application deadline for database lock waits.

original_members.claim: Admin billing requests have no application deadline for database lock waits.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, a separate transaction holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on affiliate_accounts. An authenticated admin requests GET /twitch/api/admin/billing/affiliates while that transaction remains open. The SELECT waits indefinitely, retaining the request and a checked-out connection. Concurrent requests can occupy the whole shared pool, causing other dashboard requests to fail acquisition. This is a conditional deployment scenario, not a verified production incident.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The handler awaits the loader without a deadline at the finding location, lines 40-42; subscriptions has the same pattern at lines 26-28. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/admin_billing.rs:56-65 executes SELECT from affiliate_accounts using fetch_all. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 and 476-483 creates and routes the shared pool through tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:10-12,20-59 configures acquisition deadlines but sets statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, not connect. The applicable route and global middleware in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1195-1202,1287-1298,2204-2271 contain no request deadline.
original_members.expected_behavior: Unavailable database work should terminate within an agreed budget and use the existing error response rather than retain shared connections indefinitely. The handler already maps database failures to ApiError at lines 13-15 and 40-42, but no execution-time budget is specified. Choosing that budget remains a policy change, so this is C.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication prevents anonymous exploitation. Pool capacity and acquisition timeouts bound connection count and acquisition waiting, not execution on an already acquired connection. The 20-second statement timeout in connect_readonly does not apply to the connector used here. A PostgreSQL role, DSN option, or external request deadline could mitigate the scenario; effective production settings were not inspected because database and network probes are prohibited. The subscription handler is the checked twin. No A/B fix authorization is implied.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A recycled Twitch login grants access to the previous owner's Stripe customer portal.

original_members.claim: A recycled Twitch login grants access to the previous owner's Stripe customer portal.
original_members.failure_scenario: Partner A completes checkout while named oldname, leaving a subscription with customer_reference=oldname and Stripe customer cus_A. A later renames their channel. A different Twitch account B obtains oldname and becomes a dashboard partner. B's legitimate session has B's platform ID, but GET /twitch/abbo/rechnungen selects A's subscription by the matching login and redirects B to a Stripe portal session for cus_A. B can access A's invoices and the customer-management functions enabled in that portal. An authenticated cancellation POST with B's own CSRF token likewise operates on A's subscription.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The primary file prefers login for customer_reference at 947-960, sends it to Stripe at 246-252, and selects subscriptions by login OR platform ID OR reference at 1095-1116 without verifying an immutable owner. The invoices handler passes the selected customer ID to create_billing_portal_session at 506-545; cancel_execute uses the same lookup at 420-471. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/webhook_apply.rs:236-283 and 423-446 persist the checkout reference without a Twitch owner ID. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:462-477 defines no immutable Twitch owner column. The related profile lookup in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_profile.rs:184-209 also identifies private billing data by the mutable login.
original_members.expected_behavior: Only the Twitch identity that owns a Stripe customer or subscription may access or manage it. The primary file's own contract at 28-31 promises management of the user's own subscription. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:1410-1437 explicitly establishes that renamed or reassigned Twitch logins are not identity evidence.
original_members.countermeasures: Session authentication is ID-based and fail-closed, but it authenticates B rather than establishing ownership of cus_A. Cancellation's POST and CSRF checks validate B's legitimate request, not subscription ownership; the invoice route requires no CSRF. StripeClient creates the portal using the supplied customer ID and the application's secret, with no Twitch ownership check (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/client.rs:229-240). Native billing routes are registered without an additional object-ownership guard in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1651-1704. No runtime or network probe was performed.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A stale admin cookie prevents valid partner requests from cancelling subscriptions or saving billing forms.

original_members.claim: A stale admin cookie prevents valid partner requests from cancelling subscriptions or saving billing forms.
original_members.failure_scenario: A browser sends a valid twitch_dash_session, that partner session's correct csrf_token, and an expired master_dash_session left by an earlier admin login. DashboardAuthLevel authenticates the partner, but verify_cancel_csrf unconditionally selects the nonempty admin cookie, validates against the expired admin session, and returns false. Cancellation redirects to cancel=csrf_invalid and promo-message saving returns 403. The same failure occurs with two valid sessions when the form token belongs to the authenticated partner rather than the admin session.
original_members.evidence: The primary helper at 1025-1036 selects admin before partner and never tries the partner after failed validation. cancel_handler calls it at 345-348 and promo_message_handler at 375-381. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/level.rs:349-367 authenticates the valid partner first in public context. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/auth_status.rs:94-101 returns the token for the selected authenticated session. The duplicate validator in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_profile.rs:408-439 has the same precedence defect.
original_members.expected_behavior: An unrelated stale cookie must not invalidate an authenticated partner's correct CSRF token. This exact contract is established by the existing regression test stale_admin_cookie_verdeckt_nicht_gueltige_partner_session in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/csrf.rs:637-661.
original_members.countermeasures: The shared CSRF middleware handles the stale-admin case and recognizes authenticated-session markers, but billing form routes deliberately use their own body-token validators without that middleware (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1662-1678). Session validation fails closed, so this is legitimate-request rejection rather than a CSRF bypass. Existing primary-file tests cover missing tokens and single partner cookies, not the mixed-cookie case.

original_members.failure_scenario: A browser carries an expired master_dash_session cookie alongside a valid twitch_dash_session. claim.claim: A stale admin cookie prevents valid partner requests from cancelling subscriptions or saving billing forms.

result.reason: Confirmed for the registered native billing form POSTs, not every subscription-management path. Authentication selects the valid partner session, but form CSRF validation selects an unrelated admin cookie merely because it is present. A missing or expired admin session therefore rejects the partner's correct CSRF token. This is a deterministic correctness bug, not a demonstrated security bypass.
result.failure_scenario: At SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, an allowed partner has a valid twitch_dash_session=P and obtains its CSRF token T from GET /twitch/api/v2/auth-status. The same Cookie header also contains master_dash_session=S, whose admin session no longer exists or has expired. A POST /twitch/abbo/kündigen with csrf_token=T, a configured Stripe client and an existing subscription authenticates as Partner but redirects to /twitch/pricing?cancel=csrf_invalid without reaching cancellation. A POST /twitch/abbo/rechnungsdaten with T and all required nonempty profile fields instead redirects to /twitch/pricing?cycle=1&profile=error without saving. Removing only the stale admin cookie makes both CSRF helpers validate P/T successfully.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:315-351 explicitly supports authenticated cancellation POSTs with a valid form CSRF token and dispatches them to cancel_execute. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_profile.rs:38-98 supports saving the authenticated partner's valid billing profile.

findings.title_de: Abrechnungsformular weist dauerhafte Partnerzugangssitzung ab
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Abrechnungsformular weist dauerhafte Partnerzugangssitzung ab.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Billing form CSRF validation rejects every request authenticated solely by a durable partner-access session.

original_members.claim: Billing form CSRF validation rejects every request authenticated solely by a durable partner-access session.
original_members.failure_scenario: A partner signs in through the one-time partner-login flow and receives only twitch_dash_session_partner. DashboardAuthLevel accepts this valid, device-bound session. A cancellation or promo-message POST then reaches verify_cancel_csrf, which recognizes neither that cookie nor its partner_token session type and returns false before checking the presented token. The partner cannot use those billing form actions through this supported login flow, even if the correct stored CSRF token is supplied.
original_members.evidence: The primary helper at 1008 and 1025-1031 recognizes only master_dash_session/discord_admin and twitch_dash_session/twitch. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/partner_login.rs:325-364 creates and sets only the durable partner-access cookie. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/level.rs:371-393 accepts that cookie as Partner authentication. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:695-739 generates and stores a CSRF token for the durable session. The billing-profile form validator at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_profile.rs:408-439 repeats the omission.
original_members.expected_behavior: A supported authenticated partner session with a correct session-bound CSRF token must be able to submit the partner's billing forms. These handlers gate on DashboardAuthLevel::Partner without requiring a different login method, and durable partner sessions already contain a CSRF token.
original_members.countermeasures: The durable-session loader validates expiry, identity version, device fingerprint and partner eligibility before authentication (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:1878-1947). Those protections do not bridge its cookie into the form validator. Additionally, the durable branch sets no AuthenticatedPartnerSessionId marker, so auth-status returns no CSRF token for it (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/auth_status.rs:94-102). Ordinary Twitch reauthentication provides a workaround, but no automatic bridge is present in the inspected billing route path. This is a fail-closed functionality defect, not an authentication bypass.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af bestätigt: Die Authentifizierung akzeptiert die durable Session als normalen Partner, die Billing-Formprüfung berücksichtigt deren Cookie jedoch niemals. Das ist ein Funktionsfehler, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke. Die Aussage gilt für die betroffenen Form-POSTs, nicht für sämtliche Billing-Routen.
result.failure_scenario: Ein aktiver Partner nutzt den Einmal-Login und besitzt ausschließlich twitch_dash_session_partner. Mit gültiger, nicht abgelaufener Session und passendem User-Agent sendet er POST /twitch/abbo/promo-message mit einem zulässigen Nachrichtentext. Die Authentifizierung liefert Partner, anschließend antwortet der Handler mit HTTP 403 und csrf_token_invalid. Das geschieht unabhängig vom übermittelten csrf_token, sogar beim exakten gespeicherten Wert: verify_cancel_csrf beendet sich mangels master_dash_session oder twitch_dash_session vorher mit false. Der entsprechende Kündigungs-POST landet ebenfalls bei cancel=csrf_invalid.
reachability_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/partner_login.rs:325-364: Der reguläre Einmal-Login erzeugt eine partner_token-Session und setzt ausschließlich twitch_dash_session_partner.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/level.rs:371-393 und 293-316: Die durable Session wird geprüft und für einen gewöhnlichen Partner als DashboardAuthLevel::Partner zurückgegeben.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1662-1678 und 2231: Kündigung und Promo-Formular sind im produktiven Router nativ registriert. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:476-524 verdrahtet diesen Router und den Session-State.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:335-348, 361-381 und 1008-1036: Beide Handler erreichen die gemeinsame Prüfung; diese kennt nur Admin- und kurzlebiges Partner-Cookie und weist den ausschließlich durablen Cookie deterministisch ab.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:28-31 und 361-396: Der Billing-Vertrag erlaubt eingeloggten Partnern die Verwaltung eigener Daten; der Promo-Handler verlangt Partner-Identität und gültiges CSRF, keine zusätzliche OAuth-Anmeldung.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:695-739: Auch durable Partner-Sessions erhalten ausdrücklich ein gespeichertes, sessiongebundenes csrf_token. Zusammen mit der identischen Partner-Einstufung belegt dies den vorgesehenen authentifizierten Nutzungspfad.

/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:1854-1899: Der vorhandene erfolgreiche Promo-Formtest belegt das Sollverhalten: passende Partner-Session und CSRF führen zur Speicherung und promo_saved=1. Er deckt nur die kurzlebige Session ab.
countermeasures: Fingerprint-, Ablauf- und Partnerprüfung schützen die durable Authentifizierung, ersetzen aber keine Cookie-Auswahl für CSRF: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:1878-1953.

Ein bloßes Umbenennen des durablen Cookies hilft nicht: Der Session-Lookup verlangt ausdrücklich den passenden session_type. Die Datenbank enthält eine einzelne Zeile je Session-ID, keine automatische Typabbildung: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:1993-2007; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:141-147 und 1784-1786.

Same-Origin- und Loopback-Fallbacks der Header-CSRF-Middleware reparieren die interne Formprüfung nicht. Der Billing-Router verwendet eigene Prüfungen: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1651-1704. Der Strangler ist nur Fallback für unbekannte Pfade, keine Reparaturschicht für diese nativen Routen.

Die aktuelle SPA bietet alternativ den Stripe-Kundenportal-Link an. Dieser GET-Pfad akzeptiert Partner ohne die betroffene Formprüfung und begrenzt deshalb den Kündigungsimpact: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/components/pricing/MySubscriptionCard.tsx:7-15 und 41-48; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:495-531.
gaps: Ausschließlich statische Prüfung am festen SHA; keine Tests, Builds, Datenbank-, Netzwerk- oder Browserprobes ausgeführt.

Kein aktueller SPA-Aufrufer der betroffenen Legacy-Form-POSTs gefunden. Ihre HTTP-Erreichbarkeit ist durch die produktive Routerverdrahtung belegt; eine vollständige Billing- oder Portal-Sperre wird ausdrücklich nicht behauptet.
Die vorhandenen Login- und Session-Tests belegen durable Ausstellung und Fingerprintprüfung, enthalten jedoch keine kombinierte Billing-Form-Regressionsprüfung mit ausschließlich durablem Cookie.

result.failure_scenario: An eligible partner completes a one-time login in a fresh browser. The server issues only twitch_dash_session_partner=S. Even when T equals the durable session's stored CSRF token, verify_cancel_csrf finds neither recognized cookie and returns false. The handler responds 403 csrf_token_invalid instead of saving. original_members.failure_scenario: A partner without an active manual override purchases annual Plus using a valid price ID supplied by the supported price map. The Stripe price has neither metadata.plan_id nor lookup_key. Checkout succeeds, and the webhook successfully retrieves the subscription. Because the checkout sends plan_id only as Checkout Session metadata, the retrieved subscription has no plan metadata. Its empty plan replaces the session's plus value, and the new subscription is recorded with a null plan_id. Plan resolution then returns raid_free despite the Plus purchase.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af ist der Fehler statisch belegt: Der Checkout setzt plan_id=plus ausschließlich an der Session. Erfolgreiches Nachladen der Subscription ersetzt diesen bekannten Plan ohne Plan-Fallback. Fehlt dort und am Preis die Plan-Metadata, wird ein leerer oder katalogüblicher Lookup-Key als Free behandelt. Das ist ein Korrektheitsfehler, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.
result.failure_scenario: Ein gültiger Partner ohne aktiven manuellen Plan kauft Plus jährlich über /twitch/abbo/bezahlen?plan_id=plus&cycle=12&quantity=1. Die unterstützte Preiszuordnung enthält plus/12 → price_plus_year. Dieser gültige wiederkehrende Stripe-Preis kostet 4990 Cent, hat metadata={} und lookup_key=deadlock_plus_12m_gross_v3. Der Checkout übermittelt Session-Metadata mit plan_id=plus, aber keine subscription_data.metadata. Nach erfolgreicher Zahlung liefert der signierte checkout.session.completed-Webhook die Session; das Nachladen der aktiven Subscription gelingt und liefert leere Subscription-Metadata. Der Parser übernimmt den Lookup-Key statt plus, verwirft den Session-Plan und behält lediglich die Kundenreferenz. Die Billing-Tabelle speichert den Lookup-Key als plan_id; streamer_plans wird mit plan_name=free geschrieben. Ohne gültigen manuellen Override liefert auch die effektive Planauflösung Free statt Plus.
expected_behavior_evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:114-135 definiert Plus als buchbaren kostenpflichtigen Plan mit 4990 Cent Jahrespreis und zusätzlichen Berechtigungen.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Livebereitschaft ohne konfigurierte Stripe-Preis-IDs.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Billing readiness reports live-ready even when no Stripe price IDs are configured.

original_members.claim: Billing readiness reports live-ready even when no Stripe price IDs are configured.
original_members.failure_scenario: The Stripe client and webhook secret are configured, but the price map is absent, malformed, or empty. GET /twitch/api/billing/readiness returns price_map_ready=true, integration_state=live, and ready_for_live=true. The catalog also reports payment.checkout_enabled=true. Every paid checkout nevertheless fails with missing_stripe_price_id because there are no default price IDs.
original_members.evidence: The primary file hardcodes price_map_ready=true at line 893 and derives live readiness from it at lines 896-900. Lines 919-924 use that result for catalog checkout_enabled, while lines 220-222 reject missing prices. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:166-172 explicitly defines PRICE_ID_DEFAULTS as empty; lines 465-472 turn missing or invalid mappings into an empty map, and lines 536-546 return no resolved price.
original_members.expected_behavior: The readiness field must reflect actual available price mappings. The primary file's own contract at lines 883-884 defines price_map_ready in terms of price coverage, and the catalog's payment-state function requires both checkout readiness and price-map readiness before enabling checkout.
original_members.countermeasures: Per-plan catalog availability and actual checkout independently check resolved prices, preventing an invalid purchase but not repairing the false readiness response. A matching hardcoded readiness result exists at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_stripe_sync.rs:335-358.

original_members.claim: Billing readiness reports live readiness even when no Stripe price is configured.
original_members.failure_scenario: The Stripe client and webhook secret are configured, but both price-map aliases are absent or contain invalid JSON. An authenticated GET to /twitch/api/billing/readiness returns price_map_ready=true, integration_state=live and ready_for_live=true. The catalog also advertises payment.checkout_enabled=true, although every paid checkout fails with missing_stripe_price_id.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, lines 885-900 hardcode price_map_ready=true and use it in the live/readiness flags; lines 916-924 propagate it into payment state. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:166-172 explicitly documents that price defaults are now empty. Its lines 465-472, 536-547 and 560-565 show that missing or invalid maps leave resolved_price_id returning None. The checkout handler rejects that state at lines 220-223.
original_members.expected_behavior: Price-map readiness must be false when no purchasable paid plan has a usable price mapping. In that state the service must not report ready_for_live=true or advertise checkout as enabled.
original_members.countermeasures: Per-plan catalog checks at lines 701-704 and the checkout guard at lines 220-223 prevent an actual purchase without a price. They do not correct the false readiness report. The existing readiness test at lines 1227-1234 only tests absent client configuration and still expects the obsolete unconditional price-map readiness.

claim.claim: Billing readiness reports live-ready even when no Stripe price IDs are configured.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af ist die Behauptung bestätigt. Das konstante price_map_ready=true beruht ausdrücklich auf angeblich vollständigen eingecheckten Preis-IDs. Tatsächlich ist diese Liste leer. Damit meldet die erreichbare Readiness-API volle Betriebsbereitschaft, obwohl kein kostenpflichtiger Checkout möglich ist. Die Kaufprüfungen begrenzen die Folgen, korrigieren aber nicht die falsche Statusauskunft. Keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.

findings.title_de: Vorschau meldet gesperrten Creator-Pro-Checkout bereit
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Vorschau meldet gesperrten Creator-Pro-Checkout bereit.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Checkout preview declares Creator Pro ready even though its checkout is explicitly disabled.

original_members.claim: Checkout preview declares Creator Pro ready even though its checkout is explicitly disabled.
original_members.failure_scenario: With a configured Stripe client and a pro price-map entry, an authenticated POST /twitch/api/billing/checkout-preview containing plan_id=pro and cycle_months=1 returns ready=true and the checkout-ready message. Following the actual checkout URL for that selection immediately redirects to pricing because Creator Pro is not bookable.
original_members.evidence: The primary file calculates checkout_possible at lines 812-814 using price, client readiness, and price ID only, ignoring selected_plan.buchbar. The actual checkout rejects !plan.buchbar at lines 205-209, and catalog availability includes buchbar at lines 701-703. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:137-162 defines pro with buchbar=false and lines 378-389 include that field in the preview's selected plan.
original_members.expected_behavior: The preview must report whether the selected plan can actually enter checkout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1692-1696 describes this endpoint as reporting checkout readiness; Creator Pro's catalog contract expressly keeps its checkout closed.
original_members.countermeasures: The catalog and frontend correctly hide Pro purchasing, and the actual checkout rejects it. These prevent a Pro sale but do not make the directly reachable preview result correct. The primary file's test price map at lines 1461-1463 already includes a pro price ID, so bookability cannot be inferred from price availability.

original_members.claim: Checkout preview reports unbookable Creator Pro as ready when a price mapping exists.
original_members.failure_scenario: With Stripe configured and valid Plus/Pro price mappings, an authenticated POST to /twitch/api/billing/checkout-preview with {"plan_id":"pro","cycle_months":1} returns ready=true and the checkout-ready message. Following the corresponding Pro checkout URL instead redirects to pricing without creating a session because Pro is not bookable.
original_members.evidence: Lines 783-799 select Pro from the catalog. Lines 801-819 derive readiness from its positive price and configured Stripe mapping, without checking buchbar. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:137-162 defines Pro with a 999-cent monthly price and buchbar=false; lines 374-389 include that flag in the selected catalog object. This file's lines 205-209 reject unbookable plans at checkout, and lines 699-704 suppress their catalog availability. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1692-1696 registers the preview specifically to report whether a plan is checkout-ready.
original_members.expected_behavior: A paid plan that checkout refuses because buchbar=false must also produce ready=false in checkout preview, regardless of whether its Stripe price is configured.
original_members.countermeasures: The checkout guard prevents selling Pro. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/components/pricing/PlanStufen.tsx:63-65 and 190-204 also suppress the purchase link. Those safeguards limit the impact to false preview success but do not fix the independently reachable API response. The existing preview tests cover Free, Plus, authentication and unknown IDs, not unbookable Pro.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The billing catalog silently reports an active paid user as Free when plan lookup fails.

original_members.claim: The billing catalog silently reports an active paid user as Free when plan lookup fails.
original_members.failure_scenario: A partner with an active Plus subscription has already authenticated, but the subsequent plan lookup returns a database error, such as a connection failure during its SELECT. The catalog converts that error into a successful Free snapshot. The pricing page consequently hides subscription management and shows a Plus purchase link instead of the current-plan marker, despite the existing paid subscription.
original_members.evidence: Lines 666-678 discard the lookup error and construct default_basic; lines 687 and 711-719 publish that fallback as actual subscription data. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:306-318 defines that snapshot as raid_free/default_basic, and lines 409-431 propagate SELECT errors to the caller. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/pages/Pricing.tsx:69-85 conditionally hides management using the returned subscription. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/components/pricing/PlanStufen.tsx:186-200 replaces the current-plan marker with a purchase link when is_current is false.
original_members.expected_behavior: Subscription lookup failure should remain distinguishable from a confirmed Free subscription so that the UI does not present inaccurate billing status or a duplicate purchase invitation. Class C because lines 669-670 explicitly prescribe the Free fail-safe; changing that fallback needs a decision about the intended unavailable-state response.
original_members.countermeasures: The authentication gate prevents unauthenticated access but does not address a lookup failure after authentication. The response contains no lookup-error indication, and the UI trusts the supplied status. The existing current-plan test at lines 2005-2018 verifies that a successfully resolved paid subscription suppresses another purchase, but does not cover database failure. No actual subscription downgrade occurs in this handler.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af erzeugt jeder gültige Checkout-Aufruf eine neue Subscription-Checkout-Session ohne Idempotency-Key, Abo-Prüfung oder gemeinsam gespeicherte Reservierung. Werden beide hosted Checkouts abgeschlossen, bleiben zwei unabhängig abrechenbare Abos möglich. Das widerspricht dem ausdrücklich getesteten Verbot eines erneuten Kaufs derselben bezahlten Stufe. Keine belegte Sicherheitslücke: Die GET-Aufrufe allein bewirken noch keine Zahlung.
result.failure_scenario: Ein authentifizierter Partner ohne bestehendes Plus-Abo öffnet bei gültiger Stripe-Konfiguration und hinterlegtem Plus-Jahrespreis gleichzeitig in zwei Tabs /twitch/abbo/bezahlen?plan_id=plus&cycle=12&quantity=1. Beide Handler senden POST /v1/checkout/sessions mit mode=subscription, derselben Partnerreferenz und demselben Preis, aber ohne Idempotency-Key. Beide erhalten eigene Checkout-URLs. Der Partner schließt beide Stripe-Checkouts ab. Der Jahreszyklus setzt keinen Trial. original_members.claim: A delayed cancellation response can overwrite a newer canceled subscription with active status.
original_members.failure_scenario: The customer portal fails, so the fallback requests cancel_at_period_end. Stripe computes an active subscription response, but its delivery is delayed. The subscription is then immediately canceled in Stripe, and its signed deletion webhook commits canceled status. The delayed fallback response subsequently persists active status, restoring the paid plan locally even though Stripe has canceled it.

claim.claim: A delayed cancellation response can overwrite a newer canceled subscription with active status.

result.reason: The cancellation fallback writes an earlier Stripe response without checking whether a newer subscription event has already committed. Its UPSERT unconditionally replaces status, including canceled with active. This is a reachable correctness bug, not merely the legitimate active status of a cancellation scheduled for period end. All source evidence was read at SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
result.failure_scenario: An authenticated partner submits a valid cancellation POST shortly before the subscription period ends. The local subscription has no customer ID, so the handler uses its documented direct fallback. Stripe schedules cancellation and produces a response containing the same subscription ID, status=active and cancel_at_period_end=true. While that response is delayed, the period ends and a valid customer.subscription.deleted webhook commits status=canceled. The delayed response then reaches persist_cancelled_subscription, which overwrites the already canceled row with active and replaces last_event_id with dashboard_cancel_fallback:<subscription_id>. With customer_reference and plan_id present, its subsequent plan sync also changes the partner's plan back from free to the paid plan. This ordering can occur within the client's 25-second timeout.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af ist ein konkreter Zustandsrückschritt belegbar. Der Kündigungs-Fallback übernimmt die Stripe-Antwort unverändert und schreibt deren nichtleeren Status ohne Aktualitätsprüfung über den inzwischen gespeicherten Status derselben Subscription-ID. Ein bereits verarbeitetes canceled wird dadurch wieder active. Das ist ein Korrektheitsfehler, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.
result.failure_scenario: Bei konfiguriertem Billing und Webhook sendet ein angemeldeter Partner einen gültigen Kündigungs-POST. Die Portal-Erstellung scheitert, deshalb wird cancel_at_period_end=true direkt gesetzt. Stripe verarbeitet das kurz vor dem Periodenende und erzeugt eine Antwort mit id=sub_x, status=active und cancel_at_period_end=true. Während diese Antwort verzögert ankommt, endet die Subscription; der echte customer.subscription.deleted-Webhook mit derselben id und status=canceled wird verarbeitet und committed. Anschließend erreicht die ältere Antwort innerhalb des 25-Sekunden-Timeouts cancel_execute. persist_cancelled_subscription ruft apply_event auf; dessen UPSERT setzt status=active und ersetzt last_event_id durch dashboard_cancel_fallback:sub_x. Der neuere canceled-Zustand ist überschrieben. Unterschiedliche Subscription-IDs sind ausdrücklich nicht dieses Szenario.

claim.claim: A delayed post-commit cancellation sync can undo a newer webhook's free plan mirror.

result.reason: The claimed race is reachable for supported subscriptions with populated customer_reference metadata. Cancellation commits the older subscription state, then independently mirrors its original response without checking the now-current billing row. A newer canceled webhook can therefore commit free first and subsequently be overwritten by the older active mirror. This violates the documented and tested mirror contract. No security bypass is established.
result.failure_scenario: An active partner login2, user ID 7, has a supported raid_boost subscription with metadata.customer_reference=login2. An authenticated, CSRF-valid cancellation POST reaches the fallback because the billing portal is unavailable. Stripe returns status=active and cancel_at_period_end=true shortly before the period ends. Request A commits that response at billing_page.rs:1146 but is delayed before its separate mirror transaction. A newer, correctly signed customer.subscription.deleted event B with status=canceled updates the same subscription and commits its streamer_plans mirror as free. A resumes and unconditionally writes raid_boost with expires_at=NULL from its older response. The authoritative subscription remains canceled with B's last_event_id, but its mirror is paid again. No further event is required to arrive and repair it.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A concurrent thin invoice update can erase billing-period changes saved by the cancellation fallback.

original_members.claim: A concurrent thin invoice update can erase billing-period changes saved by the cancellation fallback.
original_members.failure_scenario: The local subscription still has the previous billing period. After renewal, the fallback receives a full Stripe snapshot with the new period and writes it in its transaction. Before that transaction commits, a payment webhook reads the old committed row and builds a thin merged state, then waits at its UPSERT. Once cancellation commits, the invoice UPSERT proceeds and replaces the new current_period_end with its cached old value. The catalog subsequently reports the old expiration date.
original_members.evidence: billing_page.rs:1136-1146 invokes the shared merge within a transaction. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/webhook_apply.rs:343-355 reads the existing row without a row lock; lines 404-411 fill absent period fields from that snapshot; lines 429-442 overwrite current_period_start and current_period_end from EXCLUDED. Invoice events at lines 736-771 omit those fields and reach the same helper. The existing concurrency test at lines 1348-1434 demonstrates the old-read/blocked-UPSERT interleaving, but asserts preservation only of the cancellation flag. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:538-595 uses the resulting period_end as expires_at.
original_members.expected_behavior: Thin invoice events must preserve subscription fields they do not carry. This is the explicit merge contract at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/webhook_apply.rs:328-333, including when another transaction updates those fields concurrently.
original_members.countermeasures: The SQL specifically preserves a concurrently changed cancel_at_period_end using COALESCE($15, twitch_billing_subscriptions.cancel_at_period_end). Equivalent protection is absent for period fields and other snapshot-merged columns. A transaction does not make an unlocked read followed by an UPSERT an atomic merge under the demonstrated PostgreSQL interleaving. The signed webhook and event-ID dedup guards do not prevent distinct valid events from racing.

claim.claim: A concurrent thin invoice update can erase billing-period changes saved by the cancellation fallback.

result.reason: Confirmed at SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The cancellation fallback and invoice webhook share an unlocked read-merge-write helper. Period values copied from the invoice's earlier SELECT are later assigned unconditionally through EXCLUDED, overwriting periods committed by the fallback. The existing cancellation-flag protection does not protect either period column. This violates the explicit thin-event preservation contract, rather than exposing a demonstrated security vulnerability.
result.failure_scenario: With default READ COMMITTED isolation and two connections, sub_x initially has a valid customer_reference but NULL period columns. This state is reachable when checkout subscription retrieval fails. An authenticated cancellation POST passes CSRF, portal creation fails, and the successful direct-cancellation response contains current_period_start=S, current_period_end=E and cancel_at_period_end=true. The fallback UPSERT writes S/E but has not committed. A distinct, correctly signed invoice.payment_failed event for sub_x reads the previously committed NULL periods through the unlocked SELECT, then waits at its UPSERT. The fallback commits. The invoice resumes and assigns its precomputed NULL values to both period columns, then commits successfully. S/E have been erased, while cancel_at_period_end correctly remains 1.

findings.title_de: Kundenlookup ohne eigene SQL-Ausführungsfrist
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Kundenlookup ohne eigene SQL-Ausführungsfrist.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The billing customer lookup has no application-enforced SQL execution deadline.

original_members.claim: The billing customer lookup has no application-enforced SQL execution deadline.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, a maintenance transaction retains an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_billing_subscriptions. Authenticated invoice-link requests reach active_customer_record and wait indefinitely while retaining checked-out connections. Keeping enough requests open to fill the shared dashboard pool prevents other requests, including session lookups, from acquiring connections. They then fail after the acquisition timeout until the blocking transaction ends.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, billing_page.rs:495-508 reaches the SELECT at 1095-1118 without a timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 and 476-483 supplies the shared pool built by tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 limits connection acquisition but sets statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, which this dashboard startup does not call. The billing router and global layers at tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1651-1704 and 2204-2271 add no request deadline. Related unbounded SQL awaits were also checked at billing_page.rs:1069-1070 and 1136-1146; the latter reaches webhook_apply.rs:423-460.
original_members.expected_behavior: A blocked billing lookup should eventually fail and release its database connection instead of exhausting the shared dashboard pool. No specific SQL execution deadline is established by the reviewed contract, and an operational PostgreSQL timeout could already provide the bound, so this is a C recommendation rather than a confirmed A/B defect.
original_members.countermeasures: Authentication restricts access and LIMIT 1 bounds returned rows. Pool size and acquisition timeout bound connection creation and acquisition waits, not statements already executing. connect_readonly installs a 20-second statement timeout, but the reviewed startup uses connect. Stripe calls have a 25-second client timeout, so missing Stripe deadlines were ruled out. PostgreSQL role/database/DSN timeout settings or a deployment-level request deadline may mitigate this scenario; those settings were not verified.

original_members.failure_scenario: Partner A saves their name, email, address and VAT ID under login alpha, then renames their Twitch account. Later, independent partner B acquires alpha and authenticates using B's own verified Twitch ID. GET /twitch/api/billing/catalog returns A's persisted billing_profile to B. B can also submit their own valid CSRF token to POST /twitch/abbo/rechnungsdaten and overwrite A's row.
original_members.evidence: The assigned file chooses twitch_login before twitch_user_id at lines 368-385, loads solely by LOWER(customer_reference) at 184-211, and upserts on customer_reference at 141-167. The reachable catalog caller in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:643-655 permits authenticated partners; lines 736-744 return resolve_profile output. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260617010000_tb_dashboard_api_billing_profiles.sql:12-23 contains no owner ID. The rename implementation in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/streamer_login.rs:58-163,294-395 does not update billing profiles. A targeted Rust occurrence search found no additional production profile writer or cleanup.
original_members.expected_behavior: Billing details must remain private to the original account, not transfer with its reusable login. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:1410-1437 explicitly establishes authenticated Twitch ID as identity and states that reassigned logins are not identity.
original_members.countermeasures: Session authentication correctly verifies B's ID and partner membership. Form CSRF validation is fail-closed and SQL is parameterized. Neither binds the selected billing row to that ID, so both protections pass for B's legitimate session. Historical ownership repair may need a separately scoped migration; this review authorizes no such change.

result.reason: Die stabile Twitch-ID schützt die Anmeldung, nicht die Rechnungsprofile. Diese werden ausschließlich anhand des wiedervergebbaren Logins gelesen und überschrieben. Ein unabhängig freigegebener Partner kann damit personenbezogene Rechnungsdaten eines anderen Kontoinhabers erhalten. Statischer Nachweis am SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
result.failure_scenario: Partner A (ID 111, Login recycled) speichert sein Rechnungsprofil. A wechselt zu first_new. Die normale Umbenennung aktualisiert seine Partnerzeile, lässt das Rechnungsprofil recycled bestehen. Der bereits eigenständig freigegebene Partner B (ID 222) erhält später recycled und wird ebenfalls abgeglichen. B meldet sich regulär mit seiner eigenen ID an. GET /twitch/api/v2/billing/catalog liefert As Name, E-Mail und Anschrift als billing_profile. B liest seinen eigenen CSRF-Wert über auth-status und sendet vollständige Rechnungsfelder an POST /twitch/abbo/rechnungsdaten. Der Upsert überschreibt dieselbe Profilzeile recycled.

result.failure_scenario: Partner A (Twitch ID 111, login recycled) saves a billing profile with their name, email and address. A renames to former_owner. Later, existing partner B (ID 222) acquires recycled. Normal monitoring reconciliation updates both partner logins but leaves the billing row keyed recycled unchanged. B signs in legitimately with their own Twitch account. GET /twitch/api/v2/billing/catalog returns A's persisted billing_profile. B obtains their own csrf_token from /twitch/api/v2/auth-status and submits a valid POST /twitch/abbo/rechnungsdaten. original_members.failure_scenario: Partner A has completed stream sessions and monetization events recorded as alpha, then renames. After alpha becomes available, partner B acquires it and legitimately obtains an active Plus plan. B requests /twitch/api/v2/monetization?days=3650 without supplying streamer. Historical A sessions within that permitted window contribute their ads, bits, subscription and hype-train data to B's response.
original_members.evidence: The handler passes only the resolved login string to load_monetization_payload at lines 44-55. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/streamer_scope.rs:136-163 validates B's ID but returns only B's current login. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-analytics/src/monetization.rs:634-749 filters each monetization query by LOWER(s.streamer_login), never the session owner's Twitch ID; lines 148-163 use the same filter for detailed ad rows. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/streamer_login.rs:359-374 deliberately renames only open sessions, preserving completed sessions under their original login. The endpoint is registered at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:879-882.
original_members.expected_behavior: A partner must receive only their own account's monetization records. The assigned handler's ownership contract at lines 42-43 and cross-account rejection test at 166-184 explicitly prohibit access to another streamer.
original_members.countermeasures: The outer partner-status gate, Plus-plan gate and explicit foreign-streamer rejection protect ordinary requests. B is an active entitled partner requesting their own current login, so all pass. Parameterized SQL prevents injection but not ownership collisions in historical login values. resolved_candidate_group.claim: Stripe product synchronization lacks server-side Origin and CSRF checks for cookie-authenticated form POSTs.

original_members.claim: Stripe product synchronization lacks server-side Origin and CSRF checks for cookie-authenticated form POSTs.
original_members.failure_scenario: Conditional scenario: an administrator with admin mode active visits hostile HTML on a different HTTPS origin under the same registrable domain. That page submits a simple form POST with dry_run=0 to /twitch/api/billing/stripe/sync-products. SameSite=Lax permits same-site cookies; with Stripe configured and products not yet provisioned, the handler creates Stripe objects without checking the initiating origin or a CSRF token. Control of such a sibling origin was not established during this read-only review.
original_members.evidence: The handler checks only is_privileged at lines 64-70 and accepts form bodies at 378-395. Product and price creation occurs at 145-157 and 239-254. Its route is in the unlayered billing router at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1651-1704, merged separately at 2230-2231. Global layers at 2245-2271 provide auditing, tracing and compression, not CSRF. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/discord_admin_login.rs:920-935 sets SameSite=Lax. The existing write middleware checks Origin before accepting a session at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/csrf.rs:89-140, but is not attached here.
original_members.expected_behavior: Cookie-authenticated Stripe mutations should enforce the existing server-side browser-origin protection used for other dashboard writes, rather than rely solely on the admin role and SameSite cookies.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication prevents anonymous calls, and explicit SameSite=Lax blocks ordinary cross-site form POSTs. The remaining scenario needs a hostile same-site origin, which is unverified; consequently this is C, not a confirmed exploitable vulnerability. No network, browser or production configuration probes were performed.
