findings.title_de: Webhook bestätigt Provisions-DB-Fehler mit HTTP 200
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Webhook bestätigt Provisions-DB-Fehler mit HTTP 200.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The Stripe webhook acknowledges commission database failures with HTTP 200 even when no commission was recorded.

original_members.claim: The Stripe webhook acknowledges commission database failures with HTTP 200 even when no commission was recorded.
original_members.failure_scenario: A valid invoice.payment_succeeded event belongs to a streamer with an eligible affiliate claim. The billing transaction commits, then a transient database error occurs before process_commission inserts its ledger row. The error is only logged; process_event returns Ok and the handler responds 200 processed. Stripe receives a successful acknowledgement despite the missing commission and therefore need not retry this delivery.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, billing_webhook.rs:240 commits billing state; :297-305 discards the commission error; :310 returns success; :174-184 maps that success to HTTP 200. Context rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_commission.rs:237-257 can return a database error before ledger insertion, which starts at :333-338.
original_members.expected_behavior: A paid invoice must durably record its eligible affiliate commission or retain a retryable failure. This financial obligation is stated in affiliate_commission.rs:6-18 and exercised by billing_webhook.rs:786-820.
original_members.countermeasures: Billing-event duplicates deliberately revisit process_commission (:280-285), and :869-933 tests recovery when a replay is supplied. That does not cause replay after a 200 acknowledgement. The pending-commission recovery query in affiliate_commission.rs:502-515 only sees existing ledger rows, so it cannot recover a commission that was never inserted.

original_members.claim: The Stripe webhook acknowledges commission persistence failures with HTTP 200, permanently losing unrecorded commissions.
original_members.failure_scenario: A valid invoice.payment_succeeded event belongs to an eligible affiliate. The billing transaction commits, but a transient database connection failure or statement cancellation occurs inside process_commission before its commission ledger transaction commits. The handler logs the error and returns HTTP 200 with ok=true. Stripe consequently has no failed delivery to retry, no commission row exists, and later pending-commission replay cannot recover this payment.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, billing_webhook.rs:240 commits the billing event; :297-305 discards process_commission errors; :310 returns Ok; :174-184 turns that into HTTP 200. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_commission.rs:237-257, :325-338 and :373-417, database errors propagate before a durable commission row is guaranteed. Its :502-519 replay query only selects existing pending/failed commission rows. Targeted fixed-SHA caller searches found no production reconstruction of missing commissions from twitch_billing_events.
original_members.expected_behavior: An eligible paid invoice must durably record its commission or remain recoverable through failed-delivery retry. The commission module documents ledger persistence before payout at affiliate_commission.rs:6-18 and :333-336. The webhook explicitly supports recovery after billing commit at billing_webhook.rs:280-285, and its existing duplicate-event recovery test at :870-934 establishes that reprocessing an already recorded billing event can reconstruct a missing commission. The existing outer error path at :185-192 supplies HTTP 500 for processing failures.
original_members.countermeasures: Signature validation and transactional billing deduplication were checked; neither guarantees commission persistence. Affiliate advisory locks, the unique stripe_event_id, durable pending rows, and replay-on-duplicate prevent double payment and recover already persisted rows. They also make a subsequent webhook retry safe, but cannot recover an absent ledger row after this successful acknowledgement. This finding concerns failures before durable commission insertion, not intentionally deferred payouts without a Stripe Connect account.

result.reason: Die Behauptung hält der Gegenprüfung am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af stand. Auch Fehler vor dem ersten Commission-Schreibvorgang werden nur geloggt; anschließend meldet der Handler HTTP 200 und ok=true. Die getrennte Billing-Transaktion ist beabsichtigt, ein Verlust berechtigter Provisionen jedoch nicht durch den belegten Produktvertrag gedeckt. Die vorhandene Wiederherstellung benötigt eine erneute Event-Zustellung.
result.failure_scenario: Ein korrekt signiertes, neues invoice.payment_succeeded über 1000 Cent betrifft einen Streamer mit gültigem Affiliate-Claim, 30 Prozent Provision und weniger als 50 Euro offenen Provisionen. Für diese Event-ID existiert noch keine Commission. Billing-Event und Subscription werden erfolgreich committed. Danach verursacht eine vorübergehende PostgreSQL-Unterbrechung einen SQLx-Fehler beim ersten Commission-SELECT. process_commission beendet sich vor jedem Ledger-INSERT. process_event loggt den Fehler, gibt trotzdem Ok zurück und der Handler antwortet HTTP 200 mit status=processed. Die erwarteten 300 Cent fehlen; die Antwort fordert keinen Stripe-Retry an.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Billing-profile saves reject the authenticated partner's valid CSRF token when a master-session cookie is also present.

original_members.claim: Billing-profile saves reject the authenticated partner's valid CSRF token when a master-session cookie is also present.
original_members.failure_scenario: A browser sends a valid twitch_dash_session and a master_dash_session cookie to the public billing route. Public authentication selects the partner session, and auth-status returns its CSRF token. Submitting a complete billing profile with that token nevertheless selects the master cookie for verification, so the request redirects with profile=error and saves nothing. An expired master cookie produces the same failure.
original_members.evidence: billing_profile.rs:430-441 unconditionally prefers a nonempty admin cookie and validates it as discord_admin. Context rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/level.rs:346-368 selects the partner first for public requests. handlers/auth_status.rs:94-100 returns the selected partner session's token. auth/session.rs:1537-1556 rejects a different session's token or an expired session.
original_members.expected_behavior: A valid form token must be checked against the session that authenticated that form submission. auth_status.rs:94-100 already follows that selected-session contract.
original_members.countermeasures: The authentication extractor stores AuthenticatedPartnerSessionId, but this verifier does not consume it and does not fall back after master-cookie validation fails. lib.rs:1670-1675 registers the form route without an outer header-CSRF layer that could correct session selection. A targeted twin exists in handlers/billing_page.rs:1025-1036 for cancellation.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af belegt: Die öffentliche Authentifizierung und die CSRF-Ausgabe wählen die Partner-Session, aber der Billing-Handler prüft bei vorhandenem Master-Cookie ausschließlich dessen Session. Selbst ein ungültiges Master-Cookie verhindert dadurch das Speichern. Das ist ein funktionaler Fehler, keine belegte Sicherheitslücke.
result.failure_scenario: Ein angemeldeter Partner besitzt eine gültige twitch_dash_session=P mit CSRF-Wert TP und zusätzlich master_dash_session=stale, für das keine gültige DB-Session existiert. GET /twitch/api/v2/auth-status liefert TP. Ein gleichursprünglicher POST /twitch/abbo/rechnungsdaten mit csrf_token=TP, cycle=1 und vollständig ausgefüllten Pflichtfeldern authentifiziert weiterhin P. verify_form_csrf wählt jedoch stale/discord_admin, erhält false und leitet auf /twitch/pricing?cycle=1&profile=error um. upsert_profile wird nicht erreicht; das Rechnungsprofil bleibt unverändert.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Repeated live Stripe synchronization creates new products while reusing prices belonging to the previous products.

original_members.claim: Repeated live Stripe synchronization creates new products while reusing prices belonging to the previous products.
original_members.failure_scenario: Run live sync twice against the same Stripe account. The first invocation creates a Plus product and its two lookup-key prices. The second invocation creates another Plus product, then reuses the existing prices through their lookup keys. Its product_id_map and operations.product.id identify the new product, while the reported price IDs still belong to the first product. Supplying an existing runtime product map also does not prevent recreation.
original_members.evidence: Context rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:166-176 defines both default-ID arrays as empty. billing_stripe_sync.rs:123 therefore starts with no product ID and :145-171 always creates one in live mode. Existing prices are separately reused at :217-230; the unrelated product and prices are reported at :174-175 and :289-297. stripe/client.rs:246-249 creates products without an idempotency key.
original_members.expected_behavior: Synchronization must reuse existing plan products and return product/price mappings that describe matching Stripe objects. The endpoint's create-or-reuse contract is documented at billing_stripe_sync.rs:3-4; catalog.rs:549-573 already provides runtime product mapping and effective product-ID resolution.
original_members.countermeasures: Product verification only runs for checked-in defaults, which are empty at the review SHA. The handler neither consumes product_id_map_from_env nor derives the existing product from a reused price. Active-price lookup prevents duplicate prices, but not duplicate products or mismatched reported mappings.

original_members.claim: Repeated Stripe catalog synchronization creates duplicate products and mismatched product/price maps.
original_members.failure_scenario: Run a successful live catalog synchronization twice without changing the catalog. On the second run, the handler creates new Plus and Pro products again, then reuses the first run's prices through their lookup keys. It reports the newly created product IDs alongside price IDs attached to the previous products, leaving redundant products in Stripe. Concurrent runs also independently create products before attempting price lookup/create.
original_members.evidence: Product reuse checks only product_id_default at lines 123-144 before creating at lines 145-157. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/billing/catalog.rs:172-176 defines both default-ID tables as empty, so product reuse is unreachable for the current catalog. Price lookup at handler lines 217-229 reuses existing prices without obtaining their product. Response maps are assembled at lines 174-175 and 272-315. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/client.rs:246-249 creates products without an idempotency key or explicit stable product ID.
original_members.expected_behavior: The synchronization endpoint promises to create or reuse each plan's product and prices, as documented at lines 3-5. An unchanged repeated synchronization should reuse the existing products and report product IDs corresponding to its prices.
original_members.countermeasures: Admin authentication restricts callers but does not make repeated operations idempotent. Price lookup keys protect price reuse only, not product creation. The handler neither reads runtime product-ID overrides nor persists its generated IDs; the response explicitly confirms no persistence. The same creation path applies independently to both paid plans.

The second invocation creates another Plus product, then reuses the existing prices through their lookup keys. Its product_id_map and operations.product.id identify the new product, while the reported price IDs still belong to the first product. Supplying an existing runtime product map also does not prevent recreation.

The endpoint's create-or-reuse contract is documented at billing_stripe_sync.rs:3-4; catalog.rs:549-573 already provides runtime product mapping and effective product-ID resolution.

original_members.claim: Stripe synchronization reports price_map_ready and ready_for_live even when no usable price mapping exists.
original_members.failure_scenario: Configure a Stripe client and webhook signing secret, leave the runtime price map absent, and submit an admin dry-run sync. No objects are created and both returned ID maps are empty, yet readiness reports price_map_ready=true and ready_for_live=true. Attempting the actual Plus checkout then fails with missing_stripe_price_id.
original_members.evidence: billing_stripe_sync.rs:341-358 hardcodes price_map_ready=true. Its dry-run test at :473-476 explicitly asserts empty maps because defaults no longer exist. Context billing/catalog.rs:166-176 confirms empty defaults, and :536-546 resolves prices only through those defaults or the runtime map. handlers/billing_page.rs:220-223 rejects checkout without a resolved price.
original_members.expected_behavior: price_map_ready must reflect whether the required prices can actually be resolved; ready_for_live must not claim readiness while checkout has no usable price ID. This dependency is stated at billing_stripe_sync.rs:338-340 and enforced by the checkout path.
original_members.countermeasures: The admin gate and dry-run guard restrict writes but do not validate readiness. Returning would_create operations does not supply a usable runtime mapping. A targeted twin hardcodes the same readiness value in handlers/billing_page.rs:885-900. The documented lack of runtime-vault persistence is not itself reported as a new defect; this finding concerns the false readiness result.

findings.title_de: Checkout-Wiederholung stellt alte Jahresbonusmonate nicht wieder her
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Checkout-Wiederholung stellt alte Jahresbonusmonate nicht wieder her.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Failed checkout side effects cannot recover grandfathered annual bonus months on webhook replay.

original_members.claim: Failed checkout side effects cannot recover grandfathered annual bonus months on webhook replay.
original_members.failure_scenario: A supported legacy subscription has bonus_months=2 and a valid period end, with no existing manual bonus grant. During checkout.session.completed, either subscription retrieval temporarily fails or the post-commit streamer_plans transaction fails. The event is nevertheless committed and acknowledged. Replaying the same checkout after recovery successfully retrieves the subscription but skips the entire plan/bonus sync because is_new is false. Later subscription events also carry zero bonus months into that sync, so they do not restore the missing bonus.
original_members.evidence: billing_webhook.rs:212-240 retrieves and commits before side effects; :244 gates plan sync on is_new; :248-258 logs and ignores sync failures. Its :393-398 converts subscription retrieval errors into None. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/webhook_apply.rs:290-299, only the retrieved checkout subscription supplies bonus_months; :311-323 assigns zero bonus for ordinary subscription events; :536-545 grants the bonus in the separate sync transaction. The same file's :1514-1565 test establishes the intended period_end plus 62 days for bonus_months=2.
original_members.expected_behavior: Grandfathered subscriptions are documented to retain their bonus in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_page.rs:266-273 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/docs/internal/stripe-webhooks-internal.md:30-39. However, billing_webhook.rs:242-243 explicitly makes plan-sync errors best-effort without Stripe retry. No recovery contract reconciles those requirements, so choosing a recovery mechanism remains C rather than an automatically authorized behavior change.
original_members.countermeasures: The core subscription transaction is atomic and normal entitlement resolution reads the durable subscription directly through /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/plan.rs:496-545. Thus this is not a claim that every failed plan sync immediately removes paid access. The lost benefit is the manual bonus override, which is absent from the subscription ledger. The duplicate recovery added for affiliate commissions at billing_webhook.rs:280-307 does not cover plan or bonus synchronization. New checkouts no longer create bonus metadata; the finding is limited to the explicitly preserved legacy path.

findings.title_de: Dünner Invoice-Upsert überschreibt parallelen Aboplan
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Dünner Invoice-Upsert überschreibt parallelen Aboplan.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Thin invoice upserts can overwrite concurrently updated subscription plan and period fields.

original_members.claim: Thin invoice upserts can overwrite concurrently updated subscription plan and period fields.
original_members.failure_scenario: A subscription update changes an existing subscription from Plus/P1 to Pro/P2 and holds its row lock before committing. Concurrent invoice.payment_succeeded reads the previously committed Plus/P1 state without locking, then waits at its UPSERT. Once the subscription update commits, the invoice UPSERT writes its stale merged Plus/P1 values over Pro/P2, although the invoice supplies neither plan nor period. Both events are acknowledged successfully.
original_members.evidence: The assigned webhook handler calls apply_event inside independent transactions at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_webhook.rs:215-240. The dependency reads existing values without FOR UPDATE at lines 343-354, merges missing fields in Rust, and unconditionally writes EXCLUDED.plan_id and EXCLUDED.current_period_start/end at lines 429-440. Both invoice success and failure reach this helper at lines 748 and 771.
original_members.expected_behavior: Thin invoice events must preserve subscription fields they do not contain. This is explicitly documented at lines 328-333 and tested by invoice_failed_sets_past_due_without_overwriting_plan at lines 1264-1299 of the identified dependency.
original_members.countermeasures: The subscription primary key prevents duplicate rows, not stale merged writes. Event-ID deduplication does not serialize distinct events. The existing SQL COALESCE protection and parallel regression test preserve cancel_at_period_end only; plan, period, customer reference, quantity and other merged fields lack equivalent protection. The pool builder does not establish serializable isolation.

Das widerspricht dem ausdrücklich dokumentierten Erhalt vollständiger Abo-Daten durch dünne Rechnungsereignisse; eine Sicherheitslücke ist damit nicht belegt.
result.failure_scenario: Konfiguration mit mindestens zwei PostgreSQL-Verbindungen und READ COMMITTED, gültige Signaturen und unterschiedliche Ereignis-IDs. Anfangs enthält sub_x plan_id=plus und Zeitraum P0. Ein customer.subscription.updated für sub_x schreibt pro und Zeitraum P1, hat aber noch nicht committet. Parallel verarbeitet der andere Handler invoice.payment_succeeded für sub_x. Sein SELECT sieht über MVCC weiterhin plus/P0; die Rechnung enthält selbst weder Plan noch Zeitraum, deshalb werden plus/P0 als Fallback gebunden. Ihr UPSERT wartet auf die Subscription-Transaktion. Nach deren Commit setzt er plan_id und current_period_start/end auf die alten EXCLUDED-Werte zurück und committet erfolgreich. Endzustand ist plus/P0 statt pro/P1. Ohne manuellen Override liest der Plan-Resolver anschließend diese falschen Werte. Beide Ereignisse bleiben als verarbeitet gespeichert; deren Wiederholung wendet den neueren Subscription-Zustand nicht erneut an.

original_members.claim: Post-commit webhook plan synchronization can restore a paid plan after cancellation.
original_members.failure_scenario: Handler A commits an active subscription event, then pauses before its plan synchronization. Handler B commits a later cancellation for the same subscription and synchronizes streamer_plans to free. A resumes and synchronizes its retained active event payload, overwriting free with the paid plan. The final subscription row is canceled while its mirrored plan remains paid.
original_members.evidence: Lines 240-248 commit the subscription transaction before deriving and applying the plan update from the original event object. At /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/webhook_apply.rs:305-324 the synchronization payload contains no event/version identifier, and lines 506-518 overwrite streamer_plans unconditionally in a separate transaction.
original_members.expected_behavior: The mirrored plan must match the committed subscription state. The dependency documents this mirror at lines 9-12 and explicitly tests cancellation setting the plan to free at lines 1110-1161.
original_members.countermeasures: The two transactions separately provide atomic writes but do not preserve their combined ordering. Neither synchronization checks the subscription's current last_event_id. Distinct event IDs bypass deduplication independently. Subsequent duplicate deliveries skip plan synchronization, so replaying either event does not repair this mismatch. Checkout events use the same post-commit path.

result.reason: Am festen SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af ist eine konkrete Race belegt: Die Subscription-Transaktionen können korrekt geordnet sein, während ihre nachgelagerten Plan-Synchronisierungen umgekehrt schreiben. Dadurch wird nach endgültiger Kündigung der bezahlte Plan in streamer_plans wiederhergestellt, einschließlich des daraus abgeleiteten Raid-Vorrangs. Kein Nachweis einer allgemeinen Wiederfreischaltung aller Dashboard-Funktionen.
result.failure_scenario: Ein aktiver Partner besitzt eine Subscription mit metadata.customer_reference für seinen Login und plan_id=raid_boost, ohne manuellen Plan oder eingeschalteten Boost. Zwei gültig signierte Events mit unterschiedlichen IDs treffen ein: E1 meldet active, E2 customer.subscription.deleted mit canceled. E1 schreibt und committet den aktiven Subscription-Zustand, wird aber vor seinem Plan-Sync unterbrochen. E2 schreibt und committet canceled, synchronisiert plan_name=free und beendet den Request. Anschließend synchronisiert E1 aus seiner unveränderten Event-Payload plan_name=raid_boost und expires_at=NULL. Der endgültige Zustand lautet deshalb: Subscription canceled, gespiegelter Plan raid_boost. Der anschließende Score-Refresh bewertet diesen Plan wieder als Raid-Vorrang. Es braucht weder falsche Signaturen noch eine umgekehrte Reihenfolge der Subscription-Commits.

findings.title_de: Frühe Rechnung verliert Affiliate-Provision dauerhaft
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Frühe Rechnung verliert Affiliate-Provision dauerhaft.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: An invoice webhook processed before its subscription mapping can permanently miss affiliate commission.

original_members.claim: An invoice webhook processed before its subscription mapping can permanently miss affiliate commission.
original_members.failure_scenario: An eligible affiliate has already claimed a streamer, but this is the streamer's first subscription for a new Stripe customer. Concurrent subscription and invoice.payment_succeeded webhooks arrive; the invoice completes before the full subscription event supplies customer_reference. Its thin subscription row has no streamer mapping, so commission processing returns NoStreamer and the webhook responds 200. The later subscription event fills the mapping but does not revisit the invoice. If the acknowledged invoice is not redelivered, its commission remains absent.
original_members.evidence: Invoice application at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/stripe/webhook_apply.rs:736-748 creates only subscription/customer/status fields. At /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_commission.rs:248-260, an empty customer_reference returns NoStreamer before any ledger insertion. The assigned handler treats every successful CommissionOutcome as success at lines 297-302 and acknowledges processing at lines 174-184.
original_members.expected_behavior: A paid invoice for an eligible claimed streamer must be recorded using the configured commission rate, irrespective of concurrent subscription delivery. This obligation is described at lines 6-18 of the commission module and exercised by invoice_payment_verbucht_affiliate_provision in the assigned handler.
original_members.countermeasures: The affiliate advisory lock is acquired only after streamer resolution and cannot protect the missing mapping. Duplicate invoice handling can recover if an external replay occurs, but the 200 response requests no retry. The inspected pending-commission replay reads existing ledger rows only, so it cannot recover a commission that was never inserted. Subscription events do not call process_commission.

result.reason: Eine gültige Zahlung kann mit HTTP 200 quittiert werden, obwohl die noch fehlende Streamer-Zuordnung jede Provisionsbuchung verhindert. Das spätere Eintragen der Zuordnung verarbeitet die Zahlung nicht erneut. Die Provision fehlt dadurch dauerhaft im normalen Ablauf, ist aber durch einen ausdrücklichen Invoice-Replay nachträglich reparierbar. Geprüfte Codebasis: 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
result.failure_scenario: Ein berechtigter Affiliate hat einen gültigen Claim für streamerx; claimed_at und partnered_at sind gleich, der Provisionssatz beträgt 30 %, die offene Provisionssumme ist 0. Für den neuen Stripe-Customer cus_new besteht noch keine Subscription-Zuordnung. Ein korrekt signiertes invoice.payment_succeeded mit subscription=sub_new und amount_paid=4990 wird vor checkout.session.completed verarbeitet. Der Invoice-Pfad legt einen dünnen Subscription-Datensatz ohne customer_reference an. process_commission liefert deshalb NoStreamer, ohne einen Provisionsdatensatz anzulegen; der Handler antwortet HTTP 200. Das anschließende Checkout-Event trägt customer_reference=streamerx ein, ruft jedoch keine Provisionsverarbeitung auf. Ohne erneute Zustellung des ursprünglichen Invoice-Events bleiben die geschuldeten 1497 Cent ungebucht, auch bei späteren Zahlungen oder beim Verbinden des Auszahlungskontos.

Seine Zuordnung wird vor dem Invoice-Eingang angelegt; die umgekehrte Reihenfolge wird dort nicht geprüft.
countermeasures: Signaturprüfung und fehlende Konfiguration verhindern ungültige Eingänge beziehungsweise liefern Fehler, erzwingen aber keine Reihenfolge zwischen gültigen Billing-Events: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_webhook.rs:93-134.

Ein erneuter Invoice-Eingang nach vollständiger Zuordnung kann die Provision tatsächlich nachholen, auch wenn das Billing-Event bereits dedupliziert ist. Das belegen /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/billing_webhook.rs:280-297 und der Recovery-Test bei Zeile 870-933. Dieser Schutz setzt eine zusätzliche Zustellung voraus; der erste Eingang hat bereits HTTP 200 geliefert.

Advisory-Lock, UNIQUE(stripe_event_id) und dauerhaftes Ledger schützen bereits angelegte Provisionen. Bei NoStreamer wird diese Phase nicht erreicht: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_commission.rs:258-260,333-417.

findings.title_de: Invoice-Webhook arbeitet gesamten offenen Transferbestand synchron ab
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Invoice-Webhook arbeitet gesamten offenen Transferbestand synchron ab.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Invoice webhooks synchronously replay the affiliate's entire pending-transfer backlog before acknowledging delivery.

original_members.claim: Invoice webhooks synchronously replay the affiliate's entire pending-transfer backlog before acknowledging delivery.
original_members.failure_scenario: An affiliate with a connected Stripe account has 100 pending commissions after an outage. A valid invoice.payment_succeeded callback arrives while transfer requests stall until their 25-second timeout. The callback attempts all 100 transfers sequentially, including after individual failures, and cannot acknowledge delivery for roughly 2,500 seconds. Throughout replay it retains a database transaction and affiliate advisory lock; concurrent callbacks for that affiliate can occupy additional pool connections waiting for the lock. Duplicate delivery enters the same backlog replay again.
original_members.evidence: billing_webhook.rs:174-194 returns the HTTP response only after process_event completes; :280-307 awaits process_commission even for duplicate billing events. affiliate_commission.rs:237-241 and :423 replay pending commissions for the whole affiliate. :476-492 holds one transaction and advisory lock throughout replay; :502-531 fetches every matching pending/failed commission without LIMIT and awaits each transfer. :593-615 records transfer failures as pending and returns Ok, so replay continues. stripe/client.rs:17,65-66 bounds each individual request to 25 seconds, not the complete webhook. Supporting sources were verified unchanged against review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
original_members.expected_behavior: The webhook's post-commit followups are described as best-effort operations intended to avoid Stripe retries (billing_webhook.rs:242-265), but acknowledgment here depends on an arbitrarily large backlog. A bounded acknowledgment/resource budget is needed while retaining durable, idempotent transfer recovery. No exact budget or batching/scheduling contract is established, and replaying all pending commissions is explicitly documented, so this is C rather than an automatic behavior-changing fix.
original_members.countermeasures: Signature verification restricts entry to valid callbacks. Event uniqueness, commission uniqueness and Stripe idempotency keys prevent duplicate financial effects, but do not bound replay work. The 25-second Stripe timeout applies separately to every transfer. The pending-sum cap at affiliate_commission.rs:351-370 applies only without a connected account, so it does not constrain this scenario. The duplicate-recovery test at billing_webhook.rs:869-934 intentionally requires transfer recovery on replay. No aggregate request deadline appears in the inspected router/server layers; the exact desired execution policy therefore needs a design decision.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Gutschriftenjob lässt fällige Perioden jenseits der ersten 100 liegen.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The recurring affiliate credit-note job permanently starves due periods beyond its first 100.

original_members.claim: The recurring affiliate credit-note job permanently starves due periods beyond its first 100.
original_members.failure_scenario: There are 101 distinct completed affiliate-month periods with transferred commissions and valid profiles. The background job generates the first 100. Every subsequent run selects those same 100 periods, even after their documents and emails are complete, so period 101 never receives a credit note automatically.
original_members.evidence: The unfiltered job always calls run_pending with limit 100 at line 203; the background entry point always takes this branch at 268-275. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_gutschrift.rs:571-638, due_periods reads all historical transferred commissions, sorts by year, month, and login, and run_pending takes the first limit entries without a cursor or exclusion of completed documents. generate_for_period at 779-815 returns existing completed documents without changing commission status. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:267-289 repeats this job every six hours.
original_members.expected_behavior: A bounded recurring pending-document job must eventually process every eligible due period, not repeatedly spend its entire batch on already completed periods.
original_members.countermeasures: Period locks and existing-document detection prevent duplicate documents, but neither advances the batch. Specifying an affiliate or explicit month manually bypasses the limit, which does not restore automatic progress. No schema migration is necessary to address batch selection.

original_members.claim: Automatic credit-document generation never advances beyond the first 100 historical affiliate periods.
original_members.failure_scenario: There are 101 distinct historical affiliate-month pairs with transferred commissions. The oldest 100 already have generated and emailed documents; the 101st still needs its document. Every scheduled run selects the same oldest 100, returns existing documents, and never processes the 101st. Newer periods remain starved indefinitely.
original_members.evidence: Verified against 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The primary handler passes limit=100 to run_pending. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_gutschrift.rs:571-641, due_periods selects all transferred commissions without excluding completed documents, sorts periods chronologically using BTreeSet, and run_pending always applies take(limit.max(1)) from the beginning. Lines 779-815 return existing completed documents without changing commission status. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:267-291 invokes this same handler every six hours without a continuation cursor.
original_members.expected_behavior: The recurring run_pending job must eventually process each eligible outstanding affiliate period. A batch limit may bound work per invocation, but completed historical periods must not permanently consume every batch slot.
original_members.countermeasures: The existing-document guard, advisory lock, and unique affiliate-period constraint prevent duplicate generation but do not advance selection. Explicit affiliate or month requests can bypass the starvation manually; the scheduled path cannot. The existing chronological-order test covers only the first limited invocation, not progress across repeated runs.

findings.title_de: OAuth-Login verhindert Migration vorhandener Klartextprofile
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: OAuth-Login verhindert Migration vorhandener Klartextprofile.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: OAuth login prevents existing plaintext affiliate profile data from being migrated.

original_members.claim: OAuth login prevents existing plaintext affiliate profile data from being migrated.
original_members.failure_scenario: An existing affiliate has name and address data in affiliate_accounts but no affiliate_pii row. Their next OAuth login returns a nonempty email. The callback creates an email-only affiliate_pii row. The subsequent portal profile request skips migration and returns an empty name and address instead of the existing values.
original_members.evidence: upsert_account_and_pii at 798-804 saves only email and never calls the legacy migration. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_pii.rs:322-488, this inserts a new row with absent encrypted name/address fields. migrate_from_plaintext at 494-511 selects only accounts where the joined PII row is absent, so api_me_handler's migration at 517 cannot recover this account after login. load_profile then reads only encrypted PII. The preservation contract is explicitly asserted by api_me_migriert_legacy_plaintext_pii at 2385-2447 in the assigned affiliate source.
original_members.expected_behavior: The existing migration must preserve legacy name and address values when an affiliate logs in and opens their profile. An email refresh must not make those supported legacy values invisible.
original_members.countermeasures: The PII saver preserves fields already stored in affiliate_pii, but it has no fallback to affiliate_accounts when inserting the first row. Profile GET and PUT invoke migration too late. An account migrated before OAuth avoids the bug. Addressing callback ordering can use the existing migration mechanism without requiring a new migration.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A Twitch rename allows a second affiliate to reserve an already freshly claimed streamer.

original_members.claim: A Twitch rename allows a second affiliate to reserve an already freshly claimed streamer.
original_members.failure_scenario: Affiliate A reserves an unpartnered streamer under old_name with verified Twitch ID 123. Within the four-day reservation window, that streamer renames to new_name. Affiliate B claims new_name, which Helix verifies as the same ID 123. The existing reservation is not found, and a second fresh claim for the same streamer succeeds.
original_members.evidence: claim_handler verifies and passes streamer_user_id at 468-477, but claim_streamer_verified_at uses only streamer_login for locking, partner lookup, and existing-claim lookup at 915-978. The verified ID is used solely in the INSERT at 1017-1027. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260617030000_baseline_missing_tables.sql:54-60 enforces uniqueness only on claimed_streamer_login; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260802140000_kanal_id_spalten_historientabellen.sql:31 adds the ID column without an identity uniqueness constraint. The rename handler's operational table list excludes affiliate claims. The fresh-reservation blocking contract is stated at 464-467 and tested at 2700-2718.
original_members.expected_behavior: A fresh reservation belongs to the verified streamer identity and must continue to block another affiliate after a login rename.
original_members.countermeasures: Helix validation proves that both names refer to ID 123 but does not participate in the conflict check. Advisory locking and the unique constraint protect one login spelling, not one streamer identity. The necessary ID column already exists; the failure does not require a schema migration to detect.

findings.title_de: Affiliate-Callback macht IPv6-Loopback-HTTP zu HTTPS
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Affiliate-Callback macht IPv6-Loopback-HTTP zu HTTPS.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: IPv6 loopback configuration is incorrectly changed from HTTP to HTTPS in affiliate callback URLs.

original_members.claim: IPv6 loopback configuration is incorrectly changed from HTTP to HTTPS in affiliate callback URLs.
original_members.failure_scenario: The public dashboard URL is configured as http://[::1]:8769 for a local HTTP server. Both callback URL builders derive their origin from this setting. The loopback check rejects ::1 and constructs https://[::1]:8769 callbacks, targeting TLS on an HTTP-only listener.
original_members.evidence: origin_from_urlish at 1222-1226 preserves HTTP only when is_loopback_host returns true. That helper strips IPv6 brackets and then splits at ':', yielding an empty first component for ::1 at 1261-1267. Consequently, the explicit ::1 match at 1269 is unreachable. resolved_candidate_group.claim: Concurrent affiliate OAuth login can revert a successfully saved profile.

original_members.claim: Concurrent affiliate OAuth login can revert a successfully saved profile.
original_members.failure_scenario: An affiliate edits their profile in an authenticated browser while completing a separate OAuth login in another browser. The OAuth email-only save reads the existing PII first. The profile PUT then saves a new name, address and tax details successfully. The OAuth save subsequently UPSERTs its previously read values for every omitted field, reverting those profile changes. Both requests succeed.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, the assigned handler constructs an email-only PiiInput at lines 798-804; the competing profile save is at lines 588-624. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_pii.rs:331-352, save_affiliate_pii_with_storage_login reads existing fields without a transaction or lock. Lines 365-455 retain that snapshot for omitted fields, and lines 458-488 unconditionally replace all columns during ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.
original_members.expected_behavior: The explicit partial-update contract in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_pii.rs:254-259 and 307-312 says omitted fields retain their existing values. Its test at lines 911-935 verifies an email-only update preserves name, tax details and VAT status. Neither serial ordering of these two operations would revert the newly saved non-email fields.
original_members.countermeasures: The PII primary key prevents duplicate rows but not stale-column replacement. Atomic OAuth-state consumption prevents reuse of one callback state, not a valid login racing with a profile PUT. The affiliate routes in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1400-1463 do not serialize these handlers. The shared save helper also serves migration, which has a separate stale-selection race described below.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Affiliate profile migration can overwrite encrypted data saved after its initial selection.

original_members.claim: Affiliate profile migration can overwrite encrypted data saved after its initial selection.
original_members.failure_scenario: Affiliate A has legacy account fields and no encrypted PII row. A GET /twitch/api/affiliate/me from affiliate B starts the global migration and selects A's legacy values. Before that migration processes A, A's profile PUT migrates its row and successfully saves new profile values. B's migration then processes its stale selection and overwrites A's newly saved encrypted name, email and address with the old legacy values.
original_members.evidence: The assigned handlers invoke the global migration at lines 517 and 570; their shared wrapper calls migrate_from_plaintext at line 825. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_pii.rs:495-515, migration materializes all accounts currently lacking PII. Lines 535-551 later pass those captured legacy fields as explicit updates to save_affiliate_pii_with_storage_login. That helper's UPSERT at lines 458-488 updates an existing PII row unconditionally, without rechecking the migration eligibility predicate.
original_members.expected_behavior: Migration's WHERE p.twitch_login IS NULL predicate at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_pii.rs:500-502 establishes that existing encrypted profiles are excluded. A row created and updated after the initial selection must likewise not be overwritten by legacy data. Correcting this race does not require a schema migration.
original_members.countermeasures: The absent-PII check occurs only in the initial SELECT, outside a transaction, and becomes stale. The primary key routes the later write into DO UPDATE rather than rejecting it. Serializing only the individual save helper would not suffice: the migration can acquire serialization after the profile update and still write its explicitly captured legacy values. Both assigned GET and PUT handlers expose this same migration path.

original_members.claim: Concurrent admin affiliate toggles lose one of the requested flips.
original_members.failure_scenario: An affiliate starts with is_active=1. Two valid admin POST requests toggle that affiliate concurrently. Both read 1 before either update, both calculate 0, and both write 0 and return success. Two completed flips leave the affiliate inactive instead of restoring its original active state.

In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/admin_affiliate.rs:608-633, a standalone SELECT is followed by computing new_status and a separate UPDATE with the captured value. There is no transaction, SELECT FOR UPDATE, compare-and-swap predicate or atomic SQL inversion.
original_members.expected_behavior: The assigned endpoint contract at lines 444-445 explicitly says to flip is_active. The helper contract at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/admin_affiliate.rs:605-607 and its test at lines 1163-1184 establish the sequence 1 to 0 to 1 for two successful toggles.

findings.title_de: Gutschriftdokument versendet SMTP synchron auf Tokio-Worker
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Gutschriftdokument versendet SMTP synchron auf Tokio-Worker.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Affiliate credit-document generation performs synchronous SMTP directly on Tokio workers.

original_members.claim: Affiliate credit-document generation performs synchronous SMTP directly on Tokio workers.
original_members.failure_scenario: With SMTP configured, valid generation requests for independent affiliate periods reach an SMTP server that accepts connections but delays its reply. Each request blocks a Tokio worker while sending. If concurrent sends occupy all runtime workers, unrelated dashboard requests cannot progress until a send returns. The background generation task also blocks a runtime worker when it sends mail.
original_members.evidence: The primary async run_gutschrift_job creates SmtpAffiliateEmailSender and directly awaits generation functions at lines 157-175, 186-198 and 203. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/affiliate_gutschrift.rs:1456-1493 invokes the synchronous sender.send_gutschrift method directly inside an async function. Its implementation at lines 299-322 calls blocking lettre SmtpTransport::send. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:268-279 runs the background caller with tokio::spawn, and line 306 uses tokio::main. Neither path isolates the synchronous send on a blocking worker.
original_members.expected_behavior: Waiting for SMTP should not suspend unrelated HTTP work on the shared async executor. Classified C because the reviewed sources do not establish an explicit dashboard latency guarantee, and changing the email execution boundary requires an implementation design choice.
original_members.countermeasures: SMTP has a configured 20-second transport timeout, so this is not a claim of wholly unbounded SMTP waits. Admin authentication and CSRF restrict manual generation but do not isolate blocking work or impose a generation concurrency limit. The six-hour background interval prevents overlapping scheduled runs, but does not prevent worker blocking during a run.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Portal kürzt Lebenszeitverdienst und Provisionshistorie.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The default commission page silently truncates the affiliate portal's lifetime earnings and commission history.

original_members.claim: The default commission page silently truncates the affiliate portal's lifetime earnings and commission history.
original_members.failure_scenario: An affiliate has 26 commissions of 300 cents, with the oldest transferred and the newest 25 pending. Opening the portal fetches the endpoint without pagination parameters. Only 25 rows arrive, so the UI shows total earnings of EUR 75 instead of EUR 78, transferred earnings of zero instead of EUR 3, and no way to view the oldest commission.
original_members.evidence: The handler defaults page_size to 25 and applies LIMIT/OFFSET (190-192, 239-247). AffiliatePortal's fetchData makes a single unparameterized commissions request and retains only commissions, ignoring total (264-317). Its earnings calculations reduce that array (444-450), render it as 'Gesamtverdienst' and 'Übertragen' (547-561), and display commission history without pagination controls (694-748). All sources were read at SHA 0ecae137.
original_members.expected_behavior: The portal's lifetime earnings and transferred totals must include the complete ledger, and older commission history must remain accessible. The explicit 'Gesamtverdienst' label and history description establish that these are not first-page-only figures.
original_members.countermeasures: The response includes a correct total row count, but the existing consumer neither reads it nor fetches additional pages. The separate portal_handler aggregates the complete ledger, but this frontend does not request that endpoint. The page-size-one test verifies pagination itself, not compatibility with the shipped consumer.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Affiliate recent-claim plan names are wrong for plans stored against a Twitch user ID.

original_members.claim: Affiliate recent-claim plan names are wrong for plans stored against a Twitch user ID.
original_members.failure_scenario: Claimed streamer 'kunde' has Twitch user ID '42' and an unexpired manual analysis_dashboard plan in streamer_plans keyed by '42', with twitch_login NULL. The portal resolves the plan using ('kunde', ''), misses the valid ID-bound override, and returns plan_name 'Free' instead of 'Erweitert'. An active billing subscription whose customer_reference is '42' has the same failure.
original_members.evidence: The recent-claims loop queries only display_name and passes an empty user ID to resolve_plan_snapshot (113-126). resolve_plan_snapshot_inner explicitly supports ID-only manual overrides and subscriptions, but its ID predicates require a nonempty argument (392-431, 497-556); otherwise it falls back to raid_free (599). Plan labels map raid_free to 'Free' and analysis_dashboard to 'Erweitert' (36-44). The baseline schema permits nullable streamer_plans.twitch_login (362-378).
original_members.expected_behavior: recent_claims.plan_name must represent the claimed streamer's effective plan. The resolver contract explicitly supports platform-ID-bound overrides and subscriptions and documents why omitting the ID misses paid or granted plans.
original_members.countermeasures: Normalizing the login does not recover an ID-only record. The resolver's ID fallback cannot operate because the caller passes an empty string. The existing customer identity source includes twitch_user_id, but this lookup selects only display_name.

findings.title_de: Große Provisionsseite überläuft auf erste Seite
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Große Provisionsseite überläuft auf erste Seite.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Commission pagination overflows its signed offset and can return page one for an enormous page number.

original_members.claim: Commission pagination overflows its signed offset and can return page one for an enormous page number.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated affiliate requests page=4611686018427387905&page_size=4. Both values pass the declared i64 parsing and clamps. The mathematical offset is 18446744073709551616, which wraps to zero with default release overflow behavior, so the endpoint returns the first four commissions while reporting the enormous page number. With overflow checks enabled, the same request panics.
original_members.evidence: CommissionsQuery accepts i64 values (166-171); page has only a lower bound and page_size is clamped to 1-100 (190-191). Their multiplication is unchecked (192), and the result is bound directly to SQL OFFSET (242-247). The release profile does not enable overflow checks (Cargo.toml 128-130). A targeted twin search found the same unchecked expression in social-media handlers at 1693 and 2304; those neighbors likewise only lower-bound page.
original_members.expected_behavior: An out-of-range page must be rejected or yield an empty page, never wrap to a different page or panic. OFFSET must remain a valid representation of the requested page.
original_members.countermeasures: The page_size clamp limits returned rows but not the multiplication. Serde rejects values outside i64, whereas this input is inside i64. Affiliate authentication and GET middleware do not validate pagination. Existing tests cover small page values only.

original_members.claim: Die Provisionspagination kann durch einen gültigen i64-page-Wert überlaufen und eine falsche Seite liefern oder paniken.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein angemeldeter Affiliate mit mindestens zehn Provisionen ruft /twitch/api/affiliate/commissions?page=737869762948382066&page_size=25 auf. Der mathematische Offset beträgt 18446744073709551625. Bei ungeprüfter i64-Arithmetik wird daraus 9, sodass eine extrem hohe Seitenzahl vorhandene frühe Datensätze liefert. Bei aktivierten Überlaufprüfungen panikt stattdessen der Request-Task.
original_members.evidence: CommissionsQuery akzeptiert page und page_size als Option<i64> (affiliate_portal.rs:166-172). Der Handler begrenzt nur die Untergrenze von page sowie page_size und multipliziert ungeprüft (190-192). Der Offset wird direkt an SQL OFFSET gebunden (230-247). /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/Cargo.toml:118-130 enthält im Release-Profil keine aktivierten Überlaufprüfungen. Die Bewertung beruht auf statischer Lektüre, nicht auf einem ausgeführten Test.
original_members.expected_behavior: Die angeforderte Seite muss ihrem tatsächlichen Offset entsprechen. Ein nicht darstellbarer Offset darf weder auf eine frühere Seite zurückspringen noch einen Panic auslösen. Der bestehende Paginationstest (affiliate_portal.rs:491-533) belegt den Seiten-, Größen- und Sortierungsvertrag.
original_members.countermeasures: Die i64-Deserialisierung akzeptiert den genannten Wert. .max(1) und .clamp(1,100) verhindern den Multiplikationsüberlauf nicht. Die Route ist in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:764-767 registriert; Affiliate-Pfade passieren den Partner-Gate. Authentifizierung begrenzt den Aufruferkreis, validiert aber nicht page. SQL-Fehlerbehandlung greift erst nach der bereits übergelaufenen Berechnung.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Fehlgeschlagene Portalabfrage meldet erfolgreiche Nullsummen.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Die Affiliate-Portal-API meldet fehlgeschlagene Statistikabfragen als erfolgreiche Nullsummen und leere Listen.

original_members.claim: Die Affiliate-Portal-API meldet fehlgeschlagene Statistikabfragen als erfolgreiche Nullsummen und leere Listen.
original_members.failure_scenario: Eine gültige Affiliate-Session und der Kontodatensatz werden geladen. Anschließend fällt die Datenbank aus oder eine Statistikabfrage wird abgebrochen. Der Handler antwortet trotzdem mit HTTP 200, beispielsweise pending_payout=0 und recent_claims=[], obwohl Provisionen und Claims vorhanden sind.
original_members.evidence: affiliate_portal.rs:70-108 verwirft die Fehler der Claims-, Provisions- und Listenabfragen durch .ok() beziehungsweise .unwrap_or_default(). Zeilen 146-163 erzeugen daraus ohne Fehlerkennzeichnung eine erfolgreiche JSON-Antwort mit Nullwerten. Der vorhandene Test in Zeilen 452-488 belegt, dass die Werte tatsächliche Claims und ausstehende Provisionen darstellen sollen. Quellen entsprechen dem festen Review-SHA; Tests wurden nur gelesen.
original_members.expected_behavior: Fehlgeschlagene Pflichtabfragen müssen als Fehler erkennbar bleiben. Nullsummen und leere Listen dürfen nur erfolgreiche Abfrageergebnisse darstellen. Der benachbarte commissions_handler unterscheidet Datenbankfehler ausdrücklich mit HTTP 500 (affiliate_portal.rs:194-210 und 230-259).
original_members.countermeasures: Die Affiliate-Session-Prüfung und der erfolgreiche Konto-Lookup sichern nur die vorausgehenden Schritte. Der Partner-Gate lässt Affiliate-Pfade ausdrücklich durch (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/partner_gate.rs:59-73,159-174). Keine dieser Schichten prüft die später verworfenen Abfragefehler. Die gezielte Prüfung benachbarter Affiliate-Handler ergab dort explizite Fehlerantworten statt dieses Musters.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Der Affiliate-Konto-Lookup meldet Datenbankfehler fälschlich als HTTP 404 not_found.

original_members.claim: Der Affiliate-Konto-Lookup meldet Datenbankfehler fälschlich als HTTP 404 not_found.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein Affiliate hat eine gültige Session und ein vorhandenes Konto. Nach erfolgreicher Session-Prüfung scheitert die Kontoabfrage beispielsweise durch Verbindungsabbruch. Die Portal-API antwortet mit 404 und not_found, obwohl das Konto existiert und nur nicht gelesen werden konnte.
original_members.evidence: affiliate_portal.rs:57-65 behandelt Ok(None) und Err(e) mit derselben 404-Antwort. Der Err-Zweig protokolliert den Fehler, verliert aber dessen Bedeutung in der HTTP-Antwort. Der entsprechende Profil-Lookup in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/affiliate.rs:521-529 trennt hingegen fehlende Konten (404) von Datenbankfehlern (500).
original_members.expected_behavior: 404 not_found darf nur das erfolgreiche Ergebnis ohne Kontodatensatz bezeichnen. Ein fehlgeschlagener Lookup muss eine Serverfehlerantwort liefern, wie beim benachbarten api_me_handler.
original_members.countermeasures: Das vorhandene Fehlerlog erhält die interne Diagnose, korrigiert aber nicht die falsche Antwort an den Client. Session-Prüfung und Partner-Gate können einen anschließend auftretenden Datenbankfehler nicht abfangen. Es ist kein Schemaumbau erforderlich, um fehlgeschlagene Abfragen von fehlenden Datensätzen zu unterscheiden.

original.evidence: affiliate_portal.rs:57-65 behandelt Ok(None) und Err(e) mit derselben 404-Antwort. Der Err-Zweig protokolliert den Fehler, verliert aber dessen Bedeutung in der HTTP-Antwort. Der entsprechende Profil-Lookup in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/affiliate.rs:521-529 trennt hingegen fehlende Konten (404) von Datenbankfehlern (500).
original.expected_behavior: 404 not_found darf nur das erfolgreiche Ergebnis ohne Kontodatensatz bezeichnen. Ein fehlgeschlagener Lookup muss eine Serverfehlerantwort liefern, wie beim benachbarten api_me_handler.
original.countermeasures: Das vorhandene Fehlerlog erhält die interne Diagnose, korrigiert aber nicht die falsche Antwort an den Client. resolved_candidate_group.claim: The affiliate OAuth callback test races with another test's master-key restoration and can unexpectedly return HTTP 503.

original_members.claim: The affiliate OAuth callback test races with another test's master-key restoration and can unexpectedly return HTTP 503.
original_members.failure_scenario: With the test database configured and DB_MASTER_KEY_V1 initially absent, platforms_status_read_errors_return_500_not_disconnected records the absent value and installs its test key. The affiliate callback test then installs the same key and begins its asynchronous callback. If the status test finishes before the callback constructs FieldCipher, its guard removes the key. The callback returns HTTP 503 instead of the expected redirect, failing the assertion at line 1760.
original_members.evidence: The affiliate test sets the process-wide key at line 1731 without a lock. Its callback reaches FieldCipher::from_env through upsert_account_and_pii at line 799; persistence errors produce HTTP 503 at lines 262-267. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/social_media_status_tests.rs:3-15 defines the independently restoring guard. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-crypto/src/field.rs:27-29 reads the live environment on each call. Context files match the fixed review SHA.
original_members.expected_behavior: The callback fixture should reliably create the affiliate account, encrypted email and session, then redirect to the portal, as asserted at lines 1760-1792.
original_members.countermeasures: Separate database schemas do not isolate process-wide environment variables. Using the same test key does not prevent its removal. Neither affected test acquires a common environment lock. This is a test-only race established by static interleaving, not an observed production key change.

findings.title_de: Portal hält Verbindungen ohne wirksame SQL-Zeitgrenze
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Portal hält Verbindungen ohne wirksame SQL-Zeitgrenze.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Affiliate portal reads can indefinitely occupy the shared dashboard database pool when PostgreSQL has no statement timeout.

original_members.claim: Affiliate portal reads can indefinitely occupy the shared dashboard database pool when PostgreSQL has no statement timeout.
original_members.failure_scenario: With statement_timeout=0 and lock_timeout=0, an unfinished transaction holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on affiliate_accounts. Valid authenticated portal requests reach the account SELECT and wait while retaining pool connections. Enough concurrent requests consume pool_max connections, so unrelated dashboard requests cannot acquire a connection until the lock ends and instead hit acquisition errors. This is a conditional configuration failure scenario, not a verified production incident.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed at fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The account SELECT at lines 50-56 awaits SQL without an execution deadline. The same pattern appears in this slice's commission count and page queries at lines 194-200 and 230-249. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 constructs the shared pool using tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:10-11 selects read_only=false; lines 41-53 bound pool size and connection acquisition, but install statement_timeout only for read_only=true. The portal routes are registered at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:760-766.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled portal read should eventually fail and release its database connection rather than hold shared capacity indefinitely. The existing code does not specify a portal execution deadline or require deployment-level SQL timeouts, so selecting that policy remains a C-level recommendation, not an unambiguous B fix.
original_members.countermeasures: Affiliate-session validation restricts access. LIMIT 10 bounds recent-claim materialization, page_size is clamped to 100, and pool_max plus acquire_timeout bound connections and acquisition waits. None bounds execution after a connection has been acquired. A statement/lock timeout supplied through the DSN or PostgreSQL role/server configuration would prevent this scenario; deployment values were not read or probed. No unbounded production collection or retry loop was found in the assigned primary ranges.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Profile lookup can select inactive partner history instead of the current active partner.

original_members.claim: Profile lookup can select inactive partner history instead of the current active partner.
original_members.failure_scenario: The same Twitch ID and login have an older archived/departnered partner row and a newer active row with raid_bot_enabled=1 and no disconnect flags. Their shared profile is published. This state satisfies the production constraints. The unordered LIMIT 1 can select the older inactive row. The public profile then returns 404, although the directory lists it; the owner's GET reports active=false and PUT rejects edits with 403.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, load() computes ACTIVE as a selected boolean but filters only by login, with neither status precedence nor ordering (lines 525-540). The public handler rejects that selected inactive row at lines 799-801; PUT rejects it at lines 642-653. Production schema /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:2219-2220 uses id as the primary key, and lines 2573-2575 enforce login/user-ID uniqueness only WHERE status='active', permitting inactive history alongside the active row. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/streamer_lifecycle.rs:541-545 explicitly selects existing partner rows with active-status precedence.
original_members.expected_behavior: A currently active partner's published profile must remain reachable and editable despite retained inactive history. The active lifecycle record must take precedence. This follows from the profile's live lifecycle gate and directory query at lines 696-698, and the active-first partner selection in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/streamer_lifecycle.rs:541-545.
original_members.countermeasures: The later record.active checks fail closed but do not retry or select the active row. The owner Twitch-ID check does not distinguish history rows belonging to the same ID. Partial unique indexes prevent multiple active rows, not inactive shadowing. The public visibility recheck repeats the same unordered lookup. Existing profile tests use an artificial twitch_user_id PRIMARY KEY (/home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/partner_profiles/tests.rs:30), excluding this production-valid state. Targeted comparison found proper active filtering in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/partner_setup.rs:307-312 and in the profile directory, rather than an additional independent twin.

original_members.claim: An inactive historical partner can shadow the active published profile of a reused Twitch login.
original_members.failure_scenario: A departs while retaining login alice. B is an existing active partner with a published profile and later renames to alice. Rename reconciliation leaves inactive A's historical row unchanged and updates B to alice. When the unordered LIMIT 1 lookup selects A first, /streamer/alice returns 404 despite B being active and published. The public directory simultaneously lists B's alice profile. B's owner GET and PUT can also reject the selected historical identity before reaching B's profile.
original_members.evidence: load filters only lower(p.twitch_login) and applies unordered LIMIT 1 at primary lines 525-540. Public eligibility and owner identity checks happen after selection at 800-801,605 and 643. The directory instead filters ACTIVE before selecting entries at 696-698. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:2573-2575 makes login uniqueness conditional on status='active', permitting the inactive and active rows together. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/streamer_lifecycle.rs:260-274 retains the departed row and login. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/streamer_login.rs:547-563 only clears conflicting status='active' partner rows before updating B's login, so inactive A remains a legal competing lookup result. All cited sources match the fixed review SHA.
original_members.expected_behavior: A retained inactive account must not mask the active published account owning the current public address. The public directory and page share the ACTIVE visibility contract. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/partner_profiles/tests.rs:411-433 establishes that a published profile follows stable Twitch identity to its current login.
original_members.countermeasures: The active-only unique index prevents two active holders but does not prevent an inactive historical holder. Rename collision cleanup deliberately excludes inactive rows. The later active and owner-ID guards prevent publishing the historical account accidentally, but return an error rather than selecting the eligible account. The targeted twin search found only this lookup; its shared callers are affected without implying coverage outside the assigned slice.

findings.title_de: Profilimport meldet Erfolg trotz Twitch-Streamplanfehler
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Profilimport meldet Erfolg trotz Twitch-Streamplanfehler.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Bei fehlgeschlagenem Twitch-Streamplanabruf meldet der Profilimport trotzdem Erfolg.

original_members.claim: Bei fehlgeschlagenem Twitch-Streamplanabruf meldet der Profilimport trotzdem Erfolg.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein aktiver Partner hat kommende Twitch-Termine und klickt auf „Aus Twitch importieren“. Der erzwungene Abruf liefert erfolgreich die Benutzerinformationen, aber alle drei schnellen /schedule-Anfragen liefern HTTP 503. Die übrigen Abrufe sind erfolgreich und alles endet innerhalb der Vier-Sekunden-Grenze. Die Antwort enthält available=true und schedule=[], ersetzt den bisherigen Cachestand für 60 Sekunden und leert die angezeigten Twitch-Termine. Der Editor meldet dennoch ausdrücklich, der Streamplan sei aktualisiert. Eigene gespeicherte Zusatztermine sind davon nicht betroffen.
original_members.evidence: Codebasis 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, geprüfte Quellen ohne Drift. Die Primärdatei setzt available ausschließlich beim erfolgreichen Benutzerabruf auf true (246-267), protokolliert den Schedule-Fehler nur (311-313) und speichert trotzdem den Snapshot mit leerem Schedule (335-340). /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/pages/PartnerProfile.tsx:180-200 fordert den Neuabruf an, prüft ausschließlich available und zeigt anschließend die Erfolgsmeldung einschließlich Streamplan. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-transport-twitch/src/client.rs:31-36,239-280,463-472 belegt drei Versuche mit insgesamt 1,5 Sekunden Backoff und den danach weitergegebenen Statusfehler. Der Fehlerfall kann daher vor dem äußeren Timeout eintreten.
original_members.expected_behavior: Ein gescheiterter Streamplanabruf darf beim ausdrücklich ausgelösten Import nicht als erfolgreich aktualisierter Streamplan gemeldet werden. Der Importvertrag in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/docs/PARTNER_PROFILES.md:11-15,103-107 umfasst den frischen Streamplanabruf. Die öffentliche Profilseite kann ihre anderen Inhalte weiterhin als Rückfall anzeigen.
original_members.countermeasures: Benutzerabruffehler und der äußere Vier-Sekunden-Timeout führen zu available=false und damit zu einer sichtbaren Importfehlermeldung. Diese Schutzpfade greifen bei einem rechtzeitig abgeschlossenen Schedule-Fehler nicht. Transport-Retries und Warnlogs sind vorhanden, reichen nach erschöpften Versuchen aber nicht bis zum Editor. refresh_twitch=true umgeht den alten Cache; die nachfolgende Einfügung überschreibt ihn trotzdem. Besitzprüfung und CSRF sichern den Zugriff, verhindern diesen Fehlerfall eines berechtigten Partners aber nicht. Gezielter Vergleich mit dem benachbarten AvatarCache ergab keinen zusätzlichen belegten Zwillingsbefund; keine Vollabdeckung außerhalb dieses Abschnitts beansprucht.

All cited sources match the fixed review SHA.
original_members.expected_behavior: The final check must establish continued visibility of the same Twitch identity whose content will be rendered. The primary file explicitly promises at lines 838-839 not to render a withdrawn snapshot after concurrent lifecycle changes. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/partner_profiles/tests.rs:333-400 verifies that lifecycle withdrawal hides public profiles.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Profile SQL operations have no application-level query deadline.

original_members.claim: Profile SQL operations have no application-level query deadline.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, another transaction holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_partner_profiles without completing. Public profile requests block in load(). Enough such requests occupy every dashboard pool connection indefinitely; subsequent requests fail pool acquisition while the original handlers remain pending.
original_members.evidence: load() awaits fetch_optional at lines 525-540; directory(), history() and the profile upsert likewise await SQL without deadlines. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 uses tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-56 limits connection acquisition but sets statement_timeout only in read-only mode, which connect does not use. The router assembly at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2204-2271 supplies no request timeout.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled dependency should eventually release request resources and produce the existing unavailable response. No SQL deadline contract is specified, and deployed PostgreSQL role settings were not inspected, so this remains C rather than an automatically fixable B.
original_members.countermeasures: The pool bounds connection count and acquisition time, but acquisition timeout does not bound a query after checkout. The four-second timeout at lines 586-591 covers Twitch enrichment only. An externally configured PostgreSQL statement_timeout or lock_timeout could mitigate this; its production value is unverified. The supplied profile proxy configuration at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/caddy/partner-profiles.caddy:7-12 adds no response deadline.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Concurrent cache misses for one Twitch profile each start a full upstream refresh.

original_members.claim: Concurrent cache misses for one Twitch profile each start a full upstream refresh.
original_members.failure_scenario: Six public requests arrive for the same published partner after its cache entry expires, before any refresh completes. Each request starts at least four Helix operations, yielding at least 24 instead of four. If the upstream bucket has 20 requests remaining, this burst exhausts it and produces rate-limit failures that a shared refresh would avoid.
original_members.evidence: Lines 226-232 check freshness under a short-lived mutex but record no refresh-in-progress state. Lines 238-244 start four operations for each miss; lines 335-341 populate the cache only after completion. The public page reaches this path at lines 799-808. The public route at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:166-170 has no local rate limiter. The neighboring network enrichment cache explicitly guards in-flight refreshes at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/network.rs:168-195.
original_members.expected_behavior: Coalescing same-key refreshes would keep a traffic burst from multiplying upstream requests and causing avoidable enrichment failures. This cache has no explicit coalescing contract, so the recommendation is C.
original_members.countermeasures: Fresh entries suppress ordinary repeated reads for 60 seconds. The outer four-second deadline bounds each refresh duration, transport retries are capped at three attempts, and AppTokenManager deduplicates token acquisition. None deduplicates the profile Helix requests themselves. Active/published checks prevent arbitrary nonexistent IDs from reaching the public refresh. Deployed global proxy throttling was not inspected.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The Twitch profile cache never evicts expired keys.

original_members.claim: The Twitch profile cache never evicts expired keys.
original_members.failure_scenario: During a long-lived dashboard process, distinct partners have their profiles fetched and later disconnect or stop receiving visits. After the 60-second TTL, every abandoned snapshot remains allocated. Repeated partner turnover increases retained memory with the total historical distinct IDs rather than the currently useful cache entries, without a capacity bound.
original_members.evidence: The Arc-backed HashMap is created at lines 203-206. Lines 226-232 reject expired values for reads without removing them, and lines 335-341 only insert or replace the requested key. No eviction or pruning exists in the complete cache implementation. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:488-492 installs one cache for the router lifetime. A targeted twin check found the same retention pattern in AvatarCache at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/internal_home.rs:338-376.
original_members.expected_behavior: An eviction or capacity policy would bound retained stale metadata during continuous operation. TTL currently specifies freshness only, not a documented eviction guarantee; this resource-policy issue therefore remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: Keys come from database-backed partner identities, not arbitrary public query parameters. Schedule and clip counts are bounded, limiting each snapshot's normal size. The directory's LIMIT 500 does not cap cache keys because individual profile and owner requests bypass the directory. Revisiting an ID replaces its value, but never-used expired IDs remain until process exit.
