resolved_candidate_group.claim: Featured recommendations can switch to an unrelated Twitch account after login reuse.

original_members.claim: Featured recommendations can switch to an unrelated Twitch account after login reuse.
original_members.failure_scenario: Alice recommends Bob by saving featured=["bob"]. Bob renames his account to bob_new. A different Twitch account subsequently owns bob and becomes an active, published partner. Alice's unchanged page now recommends the new account under 'Streamer, mit denen ich gerne unterwegs bin'.
original_members.evidence: The renderer resolves recommendations solely through entry.login == featured_login. Content.featured is Vec<String> in partner_profiles.rs:65; validation at 494-500 normalizes names without resolving Twitch IDs. directory() at 696-698 supplies current logins but no IDs. The profile schema stores these references inside unconstrained JSON content.
original_members.expected_behavior: The editor describes recommendations as streamers the owner plays or creates content with (PartnerProfile.tsx:695), which suggests account identity rather than whichever account later owns a name. However, the editor explicitly accepts Twitch names, and changing persisted references requires a compatibility or migration decision, so this remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: The active/published directory gate and self-exclusion prevent hidden or self recommendations, but the replacement account passes both. Stable-ID ownership and history checks protect other profile data, not featured references. The rename test checks the owner's URL and history, not recommendations.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Upcoming-stream deduplication discards distinct manual events with nearby starts and matching titles.

original_members.claim: Upcoming-stream deduplication discards distinct manual events with nearby starts and matching titles.
original_members.failure_scenario: With Twitch synchronization disabled, a profile contains two future manual events with distinct UUIDs, both titled 'Warmup': 18:00-18:02 and 18:04-18:06. Both validate and appear in the calendar, but 'Nächste Streams' shows only the first.
original_members.evidence: upcoming_items() discards event IDs when constructing Upcoming at 164-170, then deduplicates solely by start-time proximity and case-insensitive title at 194-197. It does not compare source, end time or event identity. Validation in partner_profiles.rs:502-521 permits these distinct, nonoverlapping events.
original_members.expected_behavior: Distinct saved appointments would normally remain distinct. However, approximate deduplication is explicitly implemented and its intended cross-source merging policy is undocumented. Restricting it could change intended behavior, so this is C rather than an automatic fix candidate.
original_members.countermeasures: UUID uniqueness validation does not help because UUIDs are discarded before deduplication. The six-item display limit is applied afterward and does not explain losing one of only two events. Existing rendering tests cover calendar limits but not this deduplication case. No deduplication twin was found in the inspected profile module.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Failed clip-contest session reads silently select a fallback Twitch submitter or report successful logged-out status.

original_members.claim: Failed clip-contest session reads silently select a fallback Twitch submitter or report successful logged-out status.
original_members.failure_scenario: During the submission phase, a browser has a valid Discord contest session and a separately authenticated Twitch dashboard account without linked aliases. After dashboard authentication succeeds, the contest-session SQL lookup temporarily fails. Subsequent database queries recover. The lookup error becomes None, so submit_identity selects the Twitch account and a valid clip submission succeeds under that account instead of the active Discord identity. With only the contest cookie and a persistent database failure, GET /clips/api/session instead returns HTTP 200 with authenticated=false and zero usage; submit and vote return login-required errors.
original_members.evidence: At fixed revision 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/clip_contest.rs:225-238 discards load_clip_contest_session errors through .ok().flatten(). Lines 292-328 interpret None as permission to select the dashboard identity. The alias query at line 328 similarly discards SQL failures. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:569-581 and 1993-2014 explicitly propagate lookup SQL errors. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/clip_contest/contest.rs:373-407 returns successful anonymous session data when identity is None; lines 503-509 and 739-744 map it to authentication errors. Lines 449-456 persist the selected identity, and 647-664 commit and report submission success.
original_members.expected_behavior: Keep a failed identity lookup distinct from an absent or expired session. Return contest_unavailable without changing the selected identity or persisting a fallback submission. Successful contest-session resolution already takes precedence over dashboard authentication in clip_contest.rs:292-326. The same contest implementation propagates other identity-related database failures as unavailable at contest.rs:767-770.

findings.title_de: Onboarding hält Pool bei Zeilensperren
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Onboarding hält Pool bei Zeilensperren.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Onboarding writes can exhaust the shared dashboard pool indefinitely while waiting for a database row lock.

original_members.claim: Onboarding writes can exhaust the shared dashboard pool indefinitely while waiting for a database row lock.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, another transaction retains a lock on an existing streamer_onboarding row. pool_max authenticated POST requests for that partner reach the upsert and wait indefinitely, occupying every shared pool connection. Subsequent dashboard requests fail pool acquisition instead of serving normally.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae137, onboarding.rs:209-226 awaits the upsert without an execution deadline. lib.rs:508-510 registers the route; main.rs:400 and 476-483 supply the shared tb_db::connect pool. tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 limits connection acquisition but sets statement_timeout only for read_only=true; connect uses false. The composed router has no request timeout. ops/systemd/twitch-runtime-roles.sql:62-65 grants dashboard writes, so permission denial does not prevent this wait. The same unbounded database-await pattern appears in clip_contest.rs:803-806 for logout.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled database operation should release request and pool resources within a finite execution budget and return an error. No exact database execution budget is specified, and deployed database timeout settings were not inspected, so this remains C rather than an automatic-fix B.
original_members.countermeasures: The pool's acquisition timeout bounds only waiting for a connection, not an executing statement. Existing HTTP bounds are effective elsewhere: challenges has an eight-second wrapper, clip verification has eight seconds, Steam status has five seconds, and Discord broker requests have twenty seconds. None bounds the onboarding upsert. Server-side statement_timeout or lock_timeout could mitigate this conditional scenario; their deployed values are unverified.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Contest identity lookup failures are misreported as signed-out sessions and login-required errors.

original_members.claim: Contest identity lookup failures are misreported as signed-out sessions and login-required errors.
original_members.failure_scenario: A viewer has a valid, unexpired Discord contest session. Loading that session succeeds, but the subsequent twitch_streamer_identities lookup fails, for example because a table lock causes its statement timeout while other tables remain accessible. GET /clips/api/session returns HTTP 200 with authenticated=false, discord_authenticated=false, submissions_used=0 and eligibility_unavailable=false. The page consequently asks this already signed-in viewer to sign in again. POST /clips/api/submit under the same condition returns HTTP 401 login_required instead of a temporary service error.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/clip_contest.rs:328 converts identity_aliases(...).await into Option with .ok()?, losing the SQL error. The assigned contest.rs:373-407 then treats None as a genuinely absent session and returns a successful signed-out response; contest.rs:502-509 returns login_required for the same None. The related helper clip_contest.rs:225-237 also discards session-store errors, affecting contest.rs:739-744. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/website/src/clips.tsx:174-175 and 225-235 use these flags to display login instructions. Primary files match commit 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af; contextual evidence was read with git show at that commit.
original_members.expected_behavior: Unavailable identity storage must be distinguished from an absent or invalid login. The existing unavailable() response in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/clip_contest.rs:402-407 explicitly provides HTTP 503 and retry guidance. The same alias lookup already returns unavailable() on failure in contest.rs:767-770, and session quota lookup failures return unavailable() at 379-389. Identity lookup failures should follow that error contract rather than assert successful logout or require another login.
original_members.countermeasures: The public routes in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2057-2108 do not intercept these failures. DashboardAuthLevel extraction is infallible and does not authenticate the contest cookie, so a viewer with only that cookie reaches these handlers. Origin checks and phase checks can pass for a legitimate submission and do not preserve the discarded error. Denying writes remains fail-closed, so this is not a security bypass. eligibility_unavailable covers community eligibility failures only and remains false after identity lookup failure. The read tests cover expiry and revocation, but do not exercise session or alias storage failures. Twins were checked in current_handler, submit_handler and vote_handler; no coverage outside this assigned slice is claimed.

original_members.claim: A Discord vote can be accepted for an own clip when account linking completes while the vote waits for the month lock.
original_members.failure_scenario: An eligible Discord account D votes for a clip submitted by its currently unlinked Twitch account T. The submission was saved while unlinked, so its submitter key and aliases contain twitch:T, not discord:D. The vote resolves aliases as [discord:D], then waits behind another contest transaction. The verified D-to-T link commits before the vote obtains the month lock. persist_vote nevertheless uses the old aliases, is_own returns false, and the vote commits.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, aliases are read at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/clip_contest/contest.rs:767-770 before begin_write at 771. The unchanged vector is passed at 775-779. is_own at 213-228 only compares the supplied aliases with saved identity, broadcaster and creator identifiers; persist_vote at 675-684 performs no fresh identity lookup. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/streamers_crud.rs:877-907 can commit linking independently while the contest lock is held.
original_members.expected_behavior: A linked Discord identity must not vote for its own submission, broadcaster or creator clip. Resolving the committed link would include twitch:T and reject the scenario.
original_members.countermeasures: Saved submitter_aliases protect clips submitted after linking, so the example specifically uses a submission saved before linking. The shared month lock protects submission visibility and vote quotas but does not coordinate with the separate identity-link lock. original_members.failure_scenario: In one submission month, unlinked accounts D and T each submit one clip, producing discord:D slot 1 and twitch:T slot 1. findings.title_de: Monatsabschluss ohne eigene SQL-Ausführungsfrist
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Monatsabschluss ohne eigene SQL-Ausführungsfrist.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Monthly finalization has no application-enforced SQL deadline.

original_members.claim: Monthly finalization has no application-enforced SQL deadline.
original_members.failure_scenario: With inherited statement_timeout and lock_timeout unset, a long-lived ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_clip_contest_months stalls finalize_pending's INSERT indefinitely. On a four-connection contest pool, the minute finalizer plus three archive requests can occupy every connection. Other contest requests then fail pool acquisition, and the background finalizer never advances to its next tick until the blocking transaction ends.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. contest.rs:184-193 executes the month INSERT directly on the pool, outside lock_month; archive_handler calls it at 313. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:294-303 awaits finalization without a deadline and shares contest_writer with the router at 443-449 and 476-483. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2024-2037 caps that pool at four connections but sets only an acquisition deadline. The public archive route at 2068 has no route-specific timeout or rate limiter. Related pool-backed reads at contest.rs:255-260 and 316-331 also have no local SQL deadline.
original_members.expected_behavior: A blocked finalization attempt should terminate and release its borrowed connection so subsequent scheduled runs and independent contest reads remain possible. The acceptable query deadline is not specified, and deployment-level timeout settings were not inspected, so this remains C rather than a confirmed A/B defect.
original_members.countermeasures: lock_month sets a five-second lock_timeout at contest.rs:21, but only inside its transaction, after the unbounded INSERT discussed here. Acquisition deadlines limit new pool waiters, not statements already borrowing connections. MissedTickBehavior::Delay prevents overlapping background ticks. Helix fetching has an eight-second timeout, request bodies are limited to 4096 bytes, and result pages have explicit row limits. An inherited PostgreSQL or DSN timeout could already mitigate this scenario; verify that policy before choosing any change.

findings.title_de: Roadmap-Update markiert ungelesene private Antwort als gelesen
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Roadmap-Update markiert ungelesene private Antwort als gelesen.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A concurrent roadmap update can mark an unseen private reply to a bundled feedback entry as read.

original_members.claim: A concurrent roadmap update can mark an unseen private reply to a bundled feedback entry as read.
original_members.failure_scenario: Entry B is bundled under root A, which links to roadmap R. An admin updates B with a new private reply: B.updated_at becomes t1, but the transaction pauses before committing. A separate roadmap PATCH commits a change to R with updated_at=t2, where t2>t1. The owner opens B before the reply transaction commits. Detail sees the new roadmap but the old B and old reply history, returning observed_at=t2. The normal read-marker request waits for B's row lock, then stores owner_seen_at=t2 after the reply commits. Subsequent list/detail/counts return unread=false because GREATEST(B.updated_at, A.shared_updated_at, R.updated_at)=t2. The new private reply was never displayed before being marked read.
original_members.evidence: Sources match fixed review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The primary file collapses three independently committed sources into one timestamp at lines 164-166 and advances owner_seen_at without checking the observed revision at line 303. B's row timestamp is assigned before event insertion and transaction commit at lines 531-534 and 446-449. The duplicate branch reads its root and roadmap without locking the roadmap at lines 499-506. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/roadmap.rs:267-282 independently writes roadmap.updated_at and commits its statement. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/pages/feedback/FeedbackPage.tsx:95-105 automatically sends exactly the detail's observed_at, so the scenario requires no forged client timestamp.
original_members.expected_behavior: Reading a snapshot must not acknowledge a private reply absent from that snapshot. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/feedback/tests.rs:172-274 explicitly establishes that an older read marker must preserve unread status for a later reply.
original_members.countermeasures: REPEATABLE READ keeps detail and history mutually consistent, but does not make timestamps from different rows follow commit order. The global feedback advisory lock serializes feedback edits only; the roadmap PATCH does not acquire it. FOR SHARE protects direct roadmap assignments, but is skipped when editing a duplicate with roadmap_id=None. The feedback revision guard protects admin edits, not read acknowledgements. GREATEST prevents stale markers from moving backwards, but cannot distinguish the unseen reply from the already observed roadmap update. The checked feedback migration provides uniqueness and foreign-key constraints, not a snapshot-aware acknowledgement guard. Static review only; no tests, database requests, or mutations were performed.

findings.title_de: Feedbackdetails laden unbegrenzten Antwortverlauf
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Feedbackdetails laden unbegrenzten Antwortverlauf.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Feedback-Details materialisieren den unbegrenzt wachsenden Antwortverlauf vollständig im Arbeitsspeicher.

original_members.claim: Feedback-Details materialisieren den unbegrenzt wachsenden Antwortverlauf vollständig im Arbeitsspeicher.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein Betreiber speichert für einen Eintrag 100.000 gültige Updates mit jeweils neuer request_id, passender Revision und 4.000 ASCII-Zeichen Antwort. Ein anschließender Detailaufruf lädt mindestens 400 MB Antworttexte und erzeugt zusätzlich deren JSON-Abbild. Hat der Prozess beispielsweise nur 512 MiB verfügbaren Speicher, übersteigt bereits das gleichzeitige Halten von SQL-Zeilen und JSON diesen Rahmen; der Detailaufruf kann den Prozess durch Speichermangel beenden.
original_members.evidence: Codebasis 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af: L282-284 verwendet SELECT ohne LIMIT, fetch_all und eine vollständig gesammelte JSON-Liste. L410-411 begrenzt nur die einzelne Antwort; L459-468 verhindert lediglich Wiederholungen derselben request_id. L531-534 erhöht die Revision und legt bei jedem weiteren gültigen Update ein Ereignis an. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260909211000_dashboard_feedback.sql:37-49 enthält keine Begrenzung der Ereigniszahl. Der Consumer unter /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/dashboard_v2/src/pages/feedback/FeedbackPage.tsx:124-125 rendert ebenfalls den gesamten Verlauf.
original_members.expected_behavior: Ein großer, gültiger Verlauf sollte lesbar bleiben, ohne den verfügbaren Prozessspeicher zu überschreiten. Eine maximale Verlaufslänge oder ein Vertrag für paginierte Detailantworten ist nicht belegt; deshalb C und keine automatische Fixfreigabe.
original_members.countermeasures: Updates sind Betreiberaktionen, Antworten sind einzeln auf 4.000 Zeichen begrenzt und identische request_id werden dedupliziert. Die Erstellungsgrenze von fünf Rückmeldungen pro Stunde und zwanzig pro Tag gilt nicht für Antworten. Die 24-KiB-Grenze in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:524-526 begrenzt nur eingehende Update-Requests. Eine reale Speichergrenze und dieses Datenvolumen wurden nicht produktiv überprüft. Pagination oder eine Aufbewahrungsgrenze wären Vertragsentscheidungen.

findings.title_de: Feedback wartet unbefristet auf Advisory-Lock
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Feedback wartet unbefristet auf Advisory-Lock.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Blockierte Feedback-Transaktionen können über unbefristete Advisory-Lock-Wartezeiten den gemeinsamen Dashboard-Pool belegen.

original_members.claim: Blockierte Feedback-Transaktionen können über unbefristete Advisory-Lock-Wartezeiten den gemeinsamen Dashboard-Pool belegen.
original_members.failure_scenario: PostgreSQL hat keine wirksamen statement_timeout- oder lock_timeout-Grenzen. Eine andere offene Transaktion hält die Schreibsperre auf einem Roadmap-Eintrag. Ein gültiges Feedback-Update erwirbt den globalen Advisory-Lock und wartet anschließend bei SELECT FOR SHARE auf diesen Roadmap-Eintrag. Weitere Betreiber-Updates erwerben jeweils eine Poolverbindung und warten auf denselben Advisory-Lock. Bei entsprechend vielen parallelen Requests sind sämtliche Poolverbindungen belegt; weitere Dashboard-Abfragen scheitern beim Erwerb einer Verbindung, solange die ursprüngliche Sperre bestehen bleibt.
original_members.evidence: Am festen Review-SHA erwirbt L433-440 eine Transaktion und den globalen pg_advisory_xact_lock ohne lokale Zeitgrenze. L508-513 wartet innerhalb dieser Transaktion auf einen Roadmap-Datensatz mit FOR SHARE. Der ähnliche Create-Pfad wartet in L348-355 auf einen kontobezogenen Advisory-Lock. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 und 476-483 verbindet und übergibt den gemeinsam genutzten Pool. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-57 begrenzt den Verbindungserwerb, setzt statement_timeout aber ausschließlich für connect_readonly, nicht für den hier verwendeten connect-Pfad. Die Feedback-Routen und globalen Router-Layer enthalten keinen Request-Timeout.
original_members.expected_behavior: Eine blockierte Rückmeldungsaktion sollte nach einer begrenzten Wartezeit scheitern und ihre Verbindung freigeben, statt andere Dashboard-Abfragen dauerhaft zu verdrängen. Eine konkrete verbindliche Wartezeit ist nicht belegt; produktive PostgreSQL- und Proxy-Grenzen sind unbekannt. Daher C.
original_members.countermeasures: Poolgröße und Erwerbszeit sind begrenzt; Erwerbszeitüberschreitungen beenden jedoch nicht bereits laufende Sperrwartezeiten. Betreiberprüfung und CSRF-Schutz begrenzen den Update-Zugang, beseitigen aber keine blockierte Transaktion. Transaktionsende gibt die Advisory-Locks frei, tritt beim beschriebenen unbegrenzten Warten jedoch nicht ein. Externe PostgreSQL-, DSN- oder Proxy-Zeitgrenzen könnten den Fall abfangen und wurden wegen der read-only Grenzen ohne Laufzeitabfragen nicht verifiziert.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Preauthorized camera peers can recreate a signaling room after permanent revocation.

original_members.claim: Preauthorized camera peers can recreate a signaling room after permanent revocation.
original_members.failure_scenario: A publisher finishes authorization and its consent UPDATE, and a subscriber finishes its consent check. Both handshakes are delayed before room registration. An administrator revokes the camera, removes the room and returns success. The two pending handshakes then register in a newly created room and exchange offers and answers, permitting camera transmission while the database still records permanent revocation.
original_members.evidence: The anchored file checks publisher and subscriber authorization at lines 630-645, before acquiring the hub mutex. Lines 655-695 unconditionally create the room and insert those previously authorized peers. Revocation removes only the room present at lines 538-545. Signal forwarding at lines 766-784 checks room membership, not current consent. Unlike the preceding finding, this interleaving leaves revoked_at non-NULL.
original_members.expected_behavior: A completed permanent revocation must prevent pending connections from starting transmission. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/pages/content/CasterOverlay.tsx:283-299 promises that revocation ends running connections; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/caster_camera.html:18,23 promises permanent withdrawal.
original_members.countermeasures: The room mutex serializes individual hub mutations, but database authorization occurs outside that critical section. Room removal retains no revocation marker or connection generation. The authorization predicates reject subsequent handshakes, not already approved ones. Making the consent UPDATE conditional alone would not eliminate this separate registration window.

original_members.claim: Stopping the camera can be undone by an in-flight device switch.
original_members.failure_scenario: While publishing, the user changes camera devices and getUserMedia remains pending. When the pending device request completes, openMedia assigns its new live stream to the global stream variable and preview, restarting capture after Stop.
original_members.evidence: The anchored file's line 14 awaits getUserMedia before assigning stream and preview.srcObject. Line 20 starts this asynchronous operation whenever a device changes. Line 22 independently stops the current stream and sets stream=null, but does not invalidate pending acquisition. The device-change continuation can therefore overwrite the stopped state.
original_members.expected_behavior: Stop must leave capture stopped and the preview cleared until another explicit Start. This behavior is directly implemented by the Stop handler at line 22.
original_members.countermeasures: Stopping existing tracks and closing WebRTC peers works for the stream currently stored, but cannot stop the stream returned later. The device selector is not disabled during acquisition, and no operation generation, cancellation flag or post-await stopped-state check exists.

original_members.failure_scenario: An OBS slot switches from camera A to camera B. A's WebSocket closing handshake is delayed, while B establishes its video and sets the slot's srcObject. A's eventual onclose callback then clears that same video element, leaving B's healthy connection invisible.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Caster cameras opened before initial consent remain black after consent is granted unless the scene is reloaded or reassigned.

original_members.claim: Caster cameras opened before initial consent remain black after consent is granted unless the scene is reloaded or reassigned.
original_members.failure_scenario: Assign a newly created camera to the live scene and open OBS before its owner first grants consent. The subscriber is rejected and its WebSocket closes. The owner then successfully publishes using the same camera ID, but OBS never reconnects and continues showing a black slot.
original_members.evidence: NativeCamera.connect() only resets the peer on WebSocket closure. setCamera() at line 9 creates a connection only when nativeIds[index] changes. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/caster_overlay.rs:600-644, subscribers without consent receive not-available and the socket handler returns; publisher authentication subsequently enables consent. The fixed-commit schema snapshot confirms consent_enabled defaults to false. All assigned source files matched review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
original_members.expected_behavior: A scene already configured for a camera should display that camera once its owner grants consent and starts publishing, without requiring camera reassignment or an OBS reload.
original_members.countermeasures: The consent guard correctly prevents premature access. Scene polling every two seconds does not repair the closed connection because the camera ID remains unchanged. publisher-ready notifications reach only subscribers already registered in the room, not the rejected subscriber.

original_members.claim: An unchanged native camera is never reconnected after its signaling socket closes.
original_members.failure_scenario: An OBS scene selects a newly created camera before its owner first enables consent. The subscriber receives not-available and its WebSocket closes. When the owner subsequently releases that camera, the scene remains black indefinitely despite successful two-second scene refreshes. The same failure occurs after a temporary signaling disconnection or dashboard service restart with the camera ID unchanged.
original_members.evidence: NativeCamera.connect on line 7 only resets the peer on close and never reconnects. setCamera line 9 creates a NativeCamera only when nativeIds[index] differs from cameraId; closing the socket does not clear that cached ID. refresh line 15 polls scene data but therefore cannot repair the connection. caster_overlay.rs lines 640-644 returns after rejecting unavailable subscribers. The admin editor lines 564-580 permits selecting cameras labeled not yet released.
original_members.expected_behavior: An assigned camera must become viewable when its owner releases it, and scene polling must not permanently retain a dead connection for the same camera ID. The publisher path at caster_overlay.rs lines 667-682 explicitly supports notifying already present subscribers when publishing starts.
original_members.countermeasures: Changing the selected camera ID or reloading the entire browser source recreates the connection. A publisher reconnect can notify subscribers whose signaling sockets remain open, but cannot notify the rejected or disconnected socket in this scenario. Neither the scene refresh nor publisher-ready provides a reconnect path.

original_members.claim: An initially unavailable assigned camera never connects when its publisher subsequently starts.
original_members.failure_scenario: An administrator assigns a newly created camera before its owner grants consent. The running overlay makes one subscriber connection, receives not-available and closes. The owner subsequently starts publishing, but the overlay keeps the same cameraId and never opens another subscriber connection, so that slot remains blank until reload or reassignment.
original_members.evidence: In the anchored file, line 7 resets peer state on not-available and WebSocket closure without reconnecting. Line 9 creates NativeCamera only when nativeIds changes and retains that ID after failure. Line 15 polls the scene every two seconds but does not inspect connection state. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/caster_overlay.rs:640-644 rejects the first subscriber and returns; it is never registered for later publisher notifications.
original_members.expected_behavior: An assigned live camera should become visible when its owner starts publishing. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/bot/admin_dashboard/src/pages/content/CasterOverlay.tsx:564-579 explicitly permits selecting cameras labelled not yet enabled, and lines 711-713 describe one persistent OBS source for the scene.
original_members.countermeasures: The server notifies subscribers when publishers join, but the rejected subscriber was never inserted into the room. Periodic scene refresh is serialized correctly, yet unchanged cameraId suppresses reconstruction. No retry or connection-state invalidation is present.

original_members.evidence: The start handler at line 21 calls openMedia() before connect() and disables Start. The auth-error branch at line 18 calls closeAll(), which only closes peers and the WebSocket at line 12. It neither stops stream tracks nor restores controls. Stop starts disabled in line 3 and is enabled only on ready. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/caster_overlay.rs:477-485 still serves existing revoked camera pages, while lines 586-632 reject their publisher authentication.

original_members.claim: Rejected camera authentication leaves camera capture active while Stop remains disabled.
original_members.failure_scenario: A user opens an old invitation for a revoked camera, accepts camera access and clicks Start. openMedia successfully starts capture before the server rejects authentication. The error path closes peers and the WebSocket but leaves stream and preview active. Because ready was never received, Stop remains disabled, so capture continues until the tab closes or another start attempt replaces the stream.
original_members.evidence: The camera page permits existing revoked camera records at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/caster_overlay.rs:470-498, while publisher_authorized rejects revoked records at lines 586-598. In the camera HTML, line 14 acquires media, line 21 starts it before authentication and disables Start, and line 18 handles auth-error through closeAll. closeAll at line 12 does not stop media tracks. Stop starts disabled and is enabled only by ready.
original_members.expected_behavior: The existing Stop, successful revoke and unload paths stop media tracks. Capture after failed publication should either have an available stop control or be released. Whether local preview is deliberately intended to remain active after rejection is not explicitly contracted, so this remains C.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Steam lookup failures are returned as successful caster context with missing account IDs.

original_members.claim: Steam lookup failures are returned as successful caster context with missing account IDs.
original_members.failure_scenario: The tournament service successfully returns players who have verified Steam links, but the Steam-link SELECT fails, for example with a transient database timeout. The endpoint returns available=true and source=turnier+steam while every player's Steam identity is null. An admin selecting and publishing such a team saves the missing identities and loses those players from the observer selector.
original_members.evidence: steam_links_for_discord lines 844-855 silently converts a failed SELECT into an empty map. context_handler lines 941-964 then fills steamId64/accountId from that map and unconditionally reports available=true. The editor's toSceneTeam at lines 58-68 copies these nulls, setTeam at lines 242-246 replaces the selected team, and observerCandidates at lines 309-311 excludes players without numeric accountId.
original_members.expected_behavior: Distinguish failed Steam enrichment from genuinely unlinked players before presenting combined-source context or replacing identities. Whether this should fail the endpoint or explicitly report degraded availability is unspecified, so this remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: Tournament request and JSON failures are logged and explicitly reported as unavailable. Optional Steam enrichment may intentionally be best-effort, and administrators must explicitly select and publish a team before stored context changes. There is no automatic overwrite from merely loading the context.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A slow camera subscriber permits unbounded signaling queues and dashboard-process memory exhaustion.

original_members.claim: A slow camera subscriber permits unbounded signaling queues and dashboard-process memory exhaustion.
original_members.failure_scenario: For a consent-enabled camera, an attacker opens two subscriber WebSockets with an accepted Origin header. Each ready message reveals that connection's peer ID. One connection stops reading; the other repeatedly sends valid signal envelopes with approximately 60 KiB of data targeting the first ID. The recipient eventually blocks in socket transmission while the sender continues adding messages to its unbounded queue, permitting process memory exhaustion.
original_members.evidence: Lines 600-607 require only camera consent for subscribers. Lines 648-652 allocate an unbounded channel. Lines 708-710 await sink.send without a deadline. Lines 750-784 forward arbitrary signal data to any peer in the room using synchronous UnboundedSender::send, with no queue bound, backpressure or message-rate limit. The public handler exposes active camera IDs at lines 285-312.
original_members.expected_behavior: Untrusted signaling traffic must not grow retained server memory without a bound when a recipient stops consuming. Slow recipients must cause bounded buffering, rejection or disconnection rather than process-wide exhaustion.
original_members.countermeasures: The 64 KiB input limit bounds individual signals, not their cumulative queue. Origin validation is not authentication for a native WebSocket client. Publisher-token checks do not apply to these subscribers. The public route and global middleware in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:166-224 and 2204-2271 provide no upgraded-stream queue or message-rate guard. original_members.claim: Uncapped public camera subscriptions exhaust the publisher's WebRTC peer resources.
original_members.failure_scenario: While an invited publisher is sharing its camera, an attacker repeatedly opens subscriber WebSockets for its publicly exposed camera ID and keeps them open without answering offers. Every connection induces another retained RTCPeerConnection in the publisher's browser. Exceeding the browser's finite peer-connection or ICE-resource capacity prevents subsequent legitimate viewers from establishing a connection and can exhaust publisher resources.
original_members.evidence: Lines 640-645 admit consent-enabled subscribers without a subscriber credential. Lines 684-695 insert every subscriber and notify the publisher, without a per-camera limit. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/caster_camera.html:16-18, each subscriber-joined event creates a peer, attaches camera tracks and stores it in peers. There is no negotiation deadline; an unanswered offer need not enter failed, closed or disconnected state.
original_members.expected_behavior: Unauthenticated viewers must not be able to allocate arbitrarily many WebRTC peers inside an authenticated publisher's browser or prevent legitimate camera use by exhausting its peer capacity.
original_members.countermeasures: MAX_CASTERS limits scene roster entries, not subscribers or peer connections. Existing cleanup requires subscriber-left or a terminal connection state; an attacker can keep its signaling socket open and never answer. The Origin allowlist is forgeable by a native client. The separate OBS connection cap in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/obs/bus.rs:272-301 does not cover these camera rooms.

original_members.claim: Administrative camera revocation leaves normal subscriber WebSockets open indefinitely.
original_members.failure_scenario: An administrator revokes a camera while its OBS caster overlay remains open. disconnect_camera removes the room and sends revoked, but the normal NativeCamera client only resets its WebRTC peer and keeps the WebSocket open. resolved_candidate_group.claim: Anonymous subscribers can receive a camera feed after that camera has been removed from the active caster scene.

original_members.claim: Anonymous subscribers can receive a camera feed after that camera has been removed from the active caster scene.
original_members.failure_scenario: A visitor records a cameraId while it appears in the public scene. An administrator later removes that camera from the selected slots while its owner leaves the publishing page open. The visitor opens another subscriber WebSocket with the retained cameraId from the public website. Consent remains true, so the server admits the subscriber and the owner page automatically negotiates and transmits the live camera even though it is no longer selected.
original_members.evidence: caster_overlay.rs:285-301 publishes selected camera IDs. Saving a new scene at lines 253-282 does not disconnect cameras or change consent. subscriber_authorized at lines 600-608 checks only consent_enabled and revoked_at, not scene membership or viewer identity. Lines 684-695 notify the publisher about the subscriber, and caster_camera.html:16-18 automatically offers its media. lib.rs:184-190 registers the socket in the public router.
original_members.expected_behavior: caster_camera.html:3 describes transmission to the active caster scene, and line 18 says transmission occurs only when the caster scene requests it. However, privileged previews also use this subscriber path for unsaved scenes. Whether consent deliberately permits arbitrary public viewing outside selected slots is not conclusively specified, so this remains C pending clarification rather than an automatic authorization change.
original_members.countermeasures: Camera IDs are random, but selected IDs have already been publicly disclosed. The Origin allowlist blocks unrelated browser origins, not visitors running a subscriber on the permitted public website. Administrative scene writes and publish-token checks remain protected. The actual subscriber path has no active-scene or privileged-preview distinction, and no continuing scene-membership check.

findings.title_de: Fehlgeschlagener Iconrefresh überschreibt erfolgreichen Cache
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Fehlgeschlagener Iconrefresh überschreibt erfolgreichen Cache.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A concurrent failed hero-icon refresh overwrites a successful cache and suppresses icons for six hours.

original_members.claim: A concurrent failed hero-icon refresh overwrites a successful cache and suppresses icons for six hours.
original_members.failure_scenario: The global hero cache is cold or expired. Two valid overlay requests with different streamer or mode keys both pass the freshness check and start fetching assets. Request A succeeds and installs populated icons. Request B subsequently times out or receives a non-2xx response, producing an empty map, then unconditionally replaces A's successful cache and resets fetched_at. Subsequent overlay computations return that empty map for six hours, so recent-match and most-played hero images disappear despite a completed successful refresh.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, the primary file matches the worktree. Lines 243-250 release the cache lock before the fetch at 252. Lines 254-257 publish every result without rechecking whether another request installed fresh data. Lines 272-273 convert decoding, HTTP and transport failures into an empty map. HERO_ASSETS_TTL is six hours at line 34; lines 245-247 then reuse the overwritten empty map. Different overlay keys are independent at lines 390-395 and each invokes hero_icon_map at lines 426-432. The public route is registered at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:145-161 and merged into the production router at 2204. No execution or network probes were performed.
original_members.expected_behavior: A successfully refreshed hero map should remain reusable for its six-hour freshness interval rather than being erased by an overlapping failed refresh that started against the previous cache state. The cache contract and freshness branch are documented and implemented at lines 239-249; tests at lines 1662-1677 verify populated icon reuse without another assets fetch.
original_members.countermeasures: The mutex prevents simultaneous memory mutation but covers neither the asynchronous fetch nor freshness revalidation at publication. OverlayCache single-flight protection applies only to identical login|mode keys, not the shared hero cache. HTTP timeouts limit fetch duration but do not prevent this overwrite. Letter-tile fallback keeps rendering functional, but it does not preserve the successful icon data. The primary file contains the only HeroIconCache publication path; its cache tests cover sequential reuse, not this overlapping success/failure interleaving.

findings.title_de: Ein fehlender Steam-Matchwert verwirft gesamte Historie
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Ein fehlender Steam-Matchwert verwirft gesamte Historie.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A null timestamp or KDA field in one Steam match discards the overlay's entire match history.

original_members.claim: A null timestamp or KDA field in one Steam match discards the overlay's entire match history.
original_members.failure_scenario: A linked streamer's HTTP 200 match history contains valid scored matches plus one record with player_kills:null, player_deaths:null, player_assists:null, or start_time:null. Even an unscored record with these nulls makes deserialization of the whole SteamMatchHistory fail. The overlay then loses winrate, streak, recent games, daily results and all other match-derived modules despite usable history.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, overlay.rs:140-147 declares these fields as i64 with serde(default); response.json failure at 559-564 returns None, and 437-451 consequently drops all history. The upstream contract is concrete: /home/nathanael/repos/Deadlock-Steam-Bot/rust/crates/deadlock-proto/protos/deadlock/citadel_gcmessages_client.proto:919-924 declares optional uint32 timestamp and KDA fields. /home/nathanael/repos/Deadlock-Steam-Bot/rust/crates/steam-core/src/task/handlers/gc.rs:610-629 serializes their Option values directly, producing JSON null for absent fields. The upstream HTTP route passes the match objects through at /home/nathanael/repos/Deadlock-Steam-Bot/rust/crates/steam-web/src/routes/rank.rs:438-446. These upstream sources were unchanged against HEAD 4a5c4ff3a38e9a4bf7fe2dbf8de882b00700233d.
original_members.expected_behavior: Accept the upstream's optional numeric fields without discarding otherwise usable matches. The overlay already defaults omitted fields, and the sibling consumer /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-chat/src/stats.rs:62-76 correctly uses Option<i64> for KDA.
original_members.countermeasures: HTTP status checking and decode-error logging work, but provide no per-record recovery. serde(default) handles missing properties, not explicit null. The not_scored filter at overlay.rs:666-673 runs only after the entire response has decoded, so it cannot exclude the offending unscored record first. The sibling Option-based consumer does not share this defect.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The overlay reports available history and a zero daily balance for Steam friendship errors.

original_members.claim: The overlay reports available history and a zero daily balance for Steam friendship errors.
original_members.failure_scenario: A streamer has a Discord identity and a Steam link but lacks verified Steam friendship. The Steam endpoint returns HTTP 200 with linked:true, matches:[], stale:true, updated_at:null and error:"steam_friend_required". The overlay treats that failure as available history and displays HEUTE 0-0 even though it could not obtain the player's matches.
original_members.evidence: The upstream response exists at /home/nathanael/repos/Deadlock-Steam-Bot/rust/crates/steam-web/src/routes/rank.rs:298-304, unchanged against upstream HEAD 4a5c4ff3a38e9a4bf7fe2dbf8de882b00700233d. In the fixed review source, overlay.rs:120-130 has no error field; 437 rejects only linked:false. Lines 448-450 calculate the daily summary for any remaining response, 474 sets history_available:true, and 769-794 returns a zero summary for an empty list. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/overlay.html:794-805 renders those numbers as today's balance.
original_members.expected_behavior: An explicit failure to retrieve history must not become available history or a factual zero-match result. Preserve the existing distinction: unavailable history produces null daily fields, whereas a successful empty history produces zeroes.
original_members.countermeasures: Non-2xx responses, decode failures and linked:false are rejected. None catches this valid HTTP 200 error response with linked:true. history_stale is returned, but the rendering branch checks only whether daily fields are numeric and therefore still displays the fabricated balance.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: One failed hero-assets refresh suppresses all hero icons for six hours.

original_members.claim: One failed hero-assets refresh suppresses all hero icons for six hours.
original_members.failure_scenario: The hero cache expires while the assets API briefly times out or returns an error. The API recovers immediately afterward, but the empty map is treated as freshly fetched for six hours. A previously populated icon map is also replaced, so every overlay uses fallback tiles throughout that interval.
original_members.evidence: overlay.rs:264-274 converts request, status and decoding failures to an empty map. Lines 252-257 unconditionally replace the map and record Instant::now(); 245-247 then return it until HERO_ASSETS_TTL, defined as six hours at line 34. The 30-second overlay-data cache does not invalidate this separate hero cache.
original_members.expected_behavior: Fallback rendering is explicitly intended at overlay.rs:239-241. Whether failed refreshes should preserve previous icons or use a shorter retry interval is not specified, so this recovery-policy issue is C rather than an automatic fix.
original_members.countermeasures: The five-second request timeout and fallback tiles keep the overlay usable. They do not restore icons after the upstream recovers. Successful and failed refreshes currently share the same six-hour freshness policy; the documented best-effort fallback prevents claiming an unequivocal B contract.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A stalled identity query leaves same-key overlay requests waiting without an application deadline.

original_members.claim: A stalled identity query leaves same-key overlay requests waiting without an application deadline.
original_members.failure_scenario: On a database connection with statement_timeout=0, another transaction holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_streamers or twitch_streamer_identities. A cache-miss overlay request acquires a connection and blocks in the identity SELECT. Subsequent requests for the same login and mode wait on its inflight notification until the lock is released or an external layer cancels requests. The OBS template continues initiating polls every 20 seconds, leaving refreshes pending and accumulating outstanding work during the stall.
original_members.evidence: At fixed review SHA, overlay.rs:400 awaits identity resolution before creating the HTTP client; 521-533 executes the SELECT without timeout wrapping. Followers await notification at 355-365 without their own deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 constructs the pool with tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:10-11 selects read_only=false; its 44-53 bounds acquisition and configures statement_timeout only for read-only pools. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/overlay.html:1104-1122 contains neither fetch cancellation nor a pending-poll guard. Production router composition and serving contain no whole-request timeout.
original_members.expected_behavior: A prolonged identity-resolution failure should eventually reach the existing best-effort failure response rather than pinning later overlay refreshes. No explicit database or whole-request deadline is documented for this overlay, so the required timeout policy remains uncertain and this is classified C.
original_members.countermeasures: Pool acquisition/connect deadlines do not cover a statement already executing. The 8-second Steam and 5-second asset timeouts start after identity resolution and cannot bound this wait. InflightGuard cleans up when the leader is dropped, but does not initiate cancellation. A database role/server statement timeout or reverse-proxy timeout could limit the scenario; live settings were not inspected. The two tracked runtime-role scripts checked contain no statement_timeout setting. The neighboring streamer-comparison handler explicitly shares a 15-second deadline across cache waiting and database work, but that protection is not applied to overlay.

findings.title_de: Öffentliche Overlayanfragen erzeugen unbegrenzt Cacheeinträge
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Öffentliche Overlayanfragen erzeugen unbegrenzt Cacheeinträge.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Unauthenticated overlay requests can exhaust dashboard memory by creating cache entries that are never evicted.

original_members.claim: Unauthenticated overlay requests can exhaust dashboard memory by creating cache entries that are never evicted.
original_members.failure_scenario: An unauthenticated client repeatedly requests GET /twitch/api/v2/public/overlay with distinct nonexistent streamer values. Each completed request permanently retains its attacker-controlled key and {"ok":false} response. Continuing with new values, even across many 30-second TTL periods, grows process memory without a bound until the dashboard exhausts memory and becomes unavailable.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, overlay.rs:294-299 accepts any nonempty trimmed lowercase string; 390-395 uses it as the singleton cache key; 399-406 returns ok:false for nonexistent identities; 374-381 caches that result unconditionally. Lines 345-353 check freshness only for the requested key and never remove expired entries. The complete primary file contains no production eviction or cardinality limit; entries.clear() at 865 is test-only. Public registration is lib.rs:145-161, and the merged router layers at 2204-2314 do not impose an overlay request limit. Production wiring at main.rs:476-608 adds extensions and starts the server without a cache bound. The existing unknown-streamer test at overlay.rs:1680-1694 confirms the accepted negative-response path.
original_members.expected_behavior: An anonymous public request must not create permanent, unbounded process state. The documented 30-second per-login cache must expire or otherwise bound retained entries, including failed lookups.
original_members.countermeasures: Single-flight deduplication applies only to identical keys; the TTL prevents serving stale values but does not reclaim memory. Restricting mode to four values does not restrict streamer cardinality. Bound SQL parameters prevent injection, and missing identities avoid Steam requests, but neither prevents negative-cache insertion. Authentication is intentionally absent for this public endpoint. HOST_ROUTING_CONTRACT.md:17-22 documents public-host access to /twitch/*; live proxy configuration was not inspected. Any finite proxy rate limit would slow accumulation rather than bound permanent retention. A targeted neighboring-cache check found StreamerComparisonCache uses three fixed slots, so that protection does not cover OverlayCache.

original_members.claim: Unauthenticated overlay requests permanently retain arbitrary streamer keys, enabling process-memory exhaustion.
original_members.failure_scenario: With a healthy database, repeatedly request GET /twitch/api/v2/public/overlay?streamer=<distinct-nonexistent-name>. Every request returns ok:false but permanently adds another attacker-controlled key and JSON value to the process-global cache. Long nonexistent names amplify retained memory because no login-length validation exists. Expiration after 30 seconds and cessation of requests do not release these entries. Sustained requests can exhaust the dashboard process's memory without any registered streamer account.

Lines 375-381 cache those results unconditionally. Lines 349-353 check freshness but never delete stale entries; the only entries.clear() is test-only at 862-867. The route is public at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:145-161. Production composition at that file's 2204-2271 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:476-524 adds no authentication or cache eviction for this handler. The unknown-streamer response path is explicitly covered by overlay.rs:1680-1693.
original_members.expected_behavior: A public, attacker-keyed cache must bound retained memory rather than retain every historical request key for the process lifetime. Expiration or capacity enforcement can preserve the documented 30-second response caching and existing ok:false behavior.
original_members.countermeasures: Case normalization merges spelling variants and mode normalization limits modes to four, but neither bounds distinct streamer names. findings.title_de: Langsamer Anbieterrefresh verliert neue Zugänge nach Transaktionsablauf
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Langsamer Anbieterrefresh verliert neue Zugänge nach Transaktionsablauf.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Slow Kick/YouTube refresh responses lose newly issued credentials because the database transaction expires before the refresh deadline.

original_members.claim: Slow Kick/YouTube refresh responses lose newly issued credentials because the database transaction expires before the refresh deadline.
original_members.failure_scenario: An expiring Kick connection is refreshed by the background sweep. Its provider returns a successful response containing a new access/refresh pair after 31 seconds. PostgreSQL has already terminated the transaction after 30 idle seconds while the code awaited HTTP. The subsequent upsert fails, leaving the previous credentials stored despite completion before the outer 35-second deadline. If the provider rotated the refresh credential, the next attempt uses the invalid old value and marks the connection as requiring another login.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/platform_store.rs:339-344 sets a 35-second operation deadline; :359 opens the shared transaction; :391 awaits the provider without executing SQL; :422-424 only then writes and commits the new pair. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/auth_writer.rs:467-469 configures idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='30s'. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_oauth.rs:137-155 uses reqwest::Client::new() without a request timeout. Both real platform refresh implementations call this helper at :218-229 and :441-452. The background caller is /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2273-2286.
original_members.expected_behavior: A successful refresh that completes within the operation's allowed time must retain its transaction and persist the returned credentials atomically. The existing contract test at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/platform_store.rs:636-669 explicitly requires the new access and refresh values to be stored.
original_members.countermeasures: The UID advisory lock, refresh advisory lock and row lock prevent ordinary concurrent writers, but PostgreSQL releases them when it terminates the idle transaction. The 35-second outer timeout is later than the 30-second database timeout. Statement and lock timeouts do not bound the HTTP await. The shared Twitch refresher has a separate 10-second HTTP timeout, but the Kick and YouTube paths do not use it. Both foreign-platform branches share this defect; existing store tests return immediately and do not cover this timing window.

findings.title_de: Twitch-Broker gibt nach Refreshfehler abgelaufenen Zugang mit HTTP 200 aus
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Twitch-Broker gibt nach Refreshfehler abgelaufenen Zugang mit HTTP 200 aus.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The Twitch token broker can return HTTP 200 with an already expired token after a slow failed refresh.

original_members.claim: The Twitch token broker can return HTTP 200 with an already expired token after a slow failed refresh.
original_members.failure_scenario: A standard internal request starts at t0 with a readable Twitch token expiring at t0+1 second. The refresh endpoint takes two seconds and returns a transient error. The shared refresher returns Skipped without changing the grant. The broker rereads it, compares its expiry against t0 rather than the current time, and returns the now-expired token successfully.
original_members.evidence: platform_token.rs:306-323 treats every non-Blacklisted successful refresher outcome as eligible for rereading; 325-345 checks expiry using the original jetzt. The HTTP handler captures that time before awaiting at 691-693. At the fixed review SHA, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/token_refresher.rs:315-338 returns Ok(Skipped) for InvalidClient or Other errors after awaiting the provider. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/token_store.rs:145-191 rereads and decodes the stored expiry without comparing it to the current clock.
original_members.expected_behavior: The function promises a usable token, and platform_token.rs:339-343 explicitly rejects tokens that remain expired after refresh. That decision must use the time after the awaited refresh and reread, not the request's start time.
original_members.countermeasures: The 10-second provider timeout and 35-second overall refresh timeout allow this two-second scenario. needs_reauth and disconnect checks do not reject a transiently failed grant. The publish-specific owner verification may reject it later, but ordinary requests do not execute that verification. The foreign-platform post-refresh expiry check at 505 similarly uses the original timestamp.

findings.title_de: Twitch-Snapshot wartet außerhalb Refreshfrist auf DB
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Twitch-Snapshot wartet außerhalb Refreshfrist auf DB.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Twitch token snapshot reads can wait indefinitely outside the refresh timeout and exhaust the dashboard database pool.

original_members.claim: Twitch token snapshot reads can wait indefinitely outside the refresh timeout and exhaust the dashboard database pool.
original_members.failure_scenario: An established PostgreSQL backend stops returning the token snapshot, for example while an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table lock remains held without a server-side statement deadline. Each authorized token request remains pending with an acquired connection. Repeating this up to the configured pool size exhausts the shared dashboard pool; later requests fail acquisition while the original handlers remain stuck. The same unbounded read occurs after refresh at line 325.
original_members.evidence: platform_token.rs:279 and :325 await load_decrypted_with_scopes without a deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/token_store.rs:145-150 directly awaits fetch_optional. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 uses tb_db::connect; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:41-55 configures acquisition deadlines but installs statement_timeout only for connect_readonly, not this pool. The internal route is registered at tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:1941-1960 and has no execution-timeout layer. Assigned sources and supporting Rust sources were checked against the fixed review SHA without drift.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled token lookup should terminate with TokenFehler::NichtLieferbar and the existing 502 response instead of indefinitely retaining a request and shared pool capacity. The error mapping already exists at platform_token.rs:282-285 and :619-623.
original_members.countermeasures: Loopback and internal authentication limit callers but do not bound an accepted request. RaidTokenRefresher has a 35-second deadline, but it starts only after the first snapshot and ends before the second. Helix HTTP deadlines do not cover these database reads. The readonly pool's 20-second statement timeout is not used here; the checked runtime-role SQL resets role settings and adds no execution deadline. Deployment-specific PostgreSQL settings were not inspected. Targeted twins are platform_store.rs:212-222 (connection status) and :311-323 (due-list query), also unbounded before any per-token refresh deadline.

findings.title_de: Stockende Kick-Refreshs verzögern gesunde YouTube-Konten
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Stockende Kick-Refreshs verzögern gesunde YouTube-Konten.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Serial proactive refresh allows stalled Kick accounts to delay healthy YouTube accounts past token expiry.

original_members.claim: Serial proactive refresh allows stalled Kick accounts to delay healthy YouTube accounts past token expiry.
original_members.failure_scenario: At one sweep, twenty lower-ID Kick connections and a higher-ID YouTube connection are due. The YouTube token expires in ten minutes. Each Kick refresh stalls until its 35-second deadline, so the YouTube refresh starts approximately 700 seconds later, after its token has expired. Subsequent five-minute scheduler ticks cannot refresh it concurrently because the same scheduler task is still awaiting this batch.
original_members.evidence: platform_store.rs:317-323 fetches all due connections ordered by streamer_id and platform. platform_token.rs:357-367 awaits each refresh serially. platform_store.rs:339-344 permits 35 seconds per entry. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_oauth.rs:137-155 creates an HTTP client without a request deadline, so a stalled Kick request can consume that entire outer deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:2276-2296 runs both providers in one awaited batch every 300 seconds. The platform_connections migration has no global connection-count limit.
original_members.expected_behavior: Proactive refresh should not let an unavailable provider prevent a healthy provider's already-due tokens from being renewed before their ten-minute expiry window closes. Choosing provider isolation, bounded concurrency, or scheduling budgets is a design decision, so this remains C.
original_members.countermeasures: The 35-second per-entry timeout prevents one permanent HTTP stall, but cumulative batch time is unbounded by connection count. MissedTickBehavior::Delay does not interrupt or parallelize the running batch. On-demand refresh in platform_token.rs:476-515 can recover a YouTube connection if a consumer requests a token independently; therefore universal relay failure is not claimed. The demonstrated failure is loss of timely proactive refresh for otherwise healthy accounts.

findings.title_de: YouTube-Uplink deutet Social-State als andere Twitch-ID
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: YouTube-Uplink deutet Social-State als andere Twitch-ID.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The YouTube Uplink callback accepts Social Studio states and interprets numeric Twitch logins as another user's Twitch ID.

original_members.claim: The YouTube Uplink callback accepts Social Studio states and interprets numeric Twitch logins as another user's Twitch ID.
original_members.failure_scenario: With both Google flows configured, an authorized Social Studio user has Twitch login '12345678' and actual Twitch ID '87654321'. Social authorization stores streamer_login='12345678', twitch_user_id='87654321', platform='youtube'. resolved_candidate_group.claim: An acknowledged missing relay destination prevents platform disconnection and leaves it permanently pending.

original_members.claim: An acknowledged missing relay destination prevents platform disconnection and leaves it permanently pending.
original_members.failure_scenario: A YouTube connection is saved successfully but has no live stream target, which youtube_callback_kern explicitly permits. Disconnect receives a successful relay response with the requested connection_generation and deleted=false because no destination exists. HttpRelayZiele returns Ok(false), but plattform_trennen reports RelayFehler before deleting the connection. Repeated attempts reuse the pending generation and encounter the same absent destination, so they cannot finish disconnecting.
original_members.evidence: Primary lines 473-500 save connections even when ziel returns None. Lines 709-730 reserve disconnect state and require Ok(true) from relay deletion before delete_fenced. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/uplink.rs:1228-1234 explicitly documents false as 'there was no target'; lines 1297-1320 return the deleted boolean after validating the generation. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/target_generation.rs:102-115 preserves the pending generation on retries. The sibling Twitch disconnect repeats the same check at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/uplink.rs:1507-1511.
original_members.expected_behavior: A generation-confirmed deletion response indicating that the target is already absent should complete local disconnection. Absence is a documented successful relay result, not a transport failure; missing targets are legitimate after an otherwise successful connection.
original_members.countermeasures: HttpRelayZiele correctly rejects stale or malformed generation acknowledgements before returning Ok(false), so this scenario is not an unconfirmed deletion. Local completion is skipped entirely. The response mapping asks the user to retry, but retries retain the same pending state. The existing no-connection-row test uses a fake returning true and therefore does not cover an absent relay target.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: YouTube stream selection ignores pagination and can choose a custom stream instead of the default stream.

original_members.claim: YouTube stream selection ignores pagination and can choose a custom stream instead of the default stream.
original_members.failure_scenario: YouTube liveStreams.list returns a first page containing custom streams and a nextPageToken; the account's default stream is on a later page. ziel searches only the first page, falls back to its first custom stream, and returns that stream's key. The callback or stream-key refresh then installs the wrong target instead of the default stream.
original_members.evidence: Primary lines 490-505 make one list request without pageToken, search only antwort.items and immediately fall back to its first item. YtLiveStreamsAntwort at lines 547-550 has no nextPageToken field. The explicit contract test google_ziel_waehlt_default_stream at lines 709-728 requires selection of the default stream over an earlier custom stream. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_connect.rs:479-488 and 543-577 install the returned key without further stream selection.
original_members.expected_behavior: The default stream must take precedence over custom streams across the account's paginated stream list. Falling back to a custom stream is appropriate only after establishing that no default stream exists.
original_members.countermeasures: api_get deserializes a single response and does not paginate. Neither callback nor stream-key refresh checks whether a later page contains the default stream. findings.title_de: Großer Anbieterablaufwert löst OAuth-Callback-Panic aus
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Großer Anbieterablaufwert löst OAuth-Callback-Panic aus.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Provider-controlled expires_in can panic in Kick and YouTube OAuth callbacks.

original_members.claim: Provider-controlled expires_in can panic in Kick and YouTube OAuth callbacks.
original_members.failure_scenario: With a valid callback state, the provider returns HTTP 200 with a nonempty access_token and expires_in=9223372036854775807; the account lookup succeeds. oauth_expires_at calls Chrono's panicking Duration::seconds constructor. The callback panics instead of returning its error redirect, after its one-use OAuth state has already been deleted. Replaying the callback cannot recover the operation.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_oauth.rs:103-126 accepts expires_in as unrestricted i64; lines 137-162 validate only access_token before returning it. The callback expiry calculation is reached at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_connect.rs:419 and :470. Pinned Chrono 0.4.45 explicitly panics above i64::MAX/1000 seconds, confirmed by the read source and existing panic test at /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/chrono-0.4.45/src/time_delta.rs:206-228 and :791-795. Twin unchecked arithmetic occurs in platform refresh at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/platform_token.rs:538-544.
original_members.expected_behavior: Unrepresentable expiry values should produce an ordinary OAuth error, not a panic. The existing contract returns Result from token_request and both callback cores, with explicit invalid-response errors and callback failure redirects.
original_members.countermeasures: expires_in.max(0) handles negative values only. Access-token validation, account lookup, callback rate limits, and generation fencing do not bound expiry. Duration construction can panic before Result handling; DateTime addition also uses a panicking overflow path. No builds or tests were run.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Stream-key generation-check database errors are incorrectly reported as no connection.

original_members.claim: Stream-key generation-check database errors are incorrectly reported as no connection.
original_members.failure_scenario: A connected Kick or YouTube account has valid credentials. The initial token read and provider stream-key lookup succeed, but the subsequent generation snapshot fails or times out because of a transient database or pool failure. The function discards Err and returns KeineVerbindung. The HTTP endpoint responds 409 and tells the user to connect first, although the connection still exists.
original_members.evidence: The matches!(check_current(...).await, Ok(true)) condition at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_connect.rs:564-574 merges Ok(false) and Err. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/target_generation.rs:37-64 shows that check_current propagates SQL errors and its 10-second timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/uplink.rs:1646-1656 forwards this result; lines 1674-1688 map KeineVerbindung to the incorrect 409 connection message and Fehlgeschlagen to a retryable failure. An identical twin is present at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/uplink.rs:1439-1449.
original_members.expected_behavior: Ok(false) can mean the connection is no longer current, but a database error should return Fehlgeschlagen. This distinction is already implemented for earlier token-storage failures at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/platform_token.rs:461-467 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_connect.rs:522-529.
original_members.countermeasures: Failing closed prevents an unsafe relay update and should remain intact. Earlier database checks catch an outage already present at token retrieval, but do not prevent a failure arising during the later provider request. No caller restores the lost error distinction, and no connection deletion is needed for this scenario.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Plattformcallbacks warten unbefristet auf Upstream.
