resolved_candidate_group.claim: Kick and YouTube connection callbacks and stream-key requests can wait indefinitely for upstream HTTP responses.

original_members.claim: Kick and YouTube connection callbacks and stream-key requests can wait indefinitely for upstream HTTP responses.
original_members.failure_scenario: A legitimate callback with an unexpired state reaches the token endpoint, or an authenticated stream-key request reaches the account API. The upstream accepts the connection but never finishes its response while the caller keeps its connection open. The handler never returns its error redirect or 502 response and retains its task and outbound connection indefinitely. Repeated requests accumulate pending work.
original_members.evidence: Verified at fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. token_request constructs an unconfigured reqwest::Client at lines 137-156; api_get repeats this at lines 302-323. The pinned reqwest 0.12.28 implementation defaults connect_timeout, read_timeout and timeout to None (/home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/reqwest-0.12.28/src/async_impl/client.rs:299-314). /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_connect.rs:401-408,452-459,479,535-547 directly await these requests without a deadline. Its callback handlers provide error redirects at lines 633-636 and 686-689; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/uplink.rs:1629-1688 maps failed stream-key retrieval to 502.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled external service must terminate the connection attempt with the existing failure response rather than leave the HTTP operation pending indefinitely. Adding a finite outbound deadline preserves the existing success and failure contracts.
original_members.countermeasures: OAuth state validation and the callback rate limit restrict entry, not request duration. The inspected router and server layers supply no request deadline. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/platform_store.rs:339-344 imposes a 35-second deadline on token refresh, so refresh is not claimed to hang indefinitely. The relay client has a 10-second deadline, but this does not cover earlier provider calls. Production proxy configuration was not inspected; the defect is established in the directly reachable Rust handler.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Verlassene Kick-/YouTube-States bleiben nach Ablauf erhalten.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Abandoned Kick and YouTube connection states survive expiration without a periodic cleanup path in the inspected Rust implementation.

original_members.claim: Abandoned Kick and YouTube connection states survive expiration without a periodic cleanup path in the inspected Rust implementation.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated partner repeatedly starts a connection and abandons or declines the provider dialog. Each start inserts a fresh state row. After ten minutes those rows are unusable but remain stored. In a deployment without an external cleanup job, continued abandoned attempts eventually exhaust finite database storage and cause subsequent state inserts and other database writes to fail.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, persist_connect_state inserts a new random-keyed row with a 600-second expiry at lines 159-183; both start handlers invoke it. consume_connect_state only deletes rows with expires_at > now at lines 204-213, so even retrying an expired state cannot reclaim it. Provider-declined callbacks return before consuming state at lines 600-603 and 646-649. The expiry test at lines 971-996 only checks that an expired state is rejected. The runtime cleanup found in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/state_store.rs:189-199 deletes only platform twitch_raid. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260930220200_token_storage.sql:14-16 removes old rows once during migration, not periodically.
original_members.expected_behavior: Transient, expired connection states need bounded retention if the application owns their cleanup. The intended retention age and ownership are not specified, so this remains C rather than an automatic fix.
original_members.countermeasures: The 30-requests-per-60-seconds IP limit slows accumulation but does not bound its lifetime. The expiry column and indexes enforce neither automatic deletion nor a row limit. Existing migration cleanup is one-time, and the inspected raid cleanup excludes these platforms. An independently configured database maintenance job could prevent storage exhaustion; no live database or scheduler inspection was permitted.

original.claim: Abandoned Kick and YouTube connection states survive expiration without a periodic cleanup path in the inspected Rust implementation.
original.failure_scenario: An authenticated partner repeatedly starts a connection and abandons or declines the provider dialog. Each start inserts a fresh state row. After ten minutes those rows are unusable but remain stored. In a deployment without an external cleanup job, continued abandoned attempts eventually exhaust finite database storage and cause subsequent state inserts and other database writes to fail.
original.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, persist_connect_state inserts a new random-keyed row with a 600-second expiry at lines 159-183; both start handlers invoke it. consume_connect_state only deletes rows with expires_at > now at lines 204-213, so even retrying an expired state cannot reclaim it. Provider-declined callbacks return before consuming state at lines 600-603 and 646-649. The expiry test at lines 971-996 only checks that an expired state is rejected. The runtime cleanup found in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/state_store.rs:189-199 deletes only platform twitch_raid. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260930220200_token_storage.sql:14-16 removes old rows once during migration, not periodically.
original.expected_behavior: Transient, expired connection states need bounded retention if the application owns their cleanup. The intended retention age and ownership are not specified, so this remains C rather than an automatic fix.
original.countermeasures: The 30-requests-per-60-seconds IP limit slows accumulation but does not bound its lifetime. The expiry column and indexes enforce neither automatic deletion nor a row limit. Existing migration cleanup is one-time, and the inspected raid cleanup excludes these platforms. An independently configured database maintenance job could prevent storage exhaustion; no live database or scheduler inspection was permitted.

findings.title_de: Plattform-OAuth bindet Abschluss nicht an startenden Browser
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Plattform-OAuth bindet Abschluss nicht an startenden Browser.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Kick and YouTube OAuth callbacks permit account-linking CSRF because state is not bound to the initiating browser or session.

original_members.claim: Kick and YouTube OAuth callbacks permit account-linking CSRF because state is not bound to the initiating browser or session.
original_members.failure_scenario: Authenticated partner A starts a new Kick or YouTube connection and sends the returned provider authorization URL to victim B. B approves using B's provider account within the ten-minute state lifetime. The callback accepts A's state from B's browser, including when B has no dashboard session or has a different session. B's access and refresh credentials are stored under A's Twitch ID, and B's stream destination is installed for A's relay identity. For Kick, the forwarded URL carries the valid challenge and the server supplies its stored verifier, so PKCE does not stop this transfer.
original_members.evidence: Static proof at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/plattform_connect.rs:138-232 persists and consumes platform, streamer ID, redirect and verifier but no browser/session binding. Start handlers at 254-345 return transferable authorization URLs without setting a binding cookie. Both callbacks at 595-692 consume state without comparing callback identity. The cores at 410-436 and 461-489 save the provider grant and relay target using state.streamer_id. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/lib.rs:700-732 registers both GET callbacks; its layers at 1003-1015 add only partner-status gating and write-method CSRF protection. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/platform_store.rs:128-157,243-280 encrypts and upserts credentials under the supplied streamer ID. The database primary key is (streamer_id, platform), as defined in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260827090000_platform_connections.sql:15-28.
original_members.expected_behavior: A provider grant must be attached only when the callback proves continuity with the browser/session that initiated the connection. Reject a missing or mismatched binding before consuming the state or exchanging the code. The existing per-streamer ownership contract is documented in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260827090000_platform_connections.sql:1-11.
original_members.countermeasures: Checked authenticated server-side Twitch identity at initiation, cryptographic state generation, hashed state lookup, platform restriction, expiry, atomic single-use consumption, Kick PKCE, encrypted credentials, generation fencing, rate limiting, and the internal token endpoint's authentication. These protect other boundaries but do not establish browser continuity. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/partner_gate.rs:140-173 passes unauthenticated requests and does not compare state ownership; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/csrf.rs:89-92 exempts GET. Generation fencing only rejects states predating a disconnect. Both provider flows are verified twins within this slice. No live exploit, network probe, or production proxy inspection was performed.

findings.title_de: Gespeicherte Message-ID bestätigt nicht eingereihtes Ereignis
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Gespeicherte Message-ID bestätigt nicht eingereihtes Ereignis.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A persisted MessageId claim can acknowledge a notification that was never enqueued.

original_members.claim: A persisted MessageId claim can acknowledge a notification that was never enqueued.
original_members.failure_scenario: A valid stream.online notification with message ID m-1 commits its MessageId guard. The process terminates before the inbox INSERT. After restart, Twitch retries m-1 within 600 seconds. dispatch returns duplicate success without enqueueing, and the webhook receiver returns HTTP 204. The event is permanently lost.
original_members.evidence: Static review at SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/guard.rs:122-138 commits the claim through PgPool independently of enqueue. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:715-735 claims and acknowledges duplicates before route; :810-812 inserts the core event later. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/webhook_receiver.rs:306-319 converts every successful dispatch, including duplicates, to HTTP 204.
original_members.expected_behavior: The durable core-event delivery contract in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:5-7 and :682-683 requires successful acceptance to preserve the event for processing; an unpersisted event must remain retryable.
original_members.countermeasures: The conditional guard upsert prevents simultaneous claims but does not make guard creation and inbox insertion atomic. The release at dispatch.rs:761-773 only handles returned errors, not process termination. Guard expiry cannot recover an event already acknowledged and never placed in the inbox.

original_members.claim: EventSub retries are acknowledged as duplicates after a crash between the MessageId claim and durable enqueue.
original_members.failure_scenario: A valid stream.online notification claims its persistent MessageId guard, then the process terminates before enqueue commits. After restart within 600 seconds, Twitch resends the same message. The guard rejects the claim, dispatch returns a successful duplicate, and the webhook returns HTTP 204 even though no processing-inbox entry exists. The same loss occurs if enqueue fails and the subsequent guard release also fails during a database outage.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, dispatch.rs:717-735 commits the guard before route; dispatch.rs:804-814 queues core events separately. guard.rs:122-138 executes the claim against the pool, without the enqueue transaction. dispatch.rs:763-771 only logs a failed release. webhook_receiver.rs:306-319 maps every successful DispatchOutcome, including duplicate, to 204. ProcessingInboxStore only contains jobs created by enqueue; it cannot recover an event never queued.
original_members.expected_behavior: A core notification must remain retryable until it is durably accepted. dispatch.rs:682-683 explicitly defines Err as failed acceptance requiring retry; dispatch.rs:793-814 defines durable enqueue as core-event acceptance.
original_members.countermeasures: Signature verification and readiness checks occur before dispatch but do not couple the persistent guard to acceptance. The inbox lease/retry machinery cannot recover a missing job. Guard expiry is 600 seconds, while webhook_receiver.rs:45-47 and 237-246 reject messages older than the same 600-second replay window. Polling may reconstruct current live state, but cannot recover all original channel-update or raid effects.

original_members.claim: A restart between message-ID claim and inbox insertion makes the webhook acknowledge an undelivered core event.
original_members.failure_scenario: A valid channel.raid notification M commits its persistent message-ID claim. The process terminates before inserting M into the processing inbox and restarts within ten minutes. Twitch retries M with the same ID. The existing claim produces a duplicate outcome, which the receiver acknowledges with HTTP 204 although no inbox item or processing exists. The notification is lost.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:715-735 claims the ID before routing and returns successful duplicate outcomes without admission. Core inbox insertion occurs later at :793-814. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/guard.rs:122-138 commits the claim through its pool independently of /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_store/mod.rs:94-112. The receiver maps every successful outcome to 204 at the reported line.
original_members.expected_behavior: Core notifications must be durably admitted before being acknowledged, including retries after interruption. The durable core-delivery contract is explicit in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:1-9 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_store/mod.rs:1-9.
original_members.countermeasures: The conditional claim prevents simultaneous winners but does not establish completed admission. Error-path release in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:761-775 cannot execute after process termination. The ten-minute TTL and expired-claim sweep do not recover the absent payload; later webhook delivery also encounters the ten-minute freshness check. The sibling ingress at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/eventsub.rs:68-72 uses the same dispatcher and shares this admission gap. Static verification only, as required.

original_members.claim: A webhook retry receives HTTP 204 after a failed dispatch leaves its MessageId guard active, even though the notification was never persisted.
original_members.failure_scenario: A fresh, correctly signed channel.raid notification commits its message guard. PostgreSQL becomes unavailable before routing can enqueue the event, and the subsequent guard DELETE also fails. The receiver returns 503 for that attempt. PostgreSQL recovers while the message and its guard are still within their 600-second windows. Twitch retries the same message ID; the dispatcher treats the surviving guard as a successfully delivered duplicate and the receiver returns 204. No raid work was inserted, so the event is permanently lost.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:715-735 claims the persistent guard before routing and returns Ok with duplicate=true when the claim loses. Lines 761-774 only log a failed guard release; they retain no failed-delivery state or recovery work. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/guard.rs:122-139 refuses a still-active claim, and lines 165-177 perform release as a separate DELETE. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_store/mod.rs:83-113 inserts inbox work independently, without an atomic guard/enqueue transaction. The assigned receiver maps every Ok result to 204 at line 311. Production wiring uses this dispatcher and receiver in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1443-1477.
original_members.expected_behavior: An acceptance failure must remain retryable rather than become a successful duplicate acknowledgment before durable acceptance. EventSubDispatcher::dispatch explicitly promises that acceptance errors release the message guard at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:682-683. The receiver's error branch at lines 313-319 deliberately returns 503 for retry. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/eventsub_dispatch.rs:1444-1449 establishes that retrying a failed dispatch must not be classified as a duplicate and must persist the event.
original_members.countermeasures: Signature, timestamp and readiness checks do not prevent this case because both attempts are legitimate. Successful guard release protects ordinary failures, but a release failure is only logged. Inbox write retries are bounded and can exhaust; inbox worker retries cannot recover an event that was never inserted. The 600-second guard TTL does not protect the retry because an active guard already produces success, while later deliveries encounter the receiver's timestamp rejection. The shared internal ingress has the same root problem: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/eventsub.rs:68-72 returns successful JSON for the same duplicate outcome. This is one shared defect, not a separate twin finding. Existing retry tests cover successful release, not failed release. No tests or runtime probes were executed.

findings.title_de: Abgebrochene Fachwirkung behält siebentägige Wiederholungssperre
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Abgebrochene Fachwirkung behält siebentägige Wiederholungssperre.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Interrupted business effects retain a seven-day guard that suppresses their unfinished retry.

original_members.claim: Interrupted business effects retain a seven-day guard that suppresses their unfinished retry.
original_members.failure_scenario: The worker processes channel.update with message ID m-u and commits channel_update_db:m-u. The process terminates before the telemetry transaction commits. After restart and lease expiry, the durable inbox retries the job. run_business_effect_once sees the existing guard, skips the database effect, and the runtime deletes the job as delivered. The channel-update record and title/category update never happen.
original_members.evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/handlers.rs:62-84 commits the guard before running the effect and treats an existing claim as successful suppression; :581-593 uses it for channel.update persistence. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/telemetry.rs:790-813 opens a separate transaction for that persistence. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:191-221 marks a handler returning Ok as delivered.
original_members.expected_behavior: The at-least-once inbox contract in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:56-57 and exactly-once effect contract in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/handlers.rs:43-45 require an interrupted, uncommitted database effect to remain executable. The channel.update expectation is explicitly asserted in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/eventsub_dispatch.rs:869-889.
original_members.countermeasures: The telemetry transaction protects its own insert and live-state update, but excludes the business guard. Release runs only when the effect returns Err. Restart cannot execute that cleanup, and the inbox deletes the retry long before the seven-day guard expires. Other run_business_effect_once callers share this interruption window.

original_members.claim: A restart after a business-effect claim can discard an uncommitted channel.update.
original_members.failure_scenario: The inbox leases a channel.update job with a message_id. run_business_effect_once commits its channel_update_db guard, then the process exits before store_channel_update commits. original_members.claim: A failed stream.offline job is acknowledged on retry because its own offline throttle remains active.
original_members.failure_scenario: A broadcaster has is_live=1. The offline handler successfully claims the 120-second OfflineThrottle, but apply_stream_offline encounters a transient database error. The handler returns an error and the inbox schedules a retry. When the database recovers and that retry runs within 120 seconds, claim returns false and the handler returns Ok without retrying state finalization or the remaining offline hooks. The inbox deletes the job as delivered, leaving the live-state update unapplied and losing this job's remaining followups.

Production main.rs:1434-1448 connects this handler to InboxRuntime.
original_members.expected_behavior: A failed offline finalization must remain retryable rather than being treated as a successfully processed duplicate. handlers.rs:444-450 specifies state finalization and subsequent offline effects. inbox_runtime.rs:53-57 specifies retry handling and at-least-once delivery. tests/eventsub_dispatch.rs:765-783 verifies that successful offline processing sets is_live=0, clears active_session_id, and runs the offline hooks.
original_members.countermeasures: run_business_effect_once releases only its BusinessEffect guard after an error (handlers.rs:74-82), not the separate OfflineThrottle. The online path releases OfflineThrottle at handlers.rs:256-259, but no new online event is needed or guaranteed in this scenario. Polling may subsequently repair live state, but it does not prevent the inbox retry from being prematurely acknowledged. The existing offline tests cover successful processing and duplicate suppression, not failure after the throttle claim.

original_members.claim: OfflineThrottle suppresses retries of stream.offline jobs that failed after acquiring the throttle.
original_members.failure_scenario: A stream.offline job wins the 120-second OfflineThrottle claim. Its apply_stream_offline database update then returns a transient error. The business-effect guard is released and the inbox schedules a retry after one second. On retry, the unchanged OfflineThrottle claim fails, the handler returns Ok without finishing state finalization or later followups, and the inbox deletes the job as delivered.
original_members.evidence: handlers.rs:475-490 acquires the throttle and returns Ok on an active claim. handlers.rs:499-516 propagates state-finalization errors without releasing that throttle. run_business_effect_once at handlers.rs:74-82 only releases the BusinessEffect guard. inbox_runtime.rs:268-276 and 372-374 schedule the first retry after one second; inbox_runtime.rs:215-220 treats its no-op success as delivered, and inbox_store/mod.rs:153-164 deletes the job.
original_members.expected_behavior: Failed core processing must retry or reach dead-letter, not become a successful duplicate. This is the explicit inbox_runtime.rs:1-8 and 53-65 contract. handlers.rs:444-450 and tests/eventsub_dispatch.rs:720-809 require offline finalization and followups while throttling successfully handled duplicate notifications.
original_members.countermeasures: The seven-day business-effect guard correctly releases on returned errors, but the independent 120-second throttle does not. The next online event releases the throttle, which cannot restore an already deleted offline job. Polling can later repair live state; poller/engine.rs:166-195 uses the same throttle for the offline raid hook, so an early polling fallback can also skip that effect and then persist the offline transition.

original_members.claim: stream.offline retries are silently discarded by their own 120-second throttle.
original_members.failure_scenario: An accepted stream.offline event for broadcaster 42 claims OfflineThrottle successfully, then apply_stream_offline fails transiently, for example because its UPDATE times out. The handler returns an error and the inbox schedules a retry. With the database healthy again within five seconds and no intervening stream.online, that retry finds the original 120-second throttle still active, returns Ok immediately, and is deleted from the inbox. The offline state UPDATE and the subsequent reannounce cooldown, score refresh, and offline hook never complete for this delivery.
original_members.evidence: Static proof at review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, with no source drift in the inspected files. The primary test eventsub_dispatch.rs:720-810 establishes the offline effects; following its build_stack led to this production handler. handlers.rs:475-490 persists OfflineThrottle before any state finalization and treats an unsuccessful claim as success. The state write at :510-516 propagates errors without releasing OfflineThrottle. inbox_runtime.rs:268-288 schedules the first retry after one second; its default idle wait is five seconds (:20). On the retry's Ok return, :215-221 calls mark_delivered, which deletes the work in inbox_store/mod.rs:153-164. Production main.rs:1434-1455 wires this same handler and runtime.
original_members.expected_behavior: A failed durable inbox delivery must retry its unfinished effects rather than be acknowledged as successfully processed. inbox_runtime.rs:53-64 explicitly defines handler errors as retryable and guarantees at-least-once processing; handlers.rs:43-45 specifies releasing effect guards on failure. The primary offline test at eventsub_dispatch.rs:765-810 requires offline state, session finalization, and the offline hooks while suppressing genuinely duplicate completed effects.
original_members.countermeasures: run_business_effect_once releases only its BusinessEffect guard on error (handlers.rs:74-82), not the enclosing OfflineThrottle. MessageId dedup is applied when dispatching into the inbox, not when processing retries. Go-live releases OfflineThrottle (:256-259), but there is no go-live in this scenario. The poller may eventually repair live state, but its offline raid path also checks the same throttle (poller/engine.rs:166-195), and it does not restore the discarded inbox delivery. Targeted twin inspection covered the online release and poller claim paths; no additional confirmed twin is claimed. No tests or runtime probes were executed.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: An in-flight subscription-create response can overwrite a processed revocation and suppress subsequent resubscription.

original_members.claim: An in-flight subscription-create response can overwrite a processed revocation and suppress subsequent resubscription.
original_members.failure_scenario: An enabled stream.online subscription exists remotely but is absent from local tracking, for example because startup rehydrate failed. An ensure POST receives HTTP 409 while that subscription still exists. Before its response resumes locally, Twitch revokes the subscription and the independently running webhook receiver processes the signed revocation. untrack removes no tracking entry and retains no invalidation generation. The outstanding successful response subsequently calls track, marking the revoked subscription present. All later core ensures return true at is_tracked without attempting resubscription, although stream.online events are no longer delivered.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed against 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af with no source drift. subscriptions.rs:869-891 leaves tracking empty after a failed initial listing; 1448-1451 trusts tracking; 1502-1513 awaits create then unconditionally tracks; 2113-2129 removes the pair without fencing outstanding operations. The same unconditional post-await tracking occurs at 1989-2002. Context: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-transport-twitch/src/eventsub.rs:168-180 treats 409 as success; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/webhook_receiver.rs:143-184 and 273-279 synchronously forward revocations; /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:785-790 and 1471-1484 run maintenance and the receiver independently.
original_members.expected_behavior: A processed revocation must leave the subscription eligible for the next reconcile instead of allowing an older response to restore stale tracking. This is the explicit contract at subscriptions.rs:2103-2111 and in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/subscriptions.rs:328-397.
original_members.countermeasures: The HashSet mutex protects individual mutations, not ordering across the network await. Signature and timestamp validation establish authentic revocations but do not fence stale create responses. HTTP 409 idempotence does not establish that the subscription remains enabled when tracking is updated. Rehydrate runs only at startup in main.rs:778; cleanup_stale preserves current-callback subscriptions for active targets at subscriptions.rs:2064-2067 regardless of status, and subsequent ensures trust the stale pair. Existing revocation tests exercise only sequential ordering.

original_members.failure_scenario: Twitch accepts creation of a stream.online subscription for broadcaster 42, but its successful HTTP response is delayed. That subscription is revoked, and the signed revocation callback reaches the receiver before the create future resumes. The sink removes the tracking key. When the delayed successful create returns, the manager inserts that key again. Every subsequent ensure skips creation because the revoked subscription is marked tracked, so runtime self-healing stops until restart.

This contract is explicit in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/subscriptions.rs:2103-2112 and the existing recovery test at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/subscriptions.rs:328-398.

Subsequent chat reconciles return success from is_tracked without recreating either subscription and keep updating the successful-subscription heartbeat, although chat ingestion remains stopped until another untrack or process restart.

Lines 1448-1450 return true solely from tracked membership. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:777-790 rehydrate runs at startup; the recurring maintenance at 2341-2414 performs cleanup and ensures without rebuilding tracking. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/chat_wiring.rs:1457-1465 writes the success heartbeat after that true result. All evidence files match review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
original_members.expected_behavior: A terminally disabled remote subscription must not continue satisfying an ensure for an active channel. The existing rehydrate contract at lines 869-884 explicitly admits only enabled subscriptions into tracking, and untrack's contract at 2103-2111 requires removal of revoked tracking so reconciliation can restore delivery.
original_members.countermeasures: The enabled-status filter in rehydrate handles startup but not this running-process failure. RevocationSink and WebhookReceiver clear tracking when a revocation is actually received; the scenario explicitly loses that callback during the outage. The recurring cleanup already obtains the authoritative listing but ignores its status. Raid readiness polling is raid-specific and does not repair chat tracking. Empty-roster cleanup protection does not apply because the active partner remains in the roster.

original_members.failure_scenario: Use the old/current stream.offline subscriptions for broadcaster 42 already modeled by the assigned test at lines 499-517. After rehydrate(), call cleanup_stale({42}). Only the old remote subscription is deleted, but tracked_pairs() becomes empty although the enabled current subscription remains. A capacity snapshot then reports zero instead of one, and ensure_offline_subscription no longer deduplicates against the retained subscription.
original_members.evidence: Static trace at the pinned SHA: tracking keys contain only (type, broadcaster ID), lines 530-532. rehydrate tracks the current-callback twin, lines 870-884. cleanup skips the active current callback at 2064-2067, but successful deletion of the old callback unconditionally removes the same tracking key at 2072-2075. Capacity uses this set at 2145-2172. Production startup rehydrates at main.rs:778 and starts maintenance, which invokes cleanup at main.rs:2368. The assigned test checks deleted IDs only and does not rehydrate or verify retained tracking.
original_members.expected_behavior: Removing a stale callback must preserve tracking for an enabled subscription with the same type and broadcaster at the current callback. This follows from rehydrate's current-callback filter, cleanup's explicit current-and-active retention branch, and ensure's tracking-based deduplication.
original_members.countermeasures: The empty-active-set guard does not apply to {42}. The current-callback retention branch prevents remote deletion but does not prevent removal of its shared tracking key. A later successful ensure or rehydrate can restore tracking; neither preserves it during cleanup. No lost-event claim is made. Inspected sources match the fixed review SHA; no tests or live requests were run.

Cleanup at 2064-2075 preserves the current remote subscription but removes tracking after any successful obsolete deletion, using only type and broadcaster. Capacity payload at 2145-2172 derives its count and listeners exclusively from that tracking set. Independent cleanup and snapshot callers are wired at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:414-417,2368-2381.
original_members.expected_behavior: Cleanup must preserve tracking for the surviving active current-callback subscription. resolved_candidate_group.claim: Redelivery of stream.online overwrites a later completed stream.offline transition.

original_members.claim: Redelivery of stream.online overwrites a later completed stream.offline transition.
original_members.failure_scenario: Online job A completes successfully, but deleting its inbox row fails. Before A's 30-second lease expires, a newer offline job B completes and sets is_live to 0. A is then redelivered. Its unconditional apply_stream_online sets is_live back to 1 and releases the offline throttle, although the broadcaster is offline. Previously successful business guards skip A's session and followup effects, so they do not restore a consistent state.
original_members.evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:217-220 explicitly retains successfully handled jobs when mark_delivered fails. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/handlers.rs:245-259 reapplies online state and clears OfflineThrottle on every attempt, before business-effect deduplication. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/live_state.rs:389-425 unconditionally writes is_live=1; :469-484 writes is_live=0 for the intervening offline event.
original_members.expected_behavior: The inbox explicitly requires idempotent handlers in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:56-57 and relies on that property after delivery-write failures at :217-220. Replaying an older completed online event must not undo a later completed offline event.
original_members.countermeasures: The MessageId guard applies at ingress, not to inbox redelivery. Business-effect guards cover the later session and hook calls but not apply_stream_online or throttle release. The live-state transaction has no event-freshness comparison or completed-message check. Periodic polling can eventually correct the row but does not prevent the incorrect replay.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: claim_or_extend exposes a deletion gap that can trigger a duplicate live announcement during an active cooldown.

original_members.claim: claim_or_extend exposes a deletion gap that can trigger a duplicate live announcement during an active cooldown.
original_members.failure_scenario: A broadcaster has an existing live announcement and an active reannounce cooldown. During a short reconnect, the poller reads an offline previous state and a live current snapshot, then confirms that the cooldown marker exists. Concurrent offline processing extends that marker: its first claim fails, then release deletes it. Before the replacement claim, the poller's is_active read returns false. It treats the same-stream reconnect as occurring after cooldown and sends a new live announcement.
original_members.evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/guard.rs:156-160 extends an active guard using separate claim, DELETE and claim operations. Concurrent callers exist in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/handlers.rs:526-535 and /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/poller/engine.rs:228-239. The poller reads existence and activity separately at :612-627, then allows a new post through same_stream_reconnect_after_cooldown at :763-788. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1443-1448 and :1883-1902 start inbox and poller tasks sharing the guard store.
original_members.expected_behavior: claim_or_extend promises to reset an active guard's TTL at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/guard.rs:142-144. resolved_candidate_group.claim: stream.offline acknowledges failed session finalization and clears the session's recovery link.

original_members.claim: stream.offline acknowledges failed session finalization and clears the session's recovery link.
original_members.failure_scenario: An existing open session has an active_session_id in live state. During stream.offline, SessionStore::apply_finalize fails transiently and rolls back. SessionTracker::finalize returns false, which the handler ignores. The following apply_stream_offline succeeds, sets is_live=0 and active_session_id=NULL, and the job is acknowledged. The session remains open, while subsequent offline polling no longer selects it for normal finalization.
original_members.evidence: handlers.rs:505-513 discards finalize's boolean and only propagates the subsequent live-state update error. sessions/tracker.rs:439-450 converts apply_finalize errors into false. sessions/store.rs:565-626 performs finalization in a transaction and propagates failures. live_state.rs:475-483 then clears active_session_id independently. poller/engine.rs:598-605 only finalizes an offline session when was_live or active_session_id is present.
original_members.expected_behavior: Successful offline processing must actually close the open session. tests/eventsub_dispatch.rs:765-779 asserts both cleared live state and a non-null ended_at with notes='offline'. handlers.rs:449 explicitly describes the guarded effect as session plus live-state finalization.
original_members.countermeasures: SessionStore's transaction protects the failed session write, but does not include the subsequent handler-level offline update. The tracker retains its cache on persistence failure, yet normal polling consults live-state flags before finalizing. Orphan cleanup eventually acts only after one hour without viewer samples or 24 hours for zero-sample sessions (sessions/store.rs:630-663), using the last viewer timestamp or session start rather than the original offline time. That is delayed cleanup, not successful recovery of this event.

findings.title_de: Blockiertes DB-Schreiben hält gesamte Inbox auf
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Blockiertes DB-Schreiben hält gesamte Inbox auf.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: A blocked writable database statement can indefinitely stall the entire EventSub inbox because handler execution has no deadline.

original_members.claim: A blocked writable database statement can indefinitely stall the entire EventSub inbox because handler execution has no deadline.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, another connection leaves an update transaction on broadcaster X's twitch_live_state row open. A queued stream.online for X reaches apply_stream_online and waits on that row lock. The sole inbox worker awaits this handler indefinitely, so subsequently queued core events for other broadcasters never execute. Attempt counts do not advance, and continued accepted core notifications accumulate in the durable inbox.
original_members.evidence: Sources read at fixed commit 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:182-209 processes each leased item sequentially and awaits the spawned handler without timeout or cancellation. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/handlers.rs:245-255 awaits apply_stream_online. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/live_state.rs:387-425 performs and awaits its transactional INSERT ON CONFLICT UPDATE. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:494 and 1434-1448 wires the normal writable pool into one MonitoringEventHandler and InboxRuntime. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 sets statement_timeout only for read-only connections, not this writable pool.
original_members.expected_behavior: A stalled external operation should not permanently prevent unrelated due events from being processed. The documented worker recovery model includes bounded retries and dead-lettering, but no maximum handler duration or safe cancellation policy is specified. Selecting those limits requires a behavior decision, so this is C rather than an automatic fix.
original_members.countermeasures: Batch size 20 bounds each in-memory selection, and successful jobs are deleted. The 30-second lease controls database eligibility but does not interrupt a running handler. Five-attempt dead-lettering is reached only after the handler returns an error. Panic isolation does not handle a pending future. SQLx pool acquisition/connect deadlines do not bound an already acquired connection's statement. Helix requests have their own 20-second limit, so they are not evidence of this indefinite database wait. An independently configured PostgreSQL timeout could mitigate the scenario; live database settings were not inspected.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Rehydration verwechselt ausgehende mit eingehenden Raids.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Rehydration mistakes outgoing raid subscriptions for incoming raid subscriptions.

original_members.claim: Rehydration mistakes outgoing raid subscriptions for incoming raid subscriptions.
original_members.failure_scenario: At startup the app has an enabled channel.raid webhook subscription with condition from_broadcaster_user_id='777', the current callback, and no incoming subscription for broadcaster 777. Rehydration tracks ('channel.raid','777'). ensure_raid_subscription('777', ...) subsequently returns true without creating its required to_broadcaster_user_id subscription. A raid arriving at 777 is consequently not delivered through the outgoing subscription. The live readiness poll also accepts that same outgoing subscription as enabled.
original_members.evidence: Lines 875-884 collapse remote subscriptions to type and broadcaster ID, and lines 1448-1450 skip creation for that pair. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/wiring.rs:67-84 explicitly maps both to_broadcaster_user_id and from_broadcaster_user_id into RemoteSubscription.broadcaster_user_id, discarding direction. The twin in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/raid_adapters.rs:479-487 matches only channel.raid and that collapsed ID. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1047-1058 wires this poll into the live raid pipeline. All evidence files match the fixed review SHA.
original_members.expected_behavior: Incoming-raid readiness must require a subscription whose condition is to_broadcaster_user_id equal to the destination. This contract is explicit at lines 901-911 and verified in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/subscriptions.rs:521-540.
original_members.countermeasures: Rehydration's enabled-status and callback checks both pass for the outgoing subscription. Cleanup at lines 2063-2067 also retains it because broadcaster 777 is active. The live status poll does not compensate because it uses the same directionless projection. Revocation handling cannot help while the outgoing subscription remains valid and enabled. The existing raid test covers new creation and deduplication, not rehydration of the opposite condition.

findings.title_de: DB-Lookupfehler stuft berechtigten Chat als passiv ein
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: DB-Lookupfehler stuft berechtigten Chat als passiv ein.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Database lookup failures can misclassify authorized chat channels as passive lurkers and skip both subscriptions.

original_members.claim: Database lookup failures can misclassify authorized chat channels as passive lurkers and skip both subscriptions.
original_members.failure_scenario: A monitored streamer has no twitch_partners row, has inactive partner state, and has valid raid authorization with raid_enabled=true, needs_reauth=false and channel:bot scope. The roster query successfully selects it for chat reconciliation. The per-channel monitored-only and partner-state reads succeed, but the subsequent raid-auth existence query times out. Its error becomes false, so the channel is incorrectly marked passive and neither chat subscription is attempted. Recovery must wait for a later reconciliation.
original_members.evidence: In the assigned file, the raid-auth query error is converted to false at 1095-1098, then combined with is_monitored_only=true and is_partner_active=false at 1100. ensure_chat_subscriptions writes passive-lurker markers and exits before either create at 984-997. The analogous partner-state error conversion is at 1078-1082. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/chat_wiring.rs:1376-1386 selects authorized raid-enabled non-partners, and 1455-1459 passes them into this gate. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/subscriptions.rs:1002-1036 explicitly demonstrates that monitored-only channels with raid authorization must create both chat subscriptions.
original_members.expected_behavior: The assigned function's documented contract at 1027-1033 says database errors are treated as not being a lurker. An unknown authorization or partner-state lookup must therefore not be interpreted as proven absence and suppress subscription attempts.
original_members.countermeasures: Failure of the first monitored-only query correctly bypasses the lurker gate, but the later two reads use the opposite effective behavior. The upstream roster already verified authorization, yet these separate reads can fail afterward. The pure predicate in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-chat/src/lurker_policy.rs:47-52 cannot distinguish unknown flags from false. The 30-minute reconciliation loop eventually retries, but does not prevent the erroneous skipped cycle.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Capacity-Snapshot stoppt Poller bei DB-Warten.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Capacity snapshot database waits can stop the monitoring poller indefinitely.

original_members.claim: Capacity snapshot database waits can stop the monitoring poller indefinitely.
original_members.failure_scenario: With the writable bot pool and PostgreSQL statement_timeout=0, another connection holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_eventsub_capacity_snapshot in an open transaction. The next due capacity snapshot waits indefinitely for that table lock. Because the poller awaits this diagnostic operation inline, no subsequent monitoring ticks run, although the process remains active.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, subscriptions.rs:2204-2208 awaits CapacitySnapshotStore::record; its INSERT executes without a deadline at 2269-2287. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:414-417 awaits that method from on_capacity_tick. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/poller/engine.rs:489 awaits the hook, and 147-154 awaits each tick before starting the next. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:41-56 configures statement_timeout only for read-only pools; main.rs:494 uses the ordinary writable connect function.
original_members.expected_behavior: Capacity history is auxiliary, best-effort telemetry: subscriptions.rs:2209-2211 logs a failed write and returns rather than failing monitoring. A blocked diagnostic write must likewise terminate with an error so subsequent monitoring ticks can continue.
original_members.countermeasures: The pool acquisition deadline does not bound execution after a connection is acquired. The Helix client's 20-second HTTP timeout does not cover SQL. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/task_supervisor.rs:112-151 watches task completion, not progress. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/deadlock_twitch_bot_watchdog.py:101-120,274-284 checks only whether systemd reports active/running, so this stall is considered healthy. A separately configured PostgreSQL statement timeout would bound the scenario, but the reviewed writable-pool code provides none. Related unbounded capacity SQL awaits exist at subscriptions.rs:2136-2139 and 2234,2298-2299.

findings.title_de: Fehlermaps behalten entfernte Broadcaster
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Fehlermaps behalten entfernte Broadcaster.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: EventSub failure maps retain removed broadcasters indefinitely.

original_members.claim: EventSub failure maps retain removed broadcasters indefinitely.
original_members.failure_scenario: Keep one broadcaster active while other broadcaster IDs repeatedly enter and leave the subscription roster. For each departing broadcaster, an ineligible telemetry subscription returns HTTP 400 and never subsequently succeeds. Every distinct ID leaves a failure-counter entry and a failed-subscription entry. Normal stale cleanup removes remote subscriptions but not these entries. After N such departures, memory retains N historical identities despite a small current roster; continued churn can exhaust process memory.
original_members.evidence: subscriptions.rs:814-819 keys failure_counters by subscription type, broadcaster ID and reason; 852-865 stores failed_subscriptions by type and ID. cleanup_stale at 2042-2088 removes only tracked entries after remote deletion. purge_local_channel_state at 1129-1151 removes failure status but not counters, and its only production invocation in the assigned source is the special stale-chat-403 path at 1689. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2351-2383 selects the current roster, runs cleanup, and ensures only current rows, so removed IDs do not receive another ensure that could clear their failure state. subscriptions.rs:1766-1775 explicitly identifies ineligible-channel HTTP 400 responses.
original_members.expected_behavior: Long-lived diagnostic state should have a bounded retention policy or retirement when a broadcaster leaves the roster. Classification remains C because the intended lifetime of historical failure counters is not specified, and choosing eviction semantics is a policy decision.
original_members.countermeasures: Successful subscriptions clear failure status at subscriptions.rs:711-717,801-807, but never failure counters. The special stale-chat-403 purge does not run for normally removed broadcasters or the HTTP 400 scenario. Cooldown expiry is checked lazily for the same ID, not by a global sweep. The 10,000 remote-subscription limit does not bound historical failed IDs. The existing test at subscriptions.rs:2595-2602 deliberately preserves counters after recovery, confirming that indiscriminately clearing counters would change intended behavior.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Repeated webhook revocations can untrack an enabled replacement subscription.

original_members.claim: Repeated webhook revocations can untrack an enabled replacement subscription.
original_members.failure_scenario: A signed stream.online revocation for broadcaster 123 arrives immediately before a scheduled reconciliation. The receiver untracks the revoked subscription, but its 204 response is lost. Reconciliation successfully creates and tracks a replacement. A repeated delivery of the original revocation arrives within 600 seconds with the same message ID and body. The receiver removes the replacement's tracking pair, although the replacement remains enabled at Twitch. Local subscription status and capacity accounting become incorrect until another ensure restores tracking.
original_members.evidence: The revocation branch calls handle_revocation without message-ID deduplication. handle_revocation at lines 143-184 ignores subscription.id and passes only type and broadcaster ID to the sink. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/subscriptions.rs:351-354 the sink calls untrack; lines 2113-2129 remove whichever current tracking pair matches. Successful creates restore that same pair at lines 1493-1528, and capacity accounting uses these pairs at lines 2145-2168. The actual reconciliation path is wired in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2341-2383.
original_members.expected_behavior: A repeated revocation of an old subscription must not invalidate tracking for its enabled replacement. The receiver and sink contracts describe removing the revoked subscription so reconciliation can heal it, not removing subsequent replacements.
original_members.countermeasures: HMAC and timestamp validation accept a genuine repeated delivery within the window. The persistent message-ID guard runs only in notification dispatch, not in the revocation branch. findings.title_de: Webhook-Zeitprüfung akzeptiert außerhalb 600 Sekunden
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Webhook-Zeitprüfung akzeptiert außerhalb 600 Sekunden.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Webhook timestamp validation accepts messages outside the declared 600-second window.

original_members.claim: Webhook timestamp validation accepts messages outside the declared 600-second window.
original_members.failure_scenario: At 2026-10-08T12:10:00.500Z, a correctly signed webhook dated 2026-10-08T12:00:00Z is 600.5 seconds old. num_seconds() produces 600, so the callback accepts it instead of returning 403. Likewise, a timestamp 600.5 seconds in the future produces -600 and passes.
original_members.evidence: Lines 132-135 compare age.num_seconds() against the inclusive integer range. The pinned Chrono 0.4.45 implementation at /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/chrono-0.4.45/src/time_delta.rs:310-314 returns whole seconds, truncating fractional magnitude. The callback uses this predicate at lines 237-247. Existing tests cover exact 600 and 601 seconds, but not fractional boundary crossings.
original_members.expected_behavior: The explicit contracts at lines 45-47 and 124-135 permit exactly [-600 seconds, +600 seconds] and require rejecting anything beyond either boundary. Fractional seconds must participate in that comparison.
original_members.countermeasures: Signature verification authenticates the timestamp but does not enforce age. Notification deduplication can suppress a previously seen message while its guard remains active, but cannot reject a first delivery outside the age window. Verification and revocation messages do not use that guard. This is a boundary correctness finding, not a claimed exploitable security breach.

findings.title_de: Clipkommando verzögert Webhookbestätigung bei VOD-Lookup
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Clipkommando verzögert Webhookbestätigung bei VOD-Lookup.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The webhook ACK waits at least 12 seconds when a !clip command cannot resolve VOD metadata.

original_members.claim: The webhook ACK waits at least 12 seconds when a !clip command cannot resolve VOD metadata.
original_members.failure_scenario: A fresh, correctly signed channel.chat.message contains !clip in an authorized live partner channel with clipping enabled and no active command cooldown. Clip creation succeeds, but all four detail lookups lack usable VOD metadata. Even with instantaneous database and HTTP responses, the metadata loop sleeps for 2 + 4 + 6 seconds before returning. A delivery sender with a 10-second response deadline times out before the initial callback can return 204 and must retry.
original_members.evidence: webhook_receiver.rs:306-311 awaits the complete dispatcher before responding. dispatch.rs:817-820 awaits the chat hook rather than using the core-event inbox. chat_wiring.rs:2033-2043 awaits pipeline.handle; pipeline.rs:1176-1182 awaits commands, and its step wrapper at 1900-1911 awaits the spawned task. commands.rs:676-678 and 1874-1876 await clip creation. chat_wiring.rs:170-198 performs four metadata attempts with sleeps of 2, 4 and 6 seconds. main.rs:1476-1484 serves this receiver directly without a response-timeout layer. These supporting sources match review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
original_members.expected_behavior: Accepted public notifications should be acknowledged independently of slow clip metadata resolution. The transport-as-enqueue-producer principle is documented in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/docs/adr/0004-eventsub-webhook-only.md:26-29; commands.rs:1181-1187 also explicitly isolates another slow command from the chat pipeline. Classified C because the current chat path intentionally awaits processing, and the appropriate durable queuing or cancellation policy is not specified.
original_members.countermeasures: Signature verification, freshness checks and the readiness gate protect admission but do not bound processing time. The four-attempt limit bounds metadata polling, yet its sleeps alone exceed the example response deadline. The message-ID guard can acknowledge subsequent retries without repeating work, so this finding does not establish duplicate clips, event loss or subscription revocation. Core events already use an inbox, but chat messages bypass it. The related internal dispatch handler at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/eventsub.rs:68 also awaits dispatch; its different response contract does not independently establish the same deadline defect. Review asynchronous clip-metadata completion or durable chat acceptance before adding a blanket callback timeout, which could leave claimed messages unfinished.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Replaying a signed notification with message-type=revocation bypasses deduplication and clears subscription tracking.

original_members.claim: Replaying a signed notification with message-type=revocation bypasses deduplication and clears subscription tracking.
original_members.failure_scenario: Someone possessing an already-processed, correctly signed notification less than 600 seconds old resends its unchanged message ID, timestamp, body and signature, changing only Twitch-Eventsub-Message-Type to revocation. A normal notification body containing subscription.type, subscription.status=enabled and subscription.condition.broadcaster_user_id then reaches the revocation sink and removes that subscription's local tracking despite the previously claimed message-ID guard.
original_members.evidence: At fixed review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, webhook_receiver.rs:118-121 authenticates only message ID, timestamp and body. Lines 257 and 273-279 select revocation using the unsigned header and bypass dispatcher deduplication. Lines 143-184 log subscription.status without validating it, then invoke the sink. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1471-1474 wires the sink. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/subscriptions.rs:351-353,2113-2121 removes tracking and clears subscription failure state. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:715-736 applies deduplication only when dispatch is called.
original_members.expected_behavior: The authentication and replay-protection contract in webhook_receiver.rs:12-21 should prevent a processed notification from being reinterpreted as a subscription revocation through an unauthenticated header.
original_members.countermeasures: Valid HMAC and a fresh timestamp remain mandatory, so arbitrary unsigned payloads cannot exploit this. Startup rejects empty secrets, and the listener binds to loopback behind the intended public proxy. The sink changes local bookkeeping, not the remote subscription itself. Access to a fresh signed notification and the deployed proxy's restrictions were not established, so this is C rather than a confirmed externally exploitable vulnerability. Consider validating signed revocation payload status and applying replay protection to revocation effects.

findings.title_de: Abgelaufener Worker überschreibt neueren Inboxstand
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Abgelaufener Worker überschreibt neueren Inboxstand.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Expired inbox workers can resurrect delivered work as a dead-letter or overwrite newer retry state.

original_members.claim: Expired inbox workers can resurrect delivered work as a dead-letter or overwrite newer retry state.
original_members.failure_scenario: With two supported inbox consumers, worker A leases a row with attempt_count=4. Processing exceeds its 30-second lease, so worker B leases the same row, completes it successfully and calls mark_delivered. A subsequently fails its stale attempt and calls mark_dead_letter. That method inserts the cached LeasedWork unconditionally, although the inbox row no longer exists, creating a dead-letter for successfully delivered work. The same missing ownership check affects mark_retry: a delayed attempt with an older attempt_count can overwrite a newer consumer's higher counter and lease deadline, reducing recorded attempts and making actively leased work available again.
original_members.evidence: Code checked against 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_store/mod.rs:23-30, LeasedWork carries no lease identity or deadline. Lines 129-150 atomically claim rows but retain no lock after the SQL statement. Lines 218-249 insert/upsert dead-letter data from the cached work before deleting the inbox row, without checking whether that row exists or still belongs to this attempt. Lines 179-188 overwrite retry state using only work_id. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:18-23,167-198, workers lease 20 rows for 30 seconds, process them sequentially, and have neither lease renewal nor a handler timeout. Lines 236-275 calculate completion state from the cached attempt_count. The normal completion path at lines 215-225 reaches mark_delivered or mark_dead_letter.
original_members.expected_behavior: Successful delivery must leave work removed, not subsequently recreate it as failed. An expired attempt must not overwrite a newer attempt's lease or reduce its retry counter. The shared-consumer contract is explicit in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_store/mod.rs:4-9. Success deletes work and final failure atomically moves existing work to dead-letter according to lines 153-154 and 197-198. Crash-recovery re-leasing after expiry is explicitly tested in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/hermetic.rs:229-235.
original_members.countermeasures: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED protects simultaneous claim statements, not later completion writes. The dead-letter transaction prevents a partial move but does not validate ownership or the continued existence of the source row. Business-effect guards in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/handlers.rs:46-84 deduplicate effects, not queue state transitions. Separate work_id primary keys in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:2087,2094 do not prevent this race. Ordinary wiring starts one consumer in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1434-1448; the scenario requires a second consumer, which the store explicitly supports and InboxRuntime does not prohibit. No concurrent production deployment or runtime reproduction was claimed. Completion needs validation against the current lease/source row; at-least-once delivery alone does not protect these transitions.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: lease_due can return stream lifecycle events in reversed chronological order, leaving an offline broadcaster marked live.

original_members.claim: lease_due can return stream lifecycle events in reversed chronological order, leaving an offline broadcaster marked live.
original_members.failure_scenario: Two distinct notifications for broadcaster 42 are pending: stream.online queued at 1000 and stream.offline queued at 1001. Both are leased together. An UPDATE-FROM execution plan returning target-table order rather than the CTE's sorted order can return offline before online. The worker processes that order, so the older online event overwrites the newer offline state with is_live=1 and reopens a session.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, mod.rs:129-143 orders only the CTE selecting work IDs. The outer UPDATE RETURNING has no ordered result, and fetch_all preserves that unspecified result order. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:182-186 processes the returned vector without sorting. The deployed runtime is constructed in rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:1434-1448. Notifications reach enqueue through rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/dispatch.rs:804-814. rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/live_state.rs:389-398 unconditionally assigns is_live=1 for online; lines 475-478 assign is_live=0 for offline. This is a static SQL-ordering finding; no database probe or test was run.
original_members.expected_behavior: Preserve queued_at order within the leased batch so an earlier online notification does not overwrite a later offline notification. The query itself selects oldest work first at mod.rs:133. The offline-state contract is explicitly asserted in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/tests/eventsub_dispatch.rs:754-779: processing offline must leave is_live=0, clear the active session, and finalize it.
original_members.countermeasures: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED protects selection from competing leases, not RETURNING order. Distinct message IDs bypass duplicate-message guards. OfflineThrottle does not reject the subsequent older online event; handlers.rs:256-259 instead releases that guard on online. The live-state writes have no event-age predicate. Existing store lifecycle tests exercise one leased job at a time, not batch order. Targeted searches in tb-monitoring and the referenced EventSub queue paths found no sorting layer or additional ordering twin; no coverage outside the assigned primary ranges is claimed.

findings.title_de: Inbox-Retry wiederholt SQLx-I/O-Abbrüche nicht
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Inbox-Retry wiederholt SQLx-I/O-Abbrüche nicht.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Der Inbox-Schreibretry wiederholt SQLx-I/O-Verbindungsabbrüche nicht.

original_members.claim: Der Inbox-Schreibretry wiederholt SQLx-I/O-Verbindungsabbrüche nicht.
original_members.failure_scenario: Beim Dead-Letter-Requeue bricht eine bereits erworbene PostgreSQL-Verbindung während BEGIN ab, bevor Tabellen verändert wurden. SQLx liefert Io(ConnectionReset oder UnexpectedEof). Obwohl PostgreSQL innerhalb des vorgesehenen Backoffs wieder verfügbar wird, erfolgt kein zweiter Versuch. Der Requeue-Aufruf endet mit HTTP 500; der Auftrag bleibt im Dead-Letter.
original_members.evidence: Statische Beweiskette auf SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af: retry.rs:73-89 prüft ausschließlich Datenbankfehler mit SQLSTATE; retry.rs:111-112 reicht andere Fehler sofort weiter. mod.rs:300-301 beginnt die Requeue-Transaktion innerhalb dieses Wrappers. rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/python_stubs.rs:191-194,207-215 übersetzt den Fehler in HTTP 500. SQLx 0.9.0, lokal gelesen unter /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-core-0.9.0/src/error.rs:144-147, liefert für Io kein as_database_error(). Kein Laufzeitversuch durchgeführt.
original_members.expected_behavior: retry.rs:5-8 beschreibt Schutz gegen kurze PostgreSQL-Neustarts, und :71-72 nennt Verbindungsabbrüche als wiederholbar. Ein sicher vor der Änderung gescheiterter Transaktionsbeginn sollte diese Wiederherstellung nutzen. Klasse C, weil der gemeinsame Wrapper auch Operationen mit möglicherweise unbekanntem Commit-Ausgang behandelt; eine allgemeine Wiederholung aller I/O-Fehler wäre ohne geklärte Wiederholungsregeln nicht eindeutig korrekt.
original_members.countermeasures: SQLx wiederholt ConnectionRefused während des Verbindungsaufbaus bereits intern; das schützt nicht gegen den beschriebenen Abbruch einer laufenden BEGIN-Anfrage. Die Requeue-Transaktion verhindert Datenverlust. InboxRuntime protokolliert Store-Fehler und verarbeitet bestehende Inbox-Einträge später erneut; EventSubDispatcher gibt Enqueue-Fehler weiter. Diese Schichten vermeiden pauschale Aussagen über verlorene Events, führen den gescheiterten administrativen Requeue aber nicht erneut aus.

findings.title_de: Blockierte Inboxbestätigung hält einzigen Worker auf
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Blockierte Inboxbestätigung hält einzigen Worker auf.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Eine blockierte Inbox-Bestätigung kann den einzigen EventSub-Worker unbegrenzt anhalten.

original_members.claim: Eine blockierte Inbox-Bestätigung kann den einzigen EventSub-Worker unbegrenzt anhalten.
original_members.failure_scenario: Bei PostgreSQL mit statement_timeout=0 und ohne Idle-Transaction-Grenze hält eine andere Sitzung nach dem Leasen eine Zeilensperre auf dem Auftrag und bleibt in ihrer Transaktion untätig. Nach erfolgreicher Handler-Ausführung wartet mark_delivered unbegrenzt auf diese Sperre. Der sequenzielle Inbox-Worker verarbeitet dadurch auch alle weiteren, nicht gesperrten Aufträge nicht mehr.
original_members.evidence: Feste Codebasis 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. mod.rs:154-163 wartet auf DELETE ohne Zeitgrenze; retry.rs:106-120 begrenzt die Versuchsanzahl, wartet aber innerhalb jedes Versuchs unbegrenzt. Kontext /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_runtime.rs:182-186,215-221 zeigt die sequenzielle Verarbeitung und das direkte Warten auf mark_delivered. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:494,1443-1448 verbindet genau diesen Worker mit dem schreibenden Pool.
original_members.expected_behavior: Eine festhängende Bestätigung muss innerhalb einer endlichen Zeit als Fehler zurückkehren, damit weitere Inbox-Aufträge verarbeitet werden. Der bestehende Fehlerpfad in inbox_runtime.rs:217-221 sieht ausdrücklich vor, einen fehlgeschlagenen Löschversuch zu protokollieren und den Auftrag für die erneute Verarbeitung nach Lease-Ablauf stehenzulassen.
original_members.countermeasures: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED schützt das Leasen, nicht das spätere DELETE. Die 30-Sekunden-Lease beendet keine laufende Datenbankabfrage. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 begrenzt nur den Verbindungserwerb; statement_timeout=20000 wird ausschließlich für schreibgeschützte Pools gesetzt. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/ops/systemd/twitch-runtime-roles.sql:26,51 setzt keine entsprechende Grenze für twitchbot. Eine externe Datenbank-Zeitgrenze könnte schützen, wird im geprüften Pfad aber nicht vorausgesetzt oder erzwungen. Derselbe unbegrenzte SQL-Wartepfad besteht bei enqueue, mark_retry, mark_dead_letter und requeue_dead_letter. Keine Laufzeitprüfung durchgeführt.
