findings.title_de: Message-ID-Guard bestätigt vor dauerhafter Annahme
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Message-ID-Guard bestätigt vor dauerhafter Annahme.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The message-ID guard can acknowledge an EventSub delivery before durable acceptance, losing the event if the original attempt fails or crashes.

original_members.claim: The message-ID guard can acknowledge an EventSub delivery before durable acceptance, losing the event if the original attempt fails or crashes.
original_members.failure_scenario: Attempt A commits the guard for message M, then stalls before enqueueing stream.online or committing channel.subscription.end. An overlapping delivery B of M encounters that guard and receives a duplicate success, which the webhook returns as HTTP 204. A subsequently fails its database operation or the process terminates before persistence. No durable event exists despite B's acknowledgement. The crash variant also affects a later retry after restart while the 600-second guard remains active.
original_members.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, dispatch.rs:715-736 claims the guard and returns Ok for a losing claim before route runs at line 746. guard.rs:122-139 commits that claim independently through the pool and stores no completion state. Core enqueue happens later at dispatch.rs:810-813; subscription writes commit separately at telemetry.rs:131-164. webhook_receiver.rs:306-319 maps every Ok, including this premature duplicate, to 204. main.rs:1476-1483 serves the shared dispatcher without serializing requests. Static interleaving analysis only; no tests or probes executed.
original_members.expected_behavior: Acknowledgement must mean the delivery has been durably accepted or successfully applied. dispatch.rs:682-683 explicitly treats failed acceptance as retryable, and the assigned regression at eventsub_dispatch.rs:1442-1451 requires rollback followed by processing the same message again, rather than suppressing it as a duplicate.
original_members.countermeasures: The atomic guard prevents simultaneous claims but does not distinguish pending from completed acceptance. Releasing the guard on Err at dispatch.rs:761-775 helps sequential retries only: it cannot retract B's earlier 204 and never executes after a crash. Inbox retry and subscription transaction rollback protect existing work, not an event that was never durably accepted. The same premature-success branch covers both core enqueue and transactional subscription lifecycle routes.

findings.title_de: Paralleler Hype-Train-Beginn und Abschluss erhöht spätere Zählung
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Paralleler Hype-Train-Beginn und Abschluss erhöht spätere Zählung.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Overlapping hype-train Begin and End writes can create an unfinished Begin plus a separate End and inflate the post-stream train count.

original_members.claim: Overlapping hype-train Begin and End writes can create an unfinished Begin plus a separate End and inflate the post-stream train count.
original_members.failure_scenario: Valid Begin and End notifications for the same broadcaster and started_at overlap, for example after delayed delivery of Begin. End's UPDATE observes no committed Begin row. Begin then inserts its row, and End performs its fallback INSERT. Both calls succeed, leaving two rows for one train, with the Begin row's ended_at still NULL. The post-stream payload counts both rows and reports two trains instead of the single train reported by the ordered case.
original_members.evidence: telemetry.rs:432-479 performs End's UPDATE and fallback INSERT as independent pool operations; Begin always inserts. dispatch.rs:937-950 handles these notifications inline, with distinct message-ID guards rather than per-train ordering. The table definition and hypertable migration provide no uniqueness constraint on broadcaster plus started_at. post_stream.rs:1195-1203 computes hype_trains.count using COUNT(*) without excluding the unfinished duplicate. The assigned ordered regression at eventsub_dispatch.rs:1314-1348 expects one row and a populated ended_at.
original_members.expected_behavior: The documented normal case closes the existing Begin rather than creating an additional End row. However, behavior for reordered notifications is not explicitly specified, and Progress deliberately inserts snapshots. Consequently, changing reconciliation or snapshot semantics is not sufficiently established for automatic class-B fixing.
original_members.countermeasures: Message dedup only protects repeated delivery IDs; Begin and End have different IDs. Neither the dispatcher nor the update/fallback sequence serializes the same train. The sequential regression cannot exercise this interleaving. Overview and monetization filter ended_at IS NOT NULL, limiting their immediate count impact, but the post-stream count includes the unfinished row. Class C because the intended out-of-order and snapshot contract needs clarification.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Unbanbereinigung bestätigt Fehler ohne Wiederholung.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Unban cleanup errors are acknowledged without retry, leaving stale applied-ban entries that suppress subsequent offline sweeps.

original_members.claim: Unban cleanup errors are acknowledged without retry, leaving stale applied-ban entries that suppress subsequent offline sweeps.
original_members.failure_scenario: A globally banned viewer is manually unbanned in a channel with an existing applied-ban ledger entry. The unban event INSERT succeeds, but the subsequent cleanup DELETE encounters a transient database connection error. The delivery is acknowledged. Once the database recovers, with no further unban event, offline sweeps continue skipping the now-unbanned viewer because the stale ledger entry remains.
original_members.evidence: Static trace at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. telemetry.rs:517-522 awaits clear_global_ban_applied and then returns Ok(()); :567-599 gives cleanup no error return and only logs DELETE failures. dispatch.rs:827-852 consequently marks channel.moderate processed, while :746-774 retains the message guard on success. webhook_receiver.rs:306-319 returns HTTP 204 for successful dispatch. rust/crates/tb-chat/src/global_ban_sweep.rs:344-357 skips every existing applied pair. The assigned eventsub_dispatch.rs:1010-1070 explicitly verifies that unban removes the applied entry so the next sweep becomes due.
original_members.expected_behavior: A processed unban must clear its applied-ban entry, as asserted by eventsub_dispatch.rs:1069-1070. Failure of that required cleanup must remain recoverable rather than completing the delivery successfully.
original_members.countermeasures: Checked downstream hooks in rust/bin/tb-bot/src/chat_wiring.rs:1945-1948 and eventsub_hooks.rs:1338-1342; neither retries ledger cleanup. The newer-unban check in rust/crates/tb-chat/src/global_chatter_ban.rs:155-208 suppresses immediate chat rebans but does not repair the ledger used by offline sweeps. channel.unban is a twin because it calls the same store_ban_event cleanup. Another later unban delivery could repair the entry, but none is guaranteed after HTTP 204. No builds, tests, database calls or network probes were performed.

findings.title_de: Abgelaufener Idempotenzowner überschreibt Ersatzowner
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Abgelaufener Idempotenzowner überschreibt Ersatzowner.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: An expired idempotency owner can delete a replacement owner's slot and overwrite its cached result.

original_members.claim: An expired idempotency owner can delete a replacement owner's slot and overwrite its cached result.
original_members.failure_scenario: Request A remains blocked on a database write. At t=901 seconds, another prepare expires its inflight entry and caches 503. At t=1802, that cache entry expires and request B becomes the replacement owner for the same key. A then finishes with an uncached database error while B is still running. A's unconditional removal deletes B's slot, so request C with B's key and body becomes another owner and executes concurrently with B. If A instead succeeds, it can replace the current generation's cache with its old fingerprint and response.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA, cleanup removes expired inflight entries without canceling their OwnerSlot (lines 283-303); cache expiry permits a replacement owner (267, 202-222). OwnerSlot::complete writes the cache and removes inflight solely by scope_key, without checking channel or ownership identity (315-330). The registered link-click handler awaits its database write before completing the slot in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/telemetry_routes.rs:369-388,471-488. Its INSERT has no request-key deduplication in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/telemetry_routes.rs:77-104.
original_members.expected_behavior: The documented synchronized reservation must prevent parallel duplicate execution for the current owner (idempotency.rs:16-21,188-190). Completion of an expired reservation must not remove or overwrite a replacement reservation.
original_members.countermeasures: The mutex makes individual map operations atomic but does not distinguish owner generations. The 30-second timeout only bounds waiters, not owners. The serving path has no enclosing request timeout in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2160-2206; the writer pool does not establish a statement timeout in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:41-57. Telemetry migrations do not add natural-event uniqueness. All inspected idempotent handler variants share this completion implementation.

findings.title_de: Ungültiger zusammengesetzter Originhost gilt als Loopback
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Ungültiger zusammengesetzter Originhost gilt als Loopback.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: An Origin host such as localhost,attacker.example is incorrectly classified as loopback.

original_members.claim: An Origin host such as localhost,attacker.example is incorrectly classified as loopback.
original_members.failure_scenario: A request from peer 127.0.0.1 with a valid internal credential supplies Origin: http://localhost,attacker.example. URL parsing preserves the foreign hostname, but host_without_port splits it at the comma and returns localhost. The request reaches the handler instead of receiving HTTP 403.
original_members.evidence: is_loopback_origin passes parsed.host_str() into is_loopback_host at line 132. That helper calls host_without_port, whose line 50 keeps only the first comma-separated part; lines 95-96 then accept localhost. The pinned url 2.5.8 host parser accepts domain punctuation permitted by IDNA's URL deny-list, which excludes neither commas nor this hostname. The internal router installs this guard in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/lib.rs:423.
original_members.expected_behavior: The actual Origin hostname must be localhost or a loopback IP. security.rs:104-109 and 135-146 define this requirement; lines 448-451 and 479-488 establish that a foreign Origin must be rejected even with a loopback peer. A parsed Origin hostname is not a proxy host list.
original_members.countermeasures: The peer-IP check and internal credential comparison still apply, so this is not a demonstrated authentication bypass and is classified B rather than A. Neither check restores the required foreign-Origin rejection. Comma-list support may remain appropriate for raw proxy-list inputs, but it is unsafe when reused for an already parsed Origin host.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Abgebrochener Owner hinterlässt blockierenden Inflight-Eintrag.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Cancelled idempotency owners leave inflight entries behind and prevent same-key retries.

original_members.claim: Cancelled idempotency owners leave inflight entries behind and prevent same-key retries.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated loopback client submits a valid POST /internal/twitch/v1/live/link-click with an Idempotency-Key. The handler reserves an OwnerSlot and waits for database work, for example while the connection pool is exhausted. The client closes the HTTP/1 connection before any write occurs, cancelling the handler and dropping its OwnerSlot. A subsequent identical request cannot execute: it finds the abandoned inflight entry and receives HTTP 500 because its watch sender is closed. Repeated retries remain blocked for the 900-second inflight TTL. The first retry after expiry converts the abandoned entry into a cached HTTP 503, blocking that key for another 900 seconds despite database recovery.
original_members.evidence: At the fixed review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, OwnerSlot has no Drop implementation. prepare inserts its receiver in shared state at lines 208-222; only complete removes the reservation at line 330. Sender closure returns 500 at lines 239-248 without removing that reservation. Cleanup at lines 283-301 subsequently caches a 503 with a fresh timestamp. The reachable caller in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/telemetry_routes.rs:369-388 holds the slot across process_link_click().await; database work is awaited at lines 471-484. The server is started through axum::serve in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2193-2196. The locked Hyper 1.10.1 implementation detects EOF during a pending response in /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/hyper-1.10.1/src/proto/h1/conn.rs:491-504 and propagates the connection error through /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/hyper-1.10.1/src/proto/h1/dispatch.rs:123-140, dropping the stored handler future. This is static verification; no tests or requests were executed.
original_members.expected_behavior: A terminated, unsuccessful owner must release its reservation so an identical retry can execute. The failure-retry contract is stated in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/idempotency.rs:19-21 and encoded by the test at lines 475-489. The caller also explicitly promises that unsuccessful writes permit same-key retries in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/telemetry_routes.rs:384-387.
original_members.countermeasures: Normal Ok and Err returns call complete and recover correctly, but cancellation bypasses both branches. Watch-channel closure wakes waiters without releasing the map entry. Lazy TTL cleanup does not restore immediate retryability because it caches another failure. Loopback and authentication guards restrict callers but do not prevent their connections from closing. The same shared OwnerSlot lifetime pattern also appears in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:541-555; no cancellation cleanup exists in the primary router layers.

original_members.claim: Dropping an idempotency owner leaves its key unavailable to retries for roughly 30 minutes.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated client disconnects while its owner request is awaiting a database operation. The handler future and OwnerSlot are dropped. Repeated same-key requests encounter the retained inflight entry and receive replayed 500 because its sender is closed. After 900 seconds, cleanup replaces that entry with a cached 503, which prevents execution for another 900 seconds despite there being no owner left.
original_members.evidence: OwnerSlot has no Drop cleanup; only complete removes inflight (86-91,311-350). prepare clones retained receivers (202-206), and a closed receiver yields 500 (239-248). Stale cleanup subsequently installs a fresh 900-second 503 cache entry (264-303). The handler holds its slot directly across the awaited operation in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/telemetry_routes.rs:378-388. Baseline hyper 1.10.1 stores the service future in its connection dispatcher and terminates it on connection errors; locally inspected dependency sources were /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/hyper-1.10.1/src/proto/h1/dispatch.rs:128-140,590-624 and /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/hyper-1.10.1/src/proto/h1/conn.rs:491-518.
original_members.expected_behavior: Cancellation needs a defined recoverable ownership outcome. original_members.countermeasures: Closed-channel handling wakes waiters with 500, but does not release the map entry. Lazy TTL cleanup eventually restores availability after also caching 503. Normal handler error branches call complete, but cancellation bypasses them. The referenced legacy bot/internal_api/app.py is absent at the fixed SHA, so its cancellation contract could not be checked.

original_members.claim: Cancelling an idempotency owner leaves subsequent retries stuck on a dead in-flight entry.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated POST /internal/twitch/v1/live/link-click reserves key K, then waits for a database connection. The client disconnects before the write executes, cancelling the handler future and dropping OwnerSlot. A retry with the same key and body receives replayed HTTP 500 without executing the operation. After in-flight expiry, cleanup instead caches HTTP 503 for another 900 seconds.
original_members.evidence: OwnerSlot owns the watch sender but has no Drop cleanup. prepare inserts the entry at lines 209-215; normal removal occurs only in complete at line 330. Dropping the sender leaves the map's receiver behind, and wait_for_owner returns 500 when changed() reports closure at lines 239-249. The direct handler await is visible in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/telemetry_routes.rs:378-387 and 471-484. The pinned Hyper 1.10.1 connection dispatcher owns the service future and ends the connection on EOF or socket errors, so connection loss can drop this owner.
original_members.expected_behavior: Failed requests must not poison the key; subsequent retries must execute again. This contract is stated at idempotency.rs:19-21 and 475-488. In this scenario the original operation has not executed.
original_members.countermeasures: Normal success and returned-error paths call complete, but cancellation bypasses both. Lazy cleanup does not restore prompt retryability: lines 283-303 turn the orphan into a cached 503. resolved_candidate_group.claim: Internal API database operations can occupy the shared bot pool indefinitely because no execution deadline bounds them.

original_members.claim: Internal API database operations can occupy the shared bot pool indefinitely because no execution deadline bounds them.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, a transaction holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on twitch_streamers. At least pool_max authenticated discord-flag requests, with a valid login, valid body and permissive configured scope, keep their connections open. Each blocks in its initial SELECT after acquiring a pool connection. None has an execution deadline, so all shared connections remain occupied indefinitely and unrelated bot database work fails its acquisition timeout.
original_members.evidence: The complete router stack at lines 388-444 contains authentication, extensions and tracing but no execution timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2160-2207 serves this router without another request deadline; line 494 creates the shared writable pool with tb_db::connect. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:1262-1293 awaits the database operation. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/streamers_crud.rs:800-808 performs the blocking SELECT. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 limits acquisition/connect time but sets statement_timeout only for read-only pools.
original_members.expected_behavior: External database stalls should have a finite execution bound so internal RPCs cannot permanently consume the bot's shared pool. No owner/request execution deadline is specified in the reviewed contract, so choosing that bound or its enforcement layer is a class C design decision.
original_members.countermeasures: Pool size and acquisition timeouts bound connection count and waiting for a connection, not a query already using one. The idempotency waiter's 30-second deadline applies only to duplicate requests. Its 900-second stale cleanup does not cancel the original handler or SQL work. A deployment-level PostgreSQL statement/lock timeout would prevent this scenario, but none is imposed for the writable pool by the reviewed code; actual server configuration was not probed.

findings.title_de: Idempotenzcache behält große ignorierte JSON-Felder
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Idempotenzcache behält große ignorierte JSON-Felder.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The idempotency cache retains entire ignored JSON fields and can exhaust memory before reaching its entry limit.

original_members.claim: The idempotency cache retains entire ignored JSON fields and can exhaust memory before reaching its entry limit.
original_members.failure_scenario: A bot process has 512 MiB of remaining memory. Within the 900-second TTL, an authenticated local caller sends 600 POST /internal/twitch/v1/streamers/example/verify requests with distinct idempotency keys and bodies containing an unknown mode plus a 900 KiB ignored string field. The unknown-mode path returns a cacheable 200 without database or Twitch work. The cache retains over 527 MiB of request strings alone, exceeding available memory even though it has far fewer than 2000 entries.
original_members.evidence: Lines 100-107 serialize the entire JSON object. Lines 181-186 embed that serialization directly in fingerprint; lines 319-325 retain the full fingerprint in each successful cache entry. MAX_ENTRIES and trimming at lines 39 and 336-347 count entries, not bytes. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:735-759 passes the raw body through idempotency, lines 774-785 inspect only mode, and line 893 returns Ok for an unknown mode. Its wrapper at lines 541-544 caches this response. The router and serving wrapper impose no aggregate retained-byte budget.
original_members.expected_behavior: Retained idempotency state should fit an explicit process memory budget, rather than multiplying the per-request body allowance by 2000. The contract specifies entry count and TTL but no byte budget or fingerprint representation, so this is class C rather than an automatic behavioral fix.
original_members.countermeasures: Authentication and the loopback guard exclude unauthenticated remote callers. Axum's per-request JSON body limit bounds an individual body, and the 2000-entry cap plus lazy TTL bound completed-entry count and age during activity. None prevents the demonstrated aggregate-memory failure. No public unauthenticated attack path or production memory allocation was assumed.

findings.title_de: Interner Guard akzeptiert vorhandenen Nicht-ASCII-Origin
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Interner Guard akzeptiert vorhandenen Nicht-ASCII-Origin.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The internal API origin guard accepts present Origin headers containing non-ASCII bytes.

original_members.claim: The internal API origin guard accepts present Origin headers containing non-ASCII bytes.
original_members.failure_scenario: An authenticated HTTP request from 127.0.0.1 to GET /internal/twitch/v1/healthz contains an Origin value consisting of byte 0xFF. HTTP parsing accepts this opaque header byte, but HeaderValue::to_str() fails. The guard converts that failure to None, treats the Origin as absent, and allows the handler to return HTTP 200 instead of rejecting the invalid Origin with HTTP 403.
original_members.evidence: Static review against 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/security.rs:152-158, .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()) discards conversion failures; lines 110-114 accept None. The guard is installed in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/lib.rs:419-423. The authenticated health handler returns success at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/healthz.rs:103-118. The locked dependency sources confirm reachability: /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/httparse-1.10.1/src/lib.rs:90-97 permits 0x80-0xFF in header values, while /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/http-1.4.2/src/header/value.rs:240-245 rejects those bytes during string conversion. No tests or network probes were executed.
original_members.expected_behavior: Reject a present, undecodable Origin with HTTP 403. The explicit guard contract at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/security.rs:141-146 requires rejection of foreign or invalid origins; lines 115-117 and tests at 455-460 likewise reject malformed origin strings.
original_members.countermeasures: The peer-IP check and fail-closed internal-token guard remain effective. This scenario requires an authenticated native client; ordinary browser-generated Origin values cannot contain the supplied byte. Since absent Origin is intentionally allowed, this is a contract bug, not a demonstrated unauthenticated access or CSRF vulnerability. Handler authentication does not revalidate Origin. Nearby token-conversion failures correctly deny access and are not equivalent twins.

original_members.claim: Non-ASCII Origin headers are treated as missing and bypass the loopback-origin rejection.
original_members.failure_scenario: A loopback request with a valid internal credential supplies an Origin header containing an obs-text byte, for example the bytes https://evil.example/ followed by 0x80. This is representable as an HTTP HeaderValue, but to_str() fails. The middleware converts that failure into None and allows the request to reach the handler instead of returning HTTP 403.
original_members.evidence: The Origin extraction at lines 152-155 uses and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()), conflating an invalid present header with an absent header. is_loopback_origin accepts None at lines 111-114. The pinned http 1.4.2 implementation confirms that HeaderValue permits bytes above 0x7f while to_str rejects them: /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/http-1.4.2/src/header/value.rs:240-249 and 552-558.
original_members.expected_behavior: Missing Origin may be allowed, but a present foreign or invalid Origin must produce HTTP 403, as explicitly documented at security.rs:141-146.
original_members.countermeasures: A non-loopback peer is still rejected, and internal_api_auth_guard still requires the correct nonempty credential. Therefore this establishes incorrect Origin validation, not credential-free access. Existing middleware tests cover missing and foreign ASCII Origins but not a failed header-to-string conversion.

findings.title_de: Partneraktivierung folgt nach paralleler Anmeldesperre
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Partneraktivierung folgt nach paralleler Anmeldesperre.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Verify promotion and history reactivation can activate a partner after a concurrent signup block has committed.

original_members.claim: Verify promotion and history reactivation can activate a partner after a concurrent signup block has committed.
original_members.failure_scenario: A verification request checks an existing inactive partner and finds no signup block. Concurrently, the administrator adds a block for that Twitch ID and commits. Verification subsequently acquires its signup lock and changes the partner to active despite the block. The same interleaving is possible between the block check and UPDATE in reactivate_partner.
original_members.evidence: At review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, promotion checks the denylist at lines 480-492 before acquiring the signup advisory lock at 496-500; UPDATE at 532-546 has no denylist predicate or recheck. Reactivation similarly checks at 679-694 and updates unconditionally at 705-722. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:124-127 acquires the same ID lock when adding a block, but its partner pause UPDATE at 257-270 only covers already-active rows. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:805-819 reaches promotion; lines 1207-1208 reach the archive/history path.
original_members.expected_behavior: The signup block must prevent partner activation. This is expressly documented by the promotion guard at lines 473-479 and reactivation guard at 675-678. The normal promotion implementation in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/partner_setup.rs:713-747 checks the denylist after obtaining the signup lock.
original_members.countermeasures: The shared signup lock exists but cannot protect a check performed before acquiring it. Lookup errors fail closed, which does not address this successful stale lookup. Blacklisting and credential deletion in the block transaction limit subsequent bot activity but do not prevent the forbidden active partner row or the verification handler's success followups.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Departnering can overwrite a concurrently saved Discord identity with stale profile data.

original_members.claim: Departnering can overwrite a concurrently saved Discord identity with stale profile data.
original_members.failure_scenario: An active partner initially has Discord ID 999. Departnering loads that identity. Before its identity upsert, an authorized profile update changes the same Twitch user's Discord ID to 555 and commits successfully. Departnering then upserts its snapshot and restores 999, silently losing the successful profile update.
original_members.evidence: load_active_partner joins identity data at lines 110-128; departnering reads it at 206 and passes the snapshot to upsert_streamer_identity at 232-240. The upsert overwrites existing non-null Discord fields and membership at 154-159. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/streamers_crud.rs:848-908 provides the concurrent transactional profile update. The authorized dashboard endpoint reaches it through /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/admin_legacy_streamers.rs:190-225,267-319. The analogous stale-snapshot upsert also exists in departner_streamer at streamers_crud.rs:405-471.
original_members.expected_behavior: Departnering must preserve Discord identity data rather than revert unrelated committed profile changes. Identity preservation is the documented step at lifecycle lines 189-195 and is checked by the existing departner test at 1278 and 1296-1304. The profile endpoint explicitly reports successful saving of the new identity.
original_members.countermeasures: Profile writes lock the supplied Discord ID at streamers_crud.rs:877-882, but lifecycle writes take neither that lock nor a lock spanning their identity read and write. The unique Discord-ID index does not reject this scenario when both IDs are otherwise unused. COALESCE only preserves the current value for null input; the stale ID here is non-null.

findings.title_de: Parallele Prüfung erzeugt doppelte historische Statistik
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Parallele Prüfung erzeugt doppelte historische Statistik.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Concurrent verification backfills insert duplicate historical statistics despite the idempotency contract.

original_members.claim: Concurrent verification backfills insert duplicate historical statistics despite the idempotency contract.
original_members.failure_scenario: A category sample exists for a login and timestamp, but no matching tracked sample exists. Two independent verification requests finish promotion and overlap in backfill. Both INSERT statements evaluate NOT EXISTS against snapshots without that sample, and both insert it, leaving two tracked rows for the same logical observation.
original_members.evidence: The backfill at lines 807-824 uses INSERT SELECT with NOT EXISTS but no transaction-level serialization or conflict handling. Promotion commits at 559 or 592 before /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:831-833 invokes backfill, so the promotion locks are no longer held. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:1451-1459,2615-2617 defines the tracked table and nonunique indexes. Targeted inspection of subsequent tracked-table migrations found no uniqueness constraint for streamer and timestamp.
original_members.expected_behavior: A historical sample should be copied at most once. The helper explicitly promises idempotency at lines 795-798, and its sequential test at 1434-1456 expects the second invocation to copy zero rows.
original_members.countermeasures: NOT EXISTS prevents duplicates only when the other insertion is visible in the statement snapshot. Request idempotency only deduplicates matching supplied keys; handlers run normally without a key. The per-user promotion locks protect promotion, not this subsequent backfill. The assigned sequential test uses one connection and does not test overlapping inserts.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Concurrent archive or block toggles lose one of the requested state changes.

original_members.claim: Concurrent archive or block toggles lose one of the requested state changes.
original_members.failure_scenario: Two independent toggle requests target the same active, unarchived partner. Both read the unarchived state before either writes and both choose Archive. resolved_candidate_group.claim: Verify promotion allocates partner IDs without advancing the sequence, causing subsequent OAuth signup to fail.

original_members.claim: Verify promotion allocates partner IDs without advancing the sequence, causing subsequent OAuth signup to fail.
original_members.failure_scenario: With MAX(id)=10 and the partner sequence last_value=10, verification of a new streamer inserts id=11 explicitly. A subsequent first-time OAuth signup for another streamer receives id=11 from nextval, violates the primary key, and rolls back instead of activating that streamer. This requires no concurrent requests.

The lifecycle test schema at lines 1166-1184 omits the production default and therefore masks this interaction.
original_members.expected_behavior: Both creation paths must use the database's configured partner-ID allocator so that a successful verification cannot make an unrelated subsequent signup fail. The existing sequence default and OAuth insertion establish this contract.
original_members.countermeasures: The primary key prevents overwriting another partner but produces the signup failure. The verification transaction and per-user/per-login advisory locks do not advance the sequence. No sequence repair was found in the examined creation paths or migrations. original_members.expected_behavior: Independent valid partner activations must receive distinct IDs without breaking subsequent ordinary activations. resolved_candidate_group.claim: The require-link backfill silently discards settings for newly added streamers.

original_members.claim: The require-link backfill silently discards settings for newly added streamers.
original_members.failure_scenario: Adding a previously unknown streamer with require_link=true creates only a twitch_streamers row. The backfill then updates twitch_partners, matches no row, and returns Ok. The API reports successful creation, but neither require_discord_link nor the promised next_link_check_at is stored. Later first-time OAuth promotion defaults require_discord_link to 0.
original_members.evidence: Lifecycle lines 842-849 describe persisting these settings for a newly added non-partner, but lines 860-873 update only active partner rows and ignore rows_affected. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:416-447 accepts the setting, calls this helper after AddStreamerResult::Added, and returns success. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/streamers_crud.rs:126-186 creates only streamer and identity rows. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/partner_setup.rs:811-820 defaults the absent partner setting to 0 and the check deadline to None.
original_members.expected_behavior: The helper and caller document retention of the requested link requirement and a check deadline 30 days later. However, discovered-only streamers have no corresponding storage columns. Whether to retain this legacy option, reject it, or change its storage requires a product/schema decision, so this remains C rather than an automatic fix.
original_members.countermeasures: The streamer synchronization trigger only maintains identities; it does not create a partner row or retain these settings. The existing helper test pre-inserts an active partner, so it does not exercise a genuine new-streamer addition. Creating a partner solely to make this UPDATE succeed would change enrollment behavior and is not a safe automatic correction.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Departner retries skip raid-auth cleanup after a partial database failure.

original_members.claim: Departner retries skip raid-auth cleanup after a partial database failure.
original_members.failure_scenario: An active partner has enabled raid auth and a linked Discord account. The partner-status UPDATE commits, but the subsequent raid-auth UPDATE fails, for example because acquiring a pool connection times out. The verify=clear request returns an error before removing the Discord role. After the database recovers, retrying returns success with 'not stored': the partner is already departnered, so raid-auth disabling and role removal are skipped.
original_members.evidence: Lines 260-308 execute the status change and raid-auth disabling separately against the pool, without a transaction. Lines 206-208 return immediately when no active partner exists. The caller at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:855-869 treats this None result as successful and skips role removal. A checked twin has the same partial-commit pattern at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/streamers_crud.rs:495-538.
original_members.expected_behavior: The documented departner operation includes disabling raid auth, and the test at lines 1266-1294 explicitly requires raid_enabled=false. A failed operation must remain retryable or roll back rather than making its remaining steps unreachable.
original_members.countermeasures: Errors propagate and idempotency does not cache failures, but neither rolls back the committed status change. Inactive status and opt-out mitigate subsequent bot activity. The disconnect caller can recover Discord-role cleanup through an identity fallback, but it still does not retry raid-auth disabling; verify=clear lacks that role fallback.

original_members.claim: An interrupted departner operation leaves mandatory cleanup permanently skipped on retry.
original_members.failure_scenario: For an active partner with raid_enabled=true and a Deadlock-pause marker, the status UPDATE commits. A connection failure or process interruption occurs before the following marker-clear or raid-auth UPDATE completes. Retrying the same removal now finds no active partner and skips those operations, leaving the departed account's raid authentication enabled and potentially its pause marker intact.
original_members.evidence: Partner status is written through execute(pool) at lines 260-284, followed by separate autocommit statements at 290-308. Every retry starts with the active-only lookup at 206-208. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:652-680 calls this function and falls back to remove_streamer when it returns None. That fallback at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/streamers_crud.rs:235-285 neither disables raid authentication nor clears the pause marker. The same nontransactional status-then-auth pattern exists in departner_streamer at streamers_crud.rs:495-538.
original_members.expected_behavior: Departnering must disable raid authentication, clear the pause marker, and preserve a recoverable lifecycle transition. These required effects are documented at lifecycle lines 189-195 and 286-289; the existing departner test checks raid_enabled=false at 1288-1294.
original_members.countermeasures: with_idempotency does not cache failures, so it allows retry, but retry cannot repair the already-committed inactive row. GREATEST preserves an existing opt-out and does not address cleanup atomicity. Active-partner guards may limit actual bot activity, but the required authentication cleanup remains undone. Engagement cleanup is explicitly best-effort and is not the basis of this finding.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Archived-partner retries cannot restore raid auth after partial reactivation.

original_members.claim: Archived-partner retries cannot restore raid auth after partial reactivation.
original_members.failure_scenario: An archived partner has raid_enabled=false and needs_reauth=false. Reactivation commits status=active and clears the archive markers. A connection failure then prevents the raid-auth restoration query. Once the database recovers, retrying reactivate_partner returns the active partner without restoration; retrying the unarchive endpoint reports that the partner is not archived. Raid auth remains disabled despite the successful retry response.
original_members.evidence: Lines 705-722 commit the partner change independently before calling restoration at lines 724-731. Lines 639-645 bypass restoration for an already active partner. The endpoint retry follows lines 1002-1008 and returns before any restoration. The caller at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:1207-1218 only maps the original failure to an API error.
original_members.expected_behavior: Lines 632-634 require archived-to-active transitions to restore raid auth when reauthorization is unnecessary. The test at lines 1525-1580 verifies that exact outcome. A recoverable failure must not permanently remove the transition needed to execute that step.
original_members.countermeasures: The needs_reauth guard intentionally preserves disabled auth for expired credentials, but the scenario explicitly has needs_reauth=false. Database errors propagate and are not cached; the previously committed active state nevertheless prevents retrying the restoration.

original_members.claim: History reactivation is not atomic with raid-auth restoration and can leave conflicting lifecycle states.
original_members.failure_scenario: Reactivating a legacy archived partner commits status=active, then restoration of its otherwise healthy disabled raid authentication fails. Retrying returns through the already-active no-op and never restores that authentication. A second failure mode needs no database error: after the active-status UPDATE, a concurrent removal completes and disables raid authentication; the still-running reactivation then restores it, leaving status=departnered with raid_enabled=true.
original_members.evidence: Reactivation updates the partner using execute(pool) at lines 705-722 and separately calls raid-auth restoration at 725-731. The already-active return at 640-644 prevents retry repair. Restoration at 755-789 checks needs_reauth but not current partner status. Concurrent removal reaches departner_active_partner through /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:652-658 and disables authentication at lifecycle lines 295-308. History reactivation is reached through archive_history_path at 1079-1084.
original_members.expected_behavior: An archived-to-active transition with healthy stored authentication must restore raid authentication, while a completed removal must leave it disabled. Both expectations are explicit in lifecycle documentation at 621-634 and tests at 1525-1580 and 1266-1294.
original_members.countermeasures: The needs_reauth check prevents restoration when that flag was already set, but neither locks the complete lifecycle transition nor checks whether a concurrent removal has changed partner status. No transaction spans the partner update and restoration. The active no-op makes a partial failure durable rather than repairable by retry.

findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Partnerprüfung hält Writerpool bei Advisory-Lock.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Verify promotion can exhaust the shared writer pool through unbounded advisory-lock waits.

original_members.claim: Verify promotion can exhaust the shared writer pool through unbounded advisory-lock waits.
original_members.failure_scenario: With PostgreSQL statement_timeout and lock_timeout disabled, a stalled transaction retains the partner_signup advisory lock for a valid Twitch user ID. Send pool_max privileged verification requests for that user with no idempotency key or distinct keys. Each request acquires a writer-pool connection and waits for the same lock without a deadline. The shared pool remains occupied, so unrelated API and background database operations fail their acquisition deadline while the verification requests remain pending.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. The assigned file begins a transaction at line 496 and directly awaits blocking advisory locks at lines 497-505. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 bounds connection acquisition, but sets statement_timeout only for read-only pools. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:494-497,2160-2196 uses the writer pool for the internal router without an outer timeout. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:537-541 awaits both skipped and owner executions directly. The same signup-lock pattern exists in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/partner_setup.rs:713-716.
original_members.expected_behavior: Lock contention should terminate within a finite interval rather than indefinitely occupying shared writer connections. No intended write-lock deadline is specified in the reviewed contract or code, and deployment-level timeout settings remain unknown. Selecting the timeout policy therefore belongs to class C, not an automatic fix.
original_members.countermeasures: Loopback and privileged-auth guards prevent unauthenticated public requests. Idempotency bounds duplicate waiters to 30 seconds but does not bound owners or requests without keys. Pool acquisition deadlines do not cancel statements already running. A deployment-level statement_timeout or lock_timeout could prevent this scenario; actual database and DSN settings were not inspected. Consider a bounded transactional lock wait after establishing the intended policy.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Verify promotion can activate a streamer after a concurrent signup-denylist addition has committed.

original_members.claim: Verify promotion can activate a streamer after a concurrent signup-denylist addition has committed.
original_members.failure_scenario: An inactive partner and its monitored-streamer source exist, with no committed denylist entry. A concurrent signup-block transaction acquires the streamer's advisory lock and inserts the block. Internal verification reads the denylist before that transaction commits, sees no entry, and subsequently waits for the same lock. After blocking commits, verification acquires the lock but never rechecks the denylist. Its UPDATE activates the existing partner and clears technical_pause_reason, leaving an active partner despite the committed block. The verification handler can also grant the Discord streamer role.
original_members.evidence: Reviewed at 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/streamer_lifecycle.rs:480-492 checks using the pool before acquiring the advisory lock at 496-500; 530-560 updates and commits an existing partner without another check. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-analytics/src/partner_signup_block.rs:122-127 takes the same lock, 173-192 inserts the denylist entry, and 257-270 pauses only already-active partners. Internal verification reaches this code at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/handlers/streamers.rs:798-819 and grants the role at 845-849. Same-root twin: streamer_lifecycle.rs:679-722 performs history reactivation after an unlocked denylist check.
original_members.expected_behavior: A committed signup block must prevent activation, including verification and history reactivation. The primary file documents this requirement at 443-444 and 473-479. The existing OAuth promotion implementation at /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-raid/src/partner_setup.rs:713-748 correctly acquires the same advisory lock before checking the denylist.
original_members.countermeasures: Internal routes require loopback access, a nonempty matching internal credential, and privileged AuthLevel, so this is not an unauthenticated endpoint bypass. Lookup errors fail closed. The existing advisory lock does not protect a decision read before lock acquisition. The denylist migration and identity-sync triggers do not reject partner activation based on denylist membership. Block addition pauses only active rows and cannot protect the inactive-row scenario. Static review only; no tests, requests, or database operations were executed.

original_members.claim: Database fingerprints ignore SQLx host, port and dbname query overrides.
original_members.failure_scenario: The bot uses postgres://localhost:5432/deadlock?dbname=other while the dashboard uses postgres://localhost:5432/deadlock, with both databases present and otherwise healthy services. The startup comparison therefore misses the different databases.

The pinned SQLx 0.9.0 implementation in /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-postgres-0.9.0/src/options/parse.rs:50-84 applies host, hostaddr, port and dbname query overrides after authority/path parsing. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:460-481 contains the same omission, and lines 61-72 compare the resulting fingerprints.
original_members.expected_behavior: The health response's database identity and the different-database startup check must account for connection-selection parameters actually used by SQLx. A dbname override selecting another database must not leave its identity unchanged.
original_members.countermeasures: Runtime DSN loading in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-config/src/global.rs:361-395 only trims and requires a nonempty value; it does not prohibit these supported query parameters. original_members.failure_scenario: The bot's TWITCH_ANALYTICS_DSN is ' postgres://u:p@localhost:5432/deadlock' and the dashboard's value is the same URL without the leading space. Both runtime configurations trim the DSN and connect to the same database. The bot health handler rereads the untrimmed value, fails the starts_with check and hashes empty host, port and database fields. The dashboard hashes localhost|5432|deadlock instead, records a startup mismatch and subsequently returns 503 from readiness.
original_members.evidence: The handler reads the raw environment string at line 109. analytics_identity_fields tests its prefix before trimming at line 66; its keyword fallback at lines 75-85 finds no fields in the whitespace-prefixed URL. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-config/src/global.rs:365-381 trims this same input before constructing the pool configuration. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/health_probe.rs:61-72 caches unequal fingerprints, and lines 180-188 turn that condition into readiness failure. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:441,484 computes and installs that cache.
original_members.expected_behavior: Whitespace normalization accepted by runtime configuration must also apply before fingerprint format detection. The same normalized database URL must produce the same fingerprint in both services.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: The internal legacy proxy follows redirects instead of forwarding their responses.

original_members.claim: The internal legacy proxy follows redirects instead of forwarding their responses.
original_members.failure_scenario: With a configured legacy upstream, an authenticated loopback request reaches an unmatched internal API path. The upstream responds with 302 and a Location whose destination returns 200. Reqwest follows that redirect automatically, so the caller receives the destination's 200 response and body rather than the upstream's 302 and Location. A redirect chain exceeding the default limit instead becomes the proxy's 502 response.
original_members.evidence: LegacyProxy::new at lines 52-58 configures only a timeout, leaving Reqwest's default redirect policy enabled. Lines 112-131 forward the response returned after redirect processing. /home/nathanael/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/reqwest-0.12.28/src/redirect.rs:19-26,160-164 documents and implements automatic following of up to ten redirects. The matching proxy in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/proxy.rs:97-104 explicitly disables redirects to preserve transparent forwarding; its test at lines 571-602 requires the original 302 and Location.
original_members.expected_behavior: A transparent fallback proxy must return the upstream redirect status and Location to the caller rather than replacing them with a subsequent request's response.
original_members.countermeasures: Unmatched requests reach this handler through /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-internal-api/src/lib.rs:387,413. Loopback and token guards restrict callers but cannot preserve the upstream response. The proxy is disabled when unconfigured, but /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/bin/tb-bot/src/main.rs:2055-2058 enables it from valid configuration. URL validation accepts a loopback HTTP upstream and does not configure redirect behavior. The dashboard twin already contains the relevant safeguard.

findings.title_de: Legacy-Fallback puffert Upstream ohne Größenbegrenzung
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Legacy-Fallback puffert Upstream ohne Größenbegrenzung.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Der aktivierte Legacy-Fallback puffert Upstream-Antworten ohne Größenbegrenzung vollständig im Arbeitsspeicher.

original_members.claim: Der aktivierte Legacy-Fallback puffert Upstream-Antworten ohne Größenbegrenzung vollständig im Arbeitsspeicher.
original_members.failure_scenario: Bei konfiguriertem legacy_proxy_base_url erreicht ein gültiger interner Request auf einen unbekannten Pfad den Proxy. Ein fehlerhafter Upstream liefert innerhalb von 30 Sekunden einen Antwortstrom, der größer als der verfügbare Prozessspeicher ist. resp.bytes() sammelt diesen vollständig, bevor die Antwort ausgeliefert wird; dadurch kann der gesamte Bot wegen Speichermangels beendet werden.
original_members.evidence: Codebasis 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, zugewiesene Dateien ohne Drift. legacy_proxy.rs:90 begrenzt nur den Request-Body; :112-132 liest die komplette Upstream-Antwort ohne Byte-Limit. Erreichbarkeit: lib.rs:387,413 registriert den Fallback; tb-bot/src/main.rs:2055-2058,2160-2174 verdrahtet die konfigurierbare Instanz. operations.rs:175-176 erlaubt die Option. Kein weiteres solches Antwortpuffermuster in den zugewiesenen Dateien.
original_members.expected_behavior: Der dokumentierte 1:1-Proxyvertrag sollte auch bei großen Antworten den übrigen Bot nicht durch unbegrenztes Puffern beenden. Ein verbindliches Antwortgrößenlimit ist nicht dokumentiert; Streaming oder eine neue Grenze bleiben deshalb eine C-Empfehlung.
original_members.countermeasures: Der Proxy ist standardmäßig deaktiviert (operations.rs:130); ohne Instanz endet der Pfad sofort mit 404. Loopback- und Zugangsschutz gelten auch für den Fallback (lib.rs:419-423; security.rs:147-159,188-200). Der 30-Sekunden-Upstream-Timeout begrenzt die Dauer, nicht die empfangene Bytezahl. Keine bestätigte öffentlich ausnutzbare Sicherheitslücke; empfohlen ist speicherbegrenztes Weiterreichen unter Beibehaltung des Antwortvertrags.

findings.title_de: Legacy-Fallback wartet unbefristet auf Requestbody
findings.problem_de: Erhaltener Claim: Legacy-Fallback wartet unbefristet auf Requestbody.
findings.prerequisites_de: Voraussetzungen und Gegenbelege stehen im erhaltenen Original; keine neue Bewertung durch diese Dokumentationsrolle.

resolved_candidate_group.claim: Der aktivierte Legacy-Fallback hat keine Zeitgrenze für das Lesen eingehender Request-Bodies.

original_members.claim: Der aktivierte Legacy-Fallback hat keine Zeitgrenze für das Lesen eingehender Request-Bodies.
original_members.failure_scenario: Ein zugelassener Loopback-Client sendet einen Request auf einen unbekannten Pfad mit Content-Length: 1048576, liefert nur einen Teil des Bodys und hält die Verbindung offen. Der Handler wartet ohne Ablaufzeit in to_bytes(); der konfigurierte 30-Sekunden-Timeout beginnt noch nicht. Mehrere solche festhängenden Aufrufe behalten Verbindungen, Handlerzustand und bereits empfangene Daten dauerhaft.
original_members.evidence: legacy_proxy.rs:90-99 wartet auf den vollständigen Body; erst danach folgen Client-Request-Aufbau und upstream.send() in :101-112. Der einzige Timeout steht am reqwest-Upstream-Client in :54-55. Der Router besitzt keinen Request-Timeout-Layer (lib.rs:387-444), und tb-bot/src/main.rs:2193-2206 startet axum::serve ohne zusätzliche Body-Lesezeitgrenze. Im zugewiesenen Abschnitt existiert kein zweiter vergleichbarer manueller Request-Body-Lesepfad.
original_members.expected_behavior: Ein steckengebliebener interner Caller sollte einen Proxy-Aufruf nicht unbegrenzt offenhalten. Der bestehende Vertrag definiert allerdings nur die Upstream-Zeitgrenze, keine Eingangsfrist; deren Einführung ist daher C und keine belegte B-Fixfreigabe.
original_members.countermeasures: MAX_BODY_BYTES begrenzt die Datenmenge je Request auf 2 MiB, aber nicht die Wartezeit. Loopback- und Zugangsschutz sowie die standardmäßig deaktivierte Proxyoption reduzieren die Erreichbarkeit deutlich. Ein Client-Abbruch beendet den Fehlerzustand; das Szenario setzt eine offenbleibende Verbindung voraus. Empfehlung: eine ausdrücklich vereinbarte Body-Lesezeitgrenze oder eine entsprechende äußere Request-Grenze.

original_member.claim: A concurrent session refresh can undo successful admin fingerprint completion.
original_member.failure_scenario: A pending admin session remains unfinished for more than 1800 seconds, for example after a suspended login tab. A concurrent forward-auth request reads its fp_pending=true payload and prepares a sliding refresh. POST /twitch/auth/fingerprint then successfully writes fp_pending=false and js_fp and redirects to the dashboard. The earlier refresh persists its stale whole payload afterward, restoring fp_pending=true and removing js_fp. Forward-auth rejects the supposedly completed session and the login handler starts another OAuth login.
original_member.evidence: /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/session.rs:914-958 completes fingerprint collection by reading and replacing the encrypted payload. The same source's lines 1570-1606 independently read the payload for sliding refresh, and lines 2061-2118 persist the entire stale payload when drift exceeds 1800 seconds. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/auth/level.rs:421-442 reaches that refresh during central-session authentication. /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/forward_auth.rs:69-75 checks the resulting fingerprint; fp_pending causes rejection. The anchored file's lines 379-425 restart OAuth for such an unusable session.
original_member.expected_behavior: Successful fingerprint submission must leave fp_pending=false and the submitted js_fp intact. The anchored file's fingerprint_submit_schliesst_pending_session_ab test, lines 1906-1950, explicitly verifies both fields and successful fingerprint verification.
original_member.countermeasures: The 1800-second persistence threshold prevents this interleaving for fresh sessions, but pending sessions have a 14-day lifetime and no shorter pending deadline. Cache expiry permits a fresh concurrent read. Fingerprint completion removes the admin cache entry after writing, but neither that removal nor the cache mutex protects the encrypted row from a later stale refresh. The database upsert has no payload-version check or read-modify-write transaction. Evidence is static; no tests or mutations were performed.

original_member.claim: The shared Twitch callback creates affiliate sessions without binding OAuth state to the initiating browser.
original_member.failure_scenario: An attacker starts affiliate OAuth in their own browser, authorizes their own Twitch account and captures the unused callback URL containing code and state. They induce a victim to navigate to that URL. The callback installs an affiliate session for the attacker's account in the victim's browser, even if the victim never initiated OAuth. If the victim subsequently submits profile details, those details are saved to the attacker's account and can be retrieved by the attacker.
original_member.evidence: At lines 223-237, an unmatched dashboard state is delegated to try_shared_affiliate_callback without passing request headers, before the browser-context check at lines 301-322. In /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/affiliate.rs:123-165, login stores only redirect_uri and sets no browser-binding cookie; lines 280-306 consume that state and call complete_affiliate_login. Lines 225-278 exchange the code and set the affiliate cookie without browser validation. The primary-file test at lines 1661-1711 explicitly demonstrates successful affiliate-session issuance with an empty HeaderMap. Affiliate profile writes and reads at lines 498-644 use the resulting session's twitch_login. The dedicated affiliate callback at lines 168-223 has the same missing binding.
original_member.expected_behavior: Only the browser that initiated OAuth should receive the resulting session. The dashboard flow explicitly states this requirement at primary-file lines 127-130 and enforces it at lines 301-322; the affiliate dispatch bypasses that protection.
original_member.countermeasures: State is random, encrypted, expiring and single-use, and Twitch verifies the code and redirect URI. These measures do not bind an attacker-generated valid authorization to its initiating browser. HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax do not prevent a top-level callback from setting a new cookie. Public callback registration in lib.rs:1336-1349 adds rate limiting, not a browser-binding guard. No probes or tests were executed.

Datenbank-Constraints und Unveränderlichkeit sichern dieselben Invarianten zusätzlich ab (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/store.rs:75-130; rust/migrations/20260927110000_partner_effort_engine.sql:20-26,130-137).

Evidenz wird konservativ bewertet: überlappende Zeitintervalle werden vereinigt, unterbrochene gemeinsame Sessions starten neu, Steam-Ergebnisse benötigen passende Identität und einen endgültigen Matchausgang (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/evidence.rs:10,28; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources/live.rs:146; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/lib.rs:75).

Konfiguration ist injiziert und validiert, statt im Crate aus ENV gelesen zu werden. Quest-Zuordnung speichert Belohnung, Bonus und Regelhash; spätere Auszahlung benutzt die gespeicherten Werte (rust/crates/tb-config/src/challenges.rs:108; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/lib.rs:126; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/quests.rs:185,373,395).

Fehlende Kategoriedaten sind ein expliziter Zustand und machen unabhängige Challenges nicht pauschal unbrauchbar. Strenge Bereitschaft und Anzeige-Bereitschaft haben bewusst unterschiedliche Verträge, keine unnötige Doppelimplementierung (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/lib.rs:215-247; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/types.rs:71; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/quests.rs:406; rust/crates/tb-effort/tests/postgres.rs:1445).

Vorhandene Begrenzungen und Schichtgrenzen sind nachvollziehbar: Quellen-Timeout, vier parallele Helix-Abfragen, begrenzte zentrale Poolgröße, Read-only-Verbindungsoptionen und HTTP-Zeitgrenze. Das Dashboard nutzt die Bereitschaftsprüfung und hat einen separaten Identitäts-Scope (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources.rs:64; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources/live.rs:284; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/lib.rs:144; rust/crates/tb-dashboard-api/src/handlers/challenges.rs:32,119,135).
weaknesses: Dateitrennung ist vorhanden, fachliche Logik und SQL bleiben aber eng über denselben Engine-Typ gekoppelt. live.rs umfasst 694 Zeilen mit Helix-Kontinuität, Identitätsverknüpfung und Matchauswertung; level() verbindet auf 121 Zeilen Datenzugriff, Verfügbarkeit und Zieltext. Das erschwert isolierte Regeltests, ist aber kein unstrukturierter Gesamtmonolith (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/lib.rs:43; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources/live.rs:267,394,476; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/projection.rs:201-321).

Unterschiedliche Steam-/Helix-Evidenzverträge sollten dagegen getrennt bleiben (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/quests.rs:157; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/projection.rs:262; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/store.rs:8; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources/live.rs:395,468).

Mehrfachausfälle sind dadurch schlechter nachvollziehbar (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/lib.rs:29,132; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources/live.rs:304; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources.rs:86; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/store.rs:140).

Streak-Auswertung fragt die Kalenderabdeckung wochenweise je Partner ab; party_available lädt jeweils sämtliche Verknüpfungen. Das sind belegte Skalierungsgrenzen, keine gemessene Produktionsstörung (rust/crates/tb-effort/src/evidence.rs:127-167; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/projection.rs:64-77; rust/crates/tb-effort/src/sources/live.rs:394,456).

result.rationale: The 4/5 rating remains justified. Independent source reading confirms a shared transport boundary, explicit usage lifecycle, bounded requests and substantial existing test facilities. The maintenance concerns are credible, but the no_ledger recommendation needs a semantic correction and the orchestration criticism needs qualification. All recommendations remain C; this review confirms no security vulnerability.
corrections: no_ledger is not an effective local bookkeeping switch either. complete_chain assigns a purpose for Ledger::Off, and call_endpoint tracks any loopback request when a ledger pool exists. Document its compatibility/no-op semantics rather than merely describing it as a local test helper.

call_endpoint coordinates several sensitive phases, but transport, response parsing and ledger persistence are already separate helpers. Its 186 lines support an optional orchestration cleanup, not a claim that architectural separation is absent.

The current integration test already prints a missing-configuration skip notice. Improve discoverability and reporting of skipped execution, rather than implying that skip diagnostics or current ledger tests are missing.
accepted_recommendations: C1: Make the existing engagement ledger lifecycle scenarios discoverable from tb-llm, retain their isolated-database safeguards and expose skipped execution clearly. Add focused tests for the recovery binary's journal-origin predicate without duplicating the existing DB recovery tests.

C2: Reuse read_selection(path, uid), run_at and recover_with_pool for targeted test isolation. A shared environment-test guard is justified for keys and selection within the same test process; retain fixed production entry points and mandatory usage recording.

C3: Treat further extraction from call_endpoint as an optional, lower-priority refactoring when changing lifecycle behavior. Preserve the deadline, start-before-HTTP ordering, journal emission and detached completion behavior, using the existing integration scenarios.

strengths: Clear separation between transport contract, network implementation, and intentional headless implementation. Payload types distinguish rich messages, alerts, and DMs; the crate does not incorporate database orchestration (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/backend.rs:7-59,108-135; src/noop.rs:14; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/wiring.rs:599-603,668-684).

One shared HTTP client and POST helper centralize authentication, operation-specific idempotency, and a two-attempt retry limit. Redirects and inherited proxies are disabled, with explicit origin/path validation (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:235-279,284-342).

The large relay file is not a single oversized production function: 900 of its 1,686 lines belong to the test module, and its longest production method spans 61 lines (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:471-531,787-1686).

No orphan source module was found inside the package: lib.rs declares all implementation modules and the relay test module includes personal_invite_tests.rs. Alert/DM separation and the stricter personal-invite origin contract are intentional, not redundant implementations (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/lib.rs:3-5; src/relay.rs:491-498,763-765,789,1529-1562).

Configuration is injected into the transport rather than read from the environment inside it. Consumer settings already have typed validation, and existing domain ports isolate member fetching and directory operations outside the transport (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:235-245; rust/crates/tb-config/src/discord.rs:113-186; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/chat_wiring.rs:2483-2502; oauth_followups.rs:130-143).
weaknesses: HTTP-status/body handling is repeated across methods, while success semantics differ: role mutations return status-only success, message sends expose an unchecked ok field, create operations validate envelopes, and user resolution maps failed envelopes to absence. This makes contract changes harder to apply consistently; it is not a confirmed runtime defect (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:355-386,514-530,619-627,708-773).

The error model mixes local validation failures and malformed responses into BrokerError with synthetic HTTP statuses; reqwest JSON decoding travels through Http. A consumer additionally recognizes a broker condition by substring matching the body, creating text-level coupling (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/backend.rs:97-103; src/relay.rs:250-254,360,449-465; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/wiring.rs:508-514).

Origin validation happens when an operation is called, not when BrokerRelay is constructed. Timing policy is fixed at 10 seconds/two attempts/two-second waits, with separate 15-second overrides for two GET operations. These are bounded defaults, but they limit early configuration feedback and deterministic timing tests (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:31-33,235-255,643,666).

relay.rs holds DTOs, validation, generic HTTP mechanics, several operation families, and most tests in one module. Navigation could improve, although the measured production function sizes do not justify calling it a giant-function design (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:45-231,233-785,787-1686).

Security and invitation contracts have explicit negative cases for origins, redirects, failed/malformed voice envelopes, invalid platform IDs, non-loopback personal invitations, and invalid invitation URLs (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:804-835,908-928,1259-1288; src/personal_invite_tests.rs:35-72).

A connection-failure recovery test exists, so retry coverage is not absent. It uses a real socket and wall-clock delay rather than an injected or paused timing policy (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:1596-1636).

Configuration default/override/token-precedence tests and an announcement adapter test for edit-404-to-Gone exist outside the crate. Member-index tests construct GuildMember values directly, rather than testing member-response deserialization (rust/crates/tb-config/src/lib.rs:247-267,298-319; rust/bin/tb-bot/src/wiring.rs:909-929; streamer_link.rs:481-535).

No explicit timeout-retry or retry-exhaustion test was found in the complete crate suite. The existing connection-recovery and HTTP-error tests cover different branches (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:311-341,1085-1099,1596-1667).

No direct negative-envelope tests were found for message sends or role mutations. Such tests do exist for voice and personal invitations, so this is a localized gap rather than a general lack of failure testing (rust/crates/tb-transport-discord/src/relay.rs:381-386,708-773,1259-1288; src/personal_invite_tests.rs:35-55).

recommendations.proposal: C: Consolidate repeated HTTP failure decoding and introduce structured distinctions between endpoint validation, broker rejection, and malformed responses. Preserve operation-specific payloads, authentication, and success contracts.
